The plant produces over 100 cannabinoids, including THC and CBD. Hemp was once so important that the US Constitution was drafted on hemp paper, and the 1937 Marihuana Tax Act was driven partly by competing industrial interests.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore cannabis, one of humanity's oldest cultivated plants, used for fiber, food, and medicine for millennia. Learn about cannabinoids like CBD and THC, how they interact with the body's own signaling system, and why laws around it differ so widely.

name: The Yew: The Cancer Drug
teaser: A slow-growing tree that hides a chemotherapy compound.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how paclitaxel, a key chemotherapy drug, was first found in the bark of the Pacific yew tree. Learn how one tree yields only a tiny amount, how scientists learned to make it in labs, and why this slow tree became medical treasure.

name: Cinchona: The Malaria Bark
teaser: The South American tree whose bark wrote medical history.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow cinchona from Andean forests to global medicine: its bark contains quinine, the first effective malaria treatment. Learn how Jesuit missionaries spread it, how the Dutch broke the seed monopoly, and how it saved countless lives.

name: Peppermint: The Digestive Herb
teaser: A cooling hybrid herb used for stomachs for centuries.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet peppermint, a natural hybrid of water mint and spearmint whose oil is famous for soothing digestion. Learn how menthol creates the cooling sensation, how the oil is used in candies and medicines, and why it thrives in damp ground.

name: Neem: The Village Pharmacy
teaser: An Indian tree with a use for almost every ailment.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet neem, an Indian tree so useful its parts treat skin, teeth, pests, and fevers. Learn how neem oil repels insects, how twigs are chewed as toothbrushes, and why this 'village pharmacy' is now grown across tropical regions.

name: Plant Defenses: Chemical Warfare
teaser: How plants fight back with toxins and tricks.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore the chemical arsenal plants use against hungry animals: bitter alkaloids, burning capsaicin, sticky resins, and cyanide that releases only when chewed. Learn why caffeine and nicotine are actually insect poisons, and how herbivores evolved to cope.

name: Monstera: The Swiss Cheese Plant
teaser: A jungle climber with holes that became a house favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the monstera, a tropical climber whose leaves develop dramatic holes and splits. Learn why scientists think the holes let wind pass and light reach lower leaves, how it climbs with aerial roots, and why it thrives indoors with little fuss.

name: Snake Plant: Nearly Indestructible
teaser: A houseplant that forgives neglect.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the snake plant
exploreAction.instruction: Discover why the snake plant survives dark corners and forgotten watering: it stores water in thick leaves and uses CAM photosynthesis. Learn how its upright sword leaves purify air, and why beginners are told to start with this one.

name: Pothos: The Trailing Vine
teaser: A forgiving vine that grows almost anywhere.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet pothos, a hardy trailing vine that tolerates low light, missed waterings, and rooting in water. Learn how it climbs trees in the wild with aerial roots, why it is one of the most popular houseplants on Earth, and how to keep it happy.

name: Fiddle-Leaf Fig: The Diva
teaser: A trendy houseplant famous for dramatic tantrums.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the fiddle-leaf fig
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the fiddle-leaf fig, the houseplant known for both beauty and fussiness. Learn why its giant violin-shaped leaves drop when moved or overwatered, how its native African rainforest explains its needs, and why owners both love and dread it.

name: Succulents: Water Storage Experts
teaser: Plants engineered for drought, loved indoors.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore succulents, plants that store water in leaves, stems, or roots to survive drought. Learn how their thick waxy skins limit water loss, how overwatering — not drought — kills most indoor ones, and how they make perfect low-care companions.

name: Cactus: The Prickly Survivor
teaser: Desert plants that turned leaves into spines.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the cactus family, native to the Americas, which turned leaves into spines and stems into water tanks. Learn how pleats let them swell with rain, how shallow roots drink fast, and how saguaro cacti live for two centuries.

name: The Saguaro: Giant of the Desert
teaser: A cactus that can live 200 years and weigh tons.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the saguaro, the giant cactus of the Sonoran Desert, which can live over two centuries and weigh several tons. Learn how slowly it grows, how its flowers open at night for bats, and why it is the ecosystem's apartment building for birds.

name: Agave: The Century Plant
teaser: A desert rosette famous for tequila and spikes.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover agave, a desert plant whose spiky rosette stores sugars for years, then sends up a huge flower stalk once and dies. Learn how blue agave becomes tequila, how fibers become rope, and why it is not actually a cactus.

name: Joshua Tree: Desert Sentinel
teaser: A strange tree that defines the Mojave.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Joshua tree
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the Joshua tree, a giant yucca of the Mojave Desert whose twisted arms give it its name. Learn how only a specific moth pollinates it, how it survives freezing nights and blazing days, and why climate change threatens its habitat.

name: Welwitschia: The Two-Leaf Marvel
teaser: A desert plant with just two leaves that never stop growing.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet welwitschia, a Namib desert plant with only two leaves that grow continuously for a thousand years, splitting into ribbons. Learn how it drinks coastal fog through its leaves and why botanists call it a living fossil.

name: Desert Rose: The Bottle Plant
teaser: A succulent with a swollen trunk and striking blooms.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the desert rose
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the desert rose, a succulent whose swollen trunk stores water and whose pink flowers appear even in harsh heat. Learn how its milky sap is toxic, how bonsai lovers shape it, and why it thrives with dry winters.

name: Prickly Pear: The Tuna Cactus
teaser: A cactus with edible pads and fruit.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the prickly pear, a cactus whose pads are eaten as nopales and whose red fruit is called tuna. Learn how its tiny barbed hairs, not its spines, are the real hazard, and how cochineal insects that feed on it made a famous red dye.

name: Compost: Garden Gold
teaser: Turning kitchen scraps into living soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how composting turns food scraps and leaves into rich soil through the work of bacteria, fungi, and worms. Understand the balance of greens and browns, why heat builds inside the pile, and how finished compost feeds plants naturally.

name: Pruning: The Right Cut
teaser: How cutting plants makes them stronger.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why gardeners cut branches: pruning removes dead wood, shapes growth, and pushes energy into fruit and flowers. Learn where to cut above a bud, why timing matters by season, and how the plant's own hormones respond to the snip.

name: Grafting: Joining Plants
teaser: Why orchards grow on borrowed roots.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how grafting fuses a shoot of one plant onto the roots of another, the technique behind most fruit trees. Understand why grafted apples stay true to variety while seedlings don't, and how grafting resists diseases and controls tree size.

name: Water Lilies: Floating Blooms
teaser: Flowers that float on ponds and rivers.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the water lily, whose leaves float while its flowers rise above the water. Learn how air-filled tissue keeps leaves afloat, how its stems grow from muddy bottoms, and how the giant Amazon lily can hold the weight of a child.

name: Lotus vs Water Lily: The Confusion
teaser: Two floating flowers, two different families.

exploreAction.targetName: how to tell lotus from water lily
exploreAction.instruction: Untangle the confusion between lotus and water lily. Learn that lotus leaves rise above the water and its seed heads are flat-topped, while water lily leaves float flat on the surface. Discover how each one became a symbol in different cultures.

name: Duckweed: The Tiny Floater
teaser: The world's smallest flowering plant.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet duckweed, a flowering plant the size of a pinhead that can double its mass in a day and carpet ponds. Learn why it is studied as a superfood and biofuel, how ducks graze on it, and how it cleans water by absorbing nutrients.

name: Kelp: The Giant Seaweed
teaser: Ocean forests of fast-growing algae.

exploreAction.instruction: Dive into kelp forests, where giant brown algae grow up to half a meter a day. Learn that kelp is not a plant but an alga, how its air bladders hold it toward the sun, and why these underwater forests shelter countless sea creatures.

name: Seagrass: Underwater Meadows
teaser: The only flowering plants that grow in the sea.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet seagrass, the only flowering plants that live fully submerged in saltwater. Learn how they pollinate underwater, capture carbon, and shelter baby fish, and why one ancient seagrass meadow in the Mediterranean may be thousands of years old.

name: Sphagnum: The Bog Builder
teaser: A moss that makes peat and shapes landscapes.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover sphagnum moss, the plant that builds peat bogs by growing at the top while its lower layers rot slowly in acidic water. Learn how it holds many times its weight in water, preserves bodies for centuries, and stores vast amounts of carbon.

name: Tropical Orchids: Air Gardeners
teaser: Rainforest orchids that grow on branches, not soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet tropical orchids that live on tree branches, gathering water from mist with fleshy roots. Learn how their huge flowers mimic insects, how some smell of rotting meat to attract flies, and why collectors risked their lives for rare species.

name: The Banana 'Tree': A Giant Herb
teaser: The world's largest herb, not a tree.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the banana plant
exploreAction.instruction: Learn that the banana plant is not a tree but the world's largest herb — its 'trunk' is tightly wrapped leaves. Understand how each plant fruits once then dies, how new shoots replace it, and why every commercial banana is a clone.

name: The Coconut Palm: The Versatile Tree
teaser: A palm that provides food, drink, fiber, and shelter.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the coconut palm
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the coconut palm, called the tree of life for its endless uses: water, milk, oil, fiber, thatch, and timber. Learn how coconuts float across oceans to colonize islands, and how the palm thrives in sandy coastal soil.

name: Taro: The Ancient Tuber
teaser: A tropical root that fed the Pacific for millennia.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow taro, a tropical root crop domesticated thousands of years ago and carried across the Pacific by voyagers. Learn how its leaves and corms are cooked to remove irritants, and how it remains a staple from Hawaii to West Africa.

name: Passionflower: The Intricate Vine
teaser: A tropical flower with a name from missionaries.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the passionflower, a tropical vine whose intricate bloom was read by missionaries as a symbol of the Passion. Learn how its fruit becomes passionfruit, how its tendrils climb, and why bees and hummingbirds love it.

name: Frangipani: The Temple Flower
teaser: A fragrant tropical bloom found at temples and beaches.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover frangipani, the plumeria whose fragrant flowers are strung into leis and found around temples. Learn why the tree drops its leaves in dry seasons, how easily cuttings root, and how the flowers bloom even without leaves.

name: Wildflowers: Meadow Blooms
teaser: The wild blooms that feed bees and brighten fields.

exploreAction.instruction: Celebrate wildflowers, the native blooms that carpet meadows and roadsides without any gardener. Learn how their seeds wait in soil for the right moment, why they are vital food for bees and butterflies, and how meadows hold hundreds of species.

name: Stinging Nettle: The Defended Weed
teaser: A painful weed that is also food and medicine.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the stinging nettle, whose hollow hairs inject irritating chemicals at a touch — yet whose leaves are cooked into soup and tea. Learn why cooking disarms the sting, how it feeds butterfly caterpillars, and why it grows where soil is rich.

name: Clover: Nature's Fertilizer
teaser: A humble weed that feeds the soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how clover, a low meadow plant, hosts bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, fertilizing everything around it. Learn why farmers sow it between crops and why bees adore its tiny flowers.

name: Plants Invade the Land
teaser: How green algae conquered the continents.

exploreAction.instruction: Travel back 470 million years to when plants left the water. Learn how waxy coats, pores, and roots evolved to survive dry air, how plants changed Earth's climate by absorbing carbon, and how forests transformed the planet.

name: The First Flowers
teaser: How flowering plants appeared and took over the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the first flowering plants, which appeared around 140 million years ago and now dominate the land. Learn how flowers and their pollinators co-evolved into an explosion of forms, and why this revolution shaped insects, birds, and our food.

name: Gymnosperms: Naked Seeds
teaser: Conifers and cycads that ruled before flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore gymnosperms — conifers, cycads, and ginkgo — whose seeds sit naked on cones rather than inside fruit. Learn how they dominated the age of dinosaurs, survive cold and drought, and include the tallest and oldest trees alive.

name: Bryophytes: The Mosses
teaser: Simple plants that thrive where others cannot.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the bryophytes — mosses, liverworts, and hornworts — plants without true roots or tubes. Learn how they absorb water through their surfaces, why they dominate damp cold places, and how they can survive drying to dust and revive.

name: Ferns: The Fronded Survivors
teaser: Ancient plants that reproduce by spores, not seeds.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet ferns, ancient plants that reproduce by dust-like spores instead of seeds. Learn how their coiled fiddleheads unfurl, why they love shade and damp, and how they once grew into the coal forests that fuel our power plants.

name: Ginkgo: The Living Fossil
teaser: A tree unchanged for 200 million years.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the ginkgo, a tree that has changed little in 200 million years and survived the dinosaurs. Learn how it tolerates city pollution, why its leaves turn gold overnight, and how it survived only because monks kept planting it.

name: The Titan Arum: Corpse Flower
teaser: The world's largest flower that smells of rotting meat.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the titan arum
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the titan arum, which produces the world's largest unbranched flower spike and fills the air with the smell of rotting flesh. Learn why the smell attracts carrion flies, how the plant stores years of energy for one bloom, and where it grows wild.

name: Rafflesia: The Giant Parasite
teaser: The world's largest single flower lives as a parasite.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover rafflesia, a flower over a meter wide that has no leaves, stems, or roots — it lives entirely inside a vine as a parasite. Learn how it bursts out as a huge spotted bloom that smells of decay to attract flies.

name: The Oldest Living Trees
teaser: Trees that have outlived empires.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the oldest living trees on Earth: bristlecone pines nearing 5,000 years, and clonal colonies tens of thousands of years old. Learn how slow growth, tough wood, and high dry slopes let them survive so long.

name: The Largest Living Thing
teaser: A single organism that is bigger than a whale.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet Pando, a grove of quaking aspen that is actually one organism — tens of thousands of trunks sharing one root system. Learn how clonal growth works, how old Pando may be, and why it is considered the heaviest known living thing.

name: Plant Communication: Silent Signals
teaser: How plants warn, call for help, and listen.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore how plants communicate: warning chemicals released when chewed, scents that summon parasitic wasps, and underground fungal networks that share news. Learn what science has shown — and what remains metaphor.

name: Plants That Sleep
teaser: Leaves that fold at night and open at dawn.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover plants whose leaves fold up at night and open by day — a daily rhythm called nyctinasty. Learn why the praying plant and oxalis do this, how internal clocks drive it, and how a plant's 'sleep' was noticed by Darwin.

name: The Sensitive Plant: Touch Me
teaser: A plant whose leaves collapse at a touch.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the sensitive plant, whose feathery leaves fold and droop within seconds when touched. Learn why the movement may startle herbivores or shed rain, how water pressure drives it, and why it recovers within minutes.

name: Plant Intelligence: The Debate
teaser: Do plants think? What the research really says.

exploreAction.instruction: Weigh the debate over plant intelligence: plants sense light, touch, chemicals, and sound, and can learn simple associations. Learn what experiments actually show, where the claims outrun the evidence, and why the question fascinates scientists.

name: Seed Records: The Survivors
teaser: Seeds that waited centuries to sprout.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about record-breaking seeds: a date palm seed sprouted after 2,000 years, and Arctic lupine seeds germinated after 10,000. Understand how dryness and cold pause life without killing it, and what these seeds teach us about survival.

name: Growing Venus Flytraps
teaser: How to keep the world's most famous plant alive.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to care for a Venus flytrap: pure water, bright light, and poor soil with no minerals. Understand why tap water kills them, why they go dormant in winter, and why feeding them hamburger is a terrible idea.

name: Pitcher Plants: Trap Styles
teaser: Five continents, many shapes, one hungry idea.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour the pitcher plants of the world — from tropical hanging pitchers to North American trumpet pitchers. Learn how each species lures prey with nectar, drowns it in liquid, and digests it, and how some host ant colonies instead of eating them.

name: Sundews: The Glittering Traps
teaser: Sparkling tentacles that curl around prey.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet sundews, whose leaves glisten with sticky 'dew' that traps insects. Learn how the tentacles curl inward around prey, how the plant slowly digests it, and why sundews are among the most widespread carnivorous plants.

name: Butterworts: The Sticky Leaves
teaser: A violet-like flower with a deadly sticky leaf.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover butterworts, small carnivorous plants with greasy leaves that trap gnats and midges. Learn how the leaf curls slightly to digest prey, why they are called butterworts, and how they survive cold winters as tight buds.

name: Bladderworts: Underwater Snappers
teaser: Fastest traps in the plant world, under water.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet bladderworts, carnivorous plants with tiny underwater bladders that snap open in milliseconds to suck in prey. Learn how they grow in ponds with no roots, and why their traps are among the fastest known movements in nature.

name: Peace Lily: The Air Purifier
teaser: A forgiving bloom famous for cleaning indoor air.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the peace lily
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the peace lily, a shade-tolerant houseplant with elegant white blooms that has been studied for removing indoor air pollutants. Learn how its flower is actually a modified leaf, and how it tells you when it is thirsty by drooping.

name: Spider Plant: The Babies Plant
teaser: A houseplant that showers you with plantlets.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the spider plant
exploreAction.instruction: Discover the spider plant, a tough houseplant that sends out arching stems covered in baby plantlets. Learn how to root the babies in water, why it tolerates neglect and low light, and why it has been a kitchen-shelf favorite for generations.

name: Rubber Plant: The Comeback
teaser: A Victorian giant that returned to modern homes.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the rubber plant
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the rubber plant, a glossy-leaved tree popular in Victorian parlors and modern apartments alike. Learn how its sap was once tapped for rubber, how it grows into a small tree indoors, and how to keep its leaves polished and happy.

name: ZZ Plant: The Indestructible
teaser: A plant that thrives on neglect and low light.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the ZZ plant
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the ZZ plant, a slow-growing tropical whose waxy leaves and potato-like roots survive months without water and dim corners. Learn why it is everywhere in offices, and how its stems grow from underground rhizomes.

name: Bonsai: Miniature Trees
teaser: The art of growing full-size trees in tiny pots.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the thousand-year-old art of bonsai: pruning roots and branches, wiring trunks, and shaping with patience to grow a full tree in miniature. Understand how shallow pots and careful cuts keep trees small yet healthy.

name: Hydroponics: Growing Without Soil
teaser: Growing plants in water and nutrients.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover hydroponics, growing plants with roots in nutrient-rich water instead of soil. Learn how plants get everything from dissolved minerals, why yields can exceed soil farming, and how it feeds astronauts and cities alike.

name: Vertical Farming: Stacked Fields
teaser: Growing food in indoor towers.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore vertical farming, growing crops in stacked indoor layers with LED light and controlled climate. Learn why it uses a fraction of the water of farms, what it grows best — greens and herbs — and why energy costs remain its biggest challenge.

name: Greenhouses: Glass Houses
teaser: How a pane of glass changes a plant's world.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how greenhouses trap warmth: sunlight enters as light and becomes heat that glass holds inside. Discover how this lets gardeners grow tomatoes in winter, and how ventilation, shade, and humidity turn a glass box into a climate.

name: Permaculture: Designing with Nature
teaser: Gardening that copies natural ecosystems.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore permaculture, a design approach that builds gardens to work like natural ecosystems — stacking plants, catching water, and turning waste into soil. Learn why mixing species beats monoculture and how it aims to regenerate land.

name: Heirloom Seeds: Saving the Past
teaser: Old varieties kept alive by gardeners.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet heirloom seeds, open-pollinated varieties passed down for generations before modern hybrids. Learn why their flavors and colors differ from store varieties, how saving seeds works, and why seed banks exist to protect diversity.

name: Maple Syrup: The Sugar Season
teaser: How a tree's stored sugar becomes breakfast gold.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow maple syrup from sugar maple trees that store starch in their trunks to the early-spring run of sweet sap. Learn why freezing nights and warm days make sap flow, how 40 liters of sap become one liter of syrup, and why the season is short.

name: The Rubber Tree: Liquid Gold
teaser: A tree whose milky sap changed the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the rubber tree of the Amazon, whose latex made tires, hoses, and erasers possible. Learn how tappers wound the bark to collect sap, how one British smuggler's seeds broke Brazil's monopoly, and why plantations moved to Asia.

name: Paper: From Tree to Page
teaser: How wood becomes the sheets you write on.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace paper from tree to page: logs are chipped, cooked into pulp, and pressed into sheets. Learn how cellulose fibers bond when dried, how recycling shortens fibers, and why bamboo, cotton, and hemp also make excellent paper.

name: Lumber: The Wood We Build With
teaser: How forests become beams, planks, and furniture.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore how trees become lumber: felling, sawing, drying, and grading. Learn why wood's grain and rings affect its strength, how kiln drying prevents warping, and how sustainable forestry regrows what it harvests.

name: Charcoal: Wood Turned Black
teaser: Burning wood without air leaves pure carbon.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how charcoal is made by heating wood with little oxygen, driving off gases and leaving nearly pure carbon. Discover how it burns hotter and cleaner than wood, how it powered iron smelting for millennia, and how it filters and draws.

name: Cork: The Bark That Keeps Giving
teaser: A tree that is stripped but never felled.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the cork oak, whose bark can be stripped every nine years without killing the tree. Learn why cork is light, waterproof, and springy, how wine corks are punched from bark, and why cork oak forests shelter rare wildlife.

name: Cinnamon: Rolled Bark Spice
teaser: The spice that is literally tree bark.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cinnamon sticks are rolled strips of inner bark from a tropical tree. Follow the peeling, curling, and drying that turns bark into quills, and understand why the spice drove trade for thousands of years.

name: Teak: The Shipbuilder's Wood
teaser: A tropical hardwood that defied the sea.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet teak, a Southeast Asian hardwood so oily and dense that it resists water, rot, and termites. Learn how it built ships, decks, and furniture for centuries, and why its natural oils make it prized — and now closely managed.

name: Bamboo: Nature's Steel
teaser: A grass that builds bridges and skyscrapers.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why bamboo is called nature's steel: its hollow, segmented stems are light yet strong, and it grows faster than any timber. Learn how it is used for scaffolding, bridges, and even earthquake-resistant houses.

name: Moss Gardens: Green Carpets
teaser: The ancient Japanese art of cultivating moss.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the moss garden, a Japanese tradition that grows carpets of moss under dappled shade. Learn how mosses create a quiet, ancient feel, why they prefer acid damp ground, and how the famous Saiho-ji garden earned its nickname.

name: Lichens: The Double Organism
teaser: A fungus and an alga living as one.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover that a lichen is not one organism but a fungus hosting algae or bacteria that make food from sunlight. Learn how this partnership lets lichens colonize bare rock, survive space-like conditions, and paint cliffs in orange and green.

name: Ivy: The Clinging Climber
teaser: A vine that climbs walls without harming them.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet ivy, a vine that climbs with sticky rootlets rather than twining. Learn why it actually insulates and shields walls, how its berries feed winter birds, and why it is both loved for greenery and feared for its spread.

name: Dandelion Parachutes
teaser: The physics of the world's most famous seed flight.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how dandelion seeds fly on parachutes of hair-like bristles that catch the wind. Discover how the pappus creates a vortex that holds the seed aloft, letting it drift for kilometers — one of nature's most efficient gliders.

name: Thorns, Spines, and Prickles
teaser: Three ways plants make armor.

exploreAction.instruction: Sort out the plant world's armor: thorns are modified stems, spines are modified leaves, and prickles grow from the skin. Learn why roses have prickles, cacti have spines, and hawthorns have thorns — and how each deters grazers.

name: Autumn Leaves: The Color Show
teaser: Why leaves turn gold, orange, and red in fall.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why leaves change color in autumn: as chlorophyll breaks down, hidden carotenoids show gold and orange, while trapped sugars turn red. Discover how day length and temperature drive the show, and why some years are more vivid.

name: The Almond: Flower Before Fruit
teaser: A tree whose nut hides inside a peach-like fruit.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the almond, whose kernel is a seed inside a fruit that looks like a small peach. Learn why almonds need bees to pollinate early blossoms, why they are a thirsty crop, and how bitter almonds differ from sweet ones.

name: Walnut: The Brain-Shaped Nut
teaser: A nut whose wrinkly kernel is packed with oil.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the walnut, a nut whose oily kernel resembles a brain and has fed humans for millennia. Learn how the green husk stains everything, why the shell resists cracking, and how walnuts from Central Asia became a global crop.

name: Cashew: The Dangerous Nut
teaser: A nut that grows outside its fruit and needs careful handling.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cashews grow as a seed dangling beneath a swollen 'apple' — and that the shell between them contains a caustic oil. Discover why cashews are always sold shelled, and how the cashew apple makes juice and wine.

name: Pistachio: The Smiling Nut
teaser: A nut that cracks open on its own when ripe.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the pistachio, a small nut whose shell pops open as it ripens — a trait people have loved for thousands of years. Learn how the trees need a cold winter and a hot summer, and why most pistachios in the world come from a few regions.

name: Pecan: The Southern Nut
teaser: A North American nut tree with a long pedigree.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the pecan, a hickory-family nut native to North America that Native peoples harvested long before colonists arrived. Learn how a single tree named Centennial spread across the South, and how pecans became pie's best friend.

name: Strawberry: Not a Berry
teaser: A fruit with seeds on the outside and a berry inside.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the surprising botany of strawberries: the red flesh is a swollen receptacle, and the 'seeds' on its surface are the true fruits called achenes. Discover how runners clone strawberry plants and why they are a spring favorite.

name: Pineapple: A Fruit of Fruits
teaser: Many flowers fuse into one spiky fruit.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover that a pineapple is a compound fruit formed when dozens of flowers fuse around a single core. Learn how the plant grows in dry soil with tough leaves, how it was spread by sailors as a symbol of welcome, and how it ripens.

name: Mango: King of Fruits
teaser: A tropical fruit loved for over 4,000 years.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the mango, a fruit cultivated in South Asia for over four thousand years and now grown across the tropics. Learn about its hundreds of varieties, the allergenic compounds in its skin, and why its trees can live for centuries.

name: Pomegranate: The Crown of Seeds
teaser: A fruit full of juicy jewel-like seeds.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the pomegranate, whose leathery rind hides chambers of juicy seeds called arils. Learn why it appears in myth from Persia to Greece, how its deep red juice stains everything, and why the tree thrives in dry climates.

name: Kiwi: The Fuzzy Fruit
teaser: A Chinese fruit renamed for a New Zealand bird.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the kiwifruit from Chinese mountains to New Zealand orchards, where it was renamed after the kiwi bird. Learn why the fruit's fuzzy skin is edible, how the green flesh stays fresh for months, and how it spread worldwide.

name: Figs: Fruit and Wasp
teaser: A fruit that depends on a tiny wasp to survive.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover that a fig is not a fruit but an inverted flower cluster, pollinated only by tiny fig wasps that crawl inside. Learn how each fig species has its own wasp, why commercial figs are self-pollinating, and why figs are both ancient and strange.

name: Date Palm: The Oasis Tree
teaser: A desert palm that has fed people for millennia.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the date palm, a tree that has fed desert peoples for five thousand years, its sweet fruits drying into long-lasting food. Learn how palms survive heat and salt, how dates are pollinated by hand in some groves, and why they are called the tree of life.

name: Avocado: The Ancient Fruit
teaser: A fatty fruit that outlived its original partners.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why avocados are a botanical puzzle: their giant seed was spread by now-extinct giant animals. Discover how the fruit's healthy fats made it famous, why it was named alligator pear, and how it went from Mesoamerican staple to world food.

name: Papaya: The Fruit With an Enzyme
teaser: A tropical fruit that tenderizes meat.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the papaya, a fast-growing tropical fruit whose latex contains papain, an enzyme that breaks down protein — the reason it tenderizes meat. Learn how papain is used in medicine and brewing, and how papaya trees fruit within a year.

name: Lychee: The Delicate Fruit
teaser: A translucent fruit prized for centuries in China.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the lychee, a fruit with a rough red shell hiding sweet translucent flesh, prized in China for over two thousand years. Learn why lychees must be eaten fresh, how emperors had them raced across the country, and how the tree fruits in clusters.

name: Chlorophyll A and B
teaser: Two green pigments with different jobs.

exploreAction.instruction: Compare chlorophyll a and b, the two pigments that color plants green. Learn how each absorbs different wavelengths of light so plants can catch more of the sun, and how carotenoids back them up by capturing the blue-green light they miss.

name: Plant Cells: Built With Walls
teaser: The boxy building blocks that hold plants up.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the plant cell, wrapped in a stiff wall of cellulose that animal cells lack. Learn how the wall lets plants grow tall without bones, how chloroplasts make food inside, and how the large central vacuole stores water and presses against the wall.

name: Root Hairs: The Feeders
teaser: Tiny threads that do the plant's drinking.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover root hairs, microscopic thread-like extensions that give roots enormous surface area for absorbing water and minerals. Learn how a single plant can have billions of them, and how they are the true interface between plant and soil.

name: Capillary Action in Plants
teaser: How water climbs inside narrow tubes.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how water rises through plants partly by capillary action — the pull of water molecules against tube walls. Combine it with evaporation and root pressure to understand how tall trees move water hundreds of meters upward.

name: Osmosis: How Plants Drink
teaser: Why water moves into roots and plumps leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Understand osmosis, the movement of water across membranes toward saltier or sugar-rich solutions. Learn how it fills plant cells with pressure, why saltwater wilts land plants, and why crisp celery and droopy leaves are both about osmosis.

name: Lenticels: Breathing in Bark
teaser: Tiny bark pores that keep woody stems alive.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet lenticels, the small corky spots on bark and stems that let gases pass where bark is otherwise airtight. Learn how they allow oxygen in and carbon dioxide out, and why the pattern of lenticels differs on every tree.

name: Chloroplasts: Solar Panels
teaser: The organelles that turn light into sugar.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet chloroplasts, the organelles where photosynthesis happens — nature's solar panels. Learn how their stacked membranes catch light, how they make glucose, and how they were once free-living bacteria that moved inside plant cells long ago.

name: Starch and Sugar: Storing Energy
teaser: How plants bank their food for later.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants store extra food: as starch, a chain of sugar molecules packed into grains that keep in roots, seeds, and tubers. Discover why potatoes, rice, and wheat are all starch stores, and how plants turn starch back to sugar when needed.

name: Cellulose: The Plant Plastic
teaser: The most abundant organic molecule on Earth.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet cellulose, the strong sugar polymer that makes plant cell walls — the most abundant organic molecule on the planet. Learn how its strength built wood, paper, and cotton, and why animals struggle to digest it while termites and cows use helpers.

name: Auxin: The Growth Hormone
teaser: The plant hormone that directs growth and bending.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about auxin, the plant hormone that tells cells to stretch and roots to grow down. Discover how its movement to one side makes stems bend toward light and away from gravity, and how gardeners use it to root cuttings.

name: Ethylene: The Ripening Gas
teaser: The invisible gas that makes fruit ripen.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet ethylene, the gas plants release to signal ripening and aging. Learn why a ripe banana in a bag ripens green tomatoes nearby, how shippers control ethylene to time fruit arrival, and how ethylene makes leaves fall.

name: Gibberellins: The Stretch Hormone
teaser: The hormones that make plants grow tall.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover gibberellins, plant hormones that drive stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering. Learn how 'foolish seedling' disease on rice led to their discovery, and why breeders use them to grow taller grapes and longer stems.

name: Photoperiodism: Day-Length Clocks
teaser: How plants read the calendar by daylight.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants measure day length to time flowering — short-day plants bloom as nights lengthen, long-day plants as days stretch. Discover how chrysanthemums and poinsettias are tricked with darkness to bloom on schedule.

name: Vernalization: The Cold Spring
teaser: Why some seeds need winter before they bloom.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover vernalization, the need of some plants for a period of cold before they will flower. Learn why winter wheat must feel winter, how tulip bulbs time their spring bloom, and how farmers trick plants with refrigeration.

name: Allelopathy: Chemical Rivalry
teaser: How plants poison their neighbors' chances.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about allelopathy, where plants release chemicals that suppress rivals — black walnut poisons nearby gardens, and eucalyptus clears the ground beneath it. Discover how farmers use these effects and how forests shift as a result.

name: Weeds: Plants Out of Place
teaser: Why some plants are called weeds.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore what makes a plant a weed: not a species but a situation — a plant growing where it is unwanted. Learn why weeds are tough competitors, how their seeds wait in soil, and why one person's weed is another's wildflower.

name: Kudzu: The Vine That Ate the South
teaser: A Japanese vine that swallowed the American South.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet kudzu, a fast-growing vine introduced to the US for erosion control that proceeded to cover trees, poles, and buildings. Learn how it grows a foot a day, why it is hard to kill, and how it is now eaten and woven in its home range.

name: Invasive Plants: The Uninvited
teaser: How foreign plants take over new lands.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants travel across oceans in cargo, ballast, and gardens — and some run wild. Discover why a plant with no natural enemies in a new land can smother natives, and how managers battle species like water hyacinth and knotweed.

name: Biodiversity: Why Variety Matters
teaser: Why plant diversity keeps ecosystems healthy.

exploreAction.instruction: Understand biodiversity — the variety of plants and other life in an ecosystem. Learn why mixed meadows resist pests and drought better than single-crop fields, and how losing plant species ripples through insects, birds, and soils.

name: Pollinator Gardens: Bee Havens
teaser: Planting a garden that feeds bees and butterflies.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to plant a garden that feeds bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Understand why native flowers, bloom succession, and no pesticides matter, and how even a balcony pot becomes a stop on the pollinator highway.

name: Crop Rotation: The Field Cycle
teaser: Why farmers move crops from field to field.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why farmers rotate crops instead of planting the same field forever. Learn how different crops use and return different nutrients, how legumes recharge soil nitrogen, and how rotation breaks the cycle of pests and diseases.

name: No-Till Farming: Leave the Soil Alone
teaser: Farming without plowing the earth.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how no-till farming grows crops without plowing, leaving crop residue to protect soil. Understand how this builds organic matter, stores carbon, and reduces erosion — and why it pairs with cover crops to feed the soil.

name: Building Soil: The Gardener's Craft
teaser: How good gardens are made from the ground up.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover that soil is alive with bacteria, fungi, and worms that feed plants. Learn how adding compost, mulch, and cover crops builds healthy soil, and why healthy soil holds water, resists pests, and needs no chemical boosters.

name: Mulch: The Garden Blanket
teaser: A protective layer that does the gardener's work.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how a layer of mulch — wood chips, straw, or leaves — keeps soil moist, cool, and weed-free while slowly feeding it. Understand why mulch reduces watering, and how different mulches change the soil as they break down.

name: Starting Seeds Indoors
teaser: How gardeners give seeds a head start.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the craft of starting seeds indoors: light, warmth, moisture, and timing. Understand why seedlings stretch for weak light, how to harden them off before the garden, and which crops love a head start and which hate it.

name: Heirloom vs Hybrid Seeds
teaser: Two ways to breed a better tomato.

exploreAction.instruction: Untangle heirloom and hybrid seeds: heirlooms breed true from saved seed with unique flavors, hybrids are controlled crosses with vigor but seeds that don't come true. Learn which to choose for flavor, resilience, and saving seeds.

name: Food Forests: Edible Ecosystems
teaser: Gardens layered like a real forest.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore the food forest, a garden designed in layers like a forest — canopy fruit trees, berry shrubs, herbs, and ground covers all stacked. Learn how each layer fills a different niche, and how these gardens feed people with less work.

name: Drought Gardens: Thriving Dry
teaser: Gardens built to survive water shortages.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to garden where water is scarce: choose drought-tolerant natives, mulch hard, water deep and rarely, and group plants by thirst. Discover xeriscaping and how plants like lavender and succulents thrive on neglect.

name: Urban Gardening: Cities Grow
teaser: Growing food in the middle of the city.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how city dwellers grow food on rooftops, balconies, and vacant lots. Learn about community gardens, container growing, and how urban farms shorten food miles and cool the city while feeding neighborhoods.

name: Botanic Gardens: Living Collections
teaser: Museums of living plants from around the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the botanic garden, a living museum that collects and studies plants from everywhere. Learn how they preserve rare species, teach the public, and how the oldest ones began as medicinal herb gardens attached to universities.

name: Herbal Teas: Leaves in Water
teaser: How flowers, leaves, and roots become tea.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore herbal teas or tisanes — infusions of leaves, flowers, and roots that are not tea at all. Learn how chamomile, peppermint, and hibiscus are brewed, how each became a folk remedy, and how drying concentrates their flavors.

name: Plant Dyes: Color From Leaves
teaser: How plants painted cloth for thousands of years.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the plants that colored our world before synthetic dyes: indigo for blue, madder for red, weld for yellow. Learn how mordants fix plant pigments to cloth, how indigo's chemistry is famously tricky, and how plant dyes are returning.

name: Indigo: The Blue Gold
teaser: A plant that turned fabric the color of the sky.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover indigo, the plant whose leaves yield the deepest blue dye, worth fortunes in the trade of empires. Learn why the dye needs fermentation to appear, how it built colonies and inspired rebellions, and why blue jeans owe it a debt.

name: Cotton: The Fiber of Empires
teaser: A plant whose seed fluff clothed the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet cotton, a plant that wraps its seeds in fluffy fibers that became the world's most important textile. Learn how the fibers are spun and woven, how cotton shaped slavery and industry, and why its cultivation still matters today.

name: Flax: The Linen Fiber
teaser: A slender plant that made the coolest fabric.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover flax, the plant whose stem fibers are spun into linen — the fabric of Egyptian pharaohs and summer shirts. Learn how rotting, breaking, and combing free the fibers, and why linen stays cool and grows stronger when wet.

name: Hemp: The Versatile Plant
teaser: A crop with a use for almost everything.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet hemp, a fast-growing variety of cannabis bred for fiber and seed, once used for rope, sails, paper, and cloth. Learn why hemp was an essential crop for centuries, how its oil and seeds feed us, and why its regulation is changing.

name: Rose Oil: The Perfume of Kings
teaser: Why true rose oil costs more than gold.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why genuine rose oil is so precious: it takes thousands of hand-picked petals to produce a single gram. Discover the rose fields of Bulgaria, how steam distillation captures the scent at dawn, and how synthetic alternatives flooded the market.

name: Jasmine: The Night Scent
teaser: A flower that perfumes the evening air.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet jasmine, whose white flowers release their strongest scent at night to attract moths. Learn how jasmine became the base of countless perfumes, how the flowers are harvested before dawn, and why a single vine scents a whole garden.

name: Sandalwood: The Aromatic Heart
teaser: A tree whose fragrant heartwood is carved and distilled.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet sandalwood, a slow-growing tree whose heartwood carries a warm scent for decades. Learn how it is distilled into oil for perfumes and ceremonies, why wild trees are endangered by demand, and how plantations are trying to restore it.

name: Frankincense: The Sacred Resin
teaser: A desert tree that weeps aromatic tears.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover frankincense, the resin of a small desert tree, collected as 'tears' by cutting the bark. Learn why it was worth more than gold in ancient trade, how it is burned in ceremonies worldwide, and why the trees are now under pressure.

name: Myrrh: The Bitter Resin
teaser: A fragrant gum that traveled the ancient spice roads.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet myrrh, the aromatic resin of a small thorny tree from Arabia and East Africa, traded for thousands of years. Learn how it is tapped, why it was used in embalming and incense, and how it remains a valued medicine and perfume.

name: Clubmosses: The Ancient Groundcover
teaser: Spore plants that witnessed the age of coal.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet clubmosses, ancient spore plants whose giant relatives formed the great coal forests. Learn how modern ones are small evergreen groundcovers, how their spores were once used in fireworks and pills, and why they are living links to deep time.

name: Horsetails: The Scouring Rushes
teaser: Plants so gritty they polished armor.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover horsetails, ancient plants whose stems are packed with silica so abrasive that settlers used them to scour pots. Learn how their ancestors grew as tall as trees, and how the living ones still spread by underground runners.

name: Cycads: Living Dinosaurs
teaser: Palm-like plants older than the dinosaurs.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet cycads, ancient seed plants that look like palms but are far older, having fed dinosaurs. Learn why they are toxic unless processed, how they are pollinated by beetles, and why many species are now among the most endangered plants alive.

name: Trees of Life: Ecosystem Engineers
teaser: Why a single tree can support a whole world.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how one large tree can host hundreds of species — insects in its bark, birds in its crown, fungi on its roots. Explore keystone trees like oaks and figs, and understand why removing one old tree can ripple through an entire ecosystem.

name: Dragonfruit: The Night Bloom
teaser: A cactus fruit whose flower opens for one night.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet dragonfruit, the fruit of a climbing cactus whose spectacular flowers open for a single night and rely on moths and bats. Learn why the pink skin and spotted flesh are so striking, how the plant climbs with aerial roots, and how it fruits in dry heat.

name: Durian: The King of Fruits
teaser: A spiky fruit famous for its powerful smell.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet durian, the Southeast Asian fruit whose spiky shell hides creamy flesh — and whose smell can clear a room. Learn why some love it and others can't stand it, how it is banned on public transport, and why its flavor is intensely rich.

name: Jackfruit: The Giant Fruit
teaser: The largest tree fruit can weigh tens of kilograms.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover jackfruit, the largest fruit that grows on a tree, reaching over 30 kilograms. Learn how its flesh is eaten ripe and its young fruit cooked like meat, and why it is called a 'miracle crop' for feeding many people cheaply.

name: Rambutan: The Hairy Fruit
teaser: A sweet fruit that wears a coat of spines.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet rambutan, a tropical fruit covered in soft red 'hair,' closely related to lychee and longan. Learn how the sweet translucent flesh is peeled out, how the tree fruits in clusters, and why its name means 'hairy' in Malay.

name: Mangosteen: Queen of Fruits
teaser: A purple fruit with snow-white segments.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover mangosteen, a deep-purple fruit whose thick rind hides snow-white segments with a delicate flavor. Learn why it was long forbidden to export from Southeast Asia, how the rind stains, and why it pairs with durian as king and queen.

name: Guava: The Fragrant Fruit
teaser: A vitamin-rich fruit that scents a whole room.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet guava, a tropical fruit whose sweet aroma fills a room. Learn how the whole fruit — skin and all — is edible, why it is packed with vitamin C, and how guava trees grow from seed into fruiting shrubs within a few years.

name: Soursop: The Prickly Fruit
teaser: A soft-spiked fruit with creamy tangy flesh.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover soursop, a tropical fruit covered in soft spines with creamy, tangy white flesh. Learn how it is made into juice and ice cream, why its tree is called graviola, and how its leaves are steeped as a folk tea.

name: Passionfruit: The Tart Jewel
teaser: A wrinkled fruit full of crunchy seeds.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet passionfruit, whose wrinkled purple or yellow shell hides aromatic pulp studded with edible seeds. Learn why the vine's flower is so elaborate, how the fruit is scooped and juiced, and why it grows fast on tropical trellises.

name: Starfruit: The Star Slices
teaser: A fruit that slices into perfect five-pointed stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover starfruit, a tropical fruit that forms a perfect star when sliced. Learn why its ridges make crunchy waxy slices, how the whole fruit is eaten fresh, and why people with kidney issues should avoid it.

name: Coconut Water: The Young Drink
teaser: The clear liquid inside young coconuts.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why young green coconuts are full of clear, slightly sweet water that has been called nature's sports drink. Understand how the water becomes solid flesh as the coconut matures, and how coconut water is tapped, bottled, and sold worldwide.

name: Plantains: The Cooking Banana
teaser: A starchy banana meant for the kitchen.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet plantain, the starchy cousin of the dessert banana, always cooked before eating. Learn how it is fried, boiled, and baked across Africa, the Caribbean, and Latin America, and how its firm flesh holds up to heat.

name: Sweet Potato: The Orange Root
teaser: A sweet root with a tangled history of names.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the sweet potato
exploreAction.instruction: Untangle the sweet potato, a New World root that traveled to the Pacific long before European ships. Learn why it is not a potato and not a yam, how its orange flesh stores vitamin A, and how the vine spreads easily from cuttings.

name: Yams: The African Root
teaser: True yams that anchor West African feasts.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the true yam, a tropical root crop from Africa and Asia, different from the sweet potato sold in many markets. Learn how yams grow on twining vines, why they are central to West African ceremonies, and how they are pounded into fufu.

name: Cassava: The Drought Survivor
teaser: A root that feeds millions on poor soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover cassava, a tough root crop from South America that feeds hundreds of millions, especially where soil is poor and rain unreliable. Learn why it must be cooked or fermented to remove cyanide, and how it becomes tapioca and garri.

name: Okra: The Slimy Pod
teaser: A heat-loving pod famous for its slippery texture.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet okra, a tropical pod that thickens soups and stews with its natural mucilage. Learn how the plant grows fast in heat, how its edible pods are fried or pickled, and why it crossed from Africa to the Americas with the slave trade.

name: Barley: The Oldest Grain
teaser: A grain that fed humanity before wheat did.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet barley, one of the first grains ever cultivated, grown for ten thousand years. Learn how it became beer and bread, why it tolerates poor soil and cold, and how its history traces the very start of farming.

name: Oats: The Porridge Grain
teaser: A grain that began as a weed of wheat fields.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover oats, a grain that may have started as a weed in wheat fields before becoming a breakfast staple. Learn why oats suit cool damp climates, how they are rolled and steel-cut, and why porridge became a symbol of hearty morning food.

name: Rye: The Hardy Grain
teaser: A grain that grows where others fail.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet rye, a tough grain that thrives on poor, cold soil where wheat struggles. Learn how it made dense dark bread, how it was the grain of northern Europe, and why a fungus on rye — ergot — once caused mysterious outbreaks.

name: Quinoa: The Andean Grain
teaser: A high-altitude seed that became a superfood.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow quinoa from the high Andes, where it fed the Incas for millennia, to supermarket shelves worldwide. Learn why it is a complete protein, how its bitter coating is washed away, and how its rising price changed Andean farming.

name: Millet: The Drought Grain
teaser: A tiny grain that feeds millions on dry land.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet millet, a group of small grains that grow fast on dry land where rice and wheat fail. Learn how it has fed people across Africa and Asia for thousands of years, and why it is being rediscovered as a climate-friendly crop.

name: Sorghum: The African Grain
teaser: A hardy grain that tolerates heat and drought.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover sorghum, a tall grass grown for grain in hot dry regions across Africa and Asia. Learn how it feeds millions, becomes flour and beer, and how its ability to survive drought makes it a crop of the future.

name: Lentils: The Tiny Legumes
teaser: Small pulses that nourish the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet lentils, among the oldest cultivated crops, grown for eight thousand years. Learn how these tiny legumes pack protein, cook quickly, and enrich the soil by fixing nitrogen, and why they feed millions from India to the Middle East.

name: Chickpeas: The Garbanzo
teaser: A knobby legume behind hummus and falafel.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover chickpeas, the bumpy legumes that became hummus, falafel, and chana masala. Learn how they were domesticated in the Middle East thousands of years ago, how they fix nitrogen in the soil, and why their flour is used in baking.

name: Peanuts: The Ground Nuts
teaser: A legume that buries its pods to ripen.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why the peanut is a legume, not a nut, and how it flowers above ground but buries its pods to ripen below. Follow it from South America to Africa and the American South, and meet George Washington Carver's work to save Southern farms.

name: Beans: The Ancient Legumes
teaser: Pods of protein that traveled the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet beans — common, kidney, black, and pinto — legumes domesticated in the Americas and carried worldwide. Learn how they fix nitrogen, pair with corn in the classic 'three sisters' garden, and why they have fed civilizations for millennia.

name: Soy: Milk and Tofu
teaser: How a bean becomes milk, curd, and sauce.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the soybean through its transformations: soaked, ground, and strained into soy milk; curdled into tofu; fermented into miso, tempeh, and soy sauce. Learn how East Asian cooks turned one bean into an entire cuisine.

name: The Cabbage Family: One Species, Many Crops
teaser: How kale, broccoli, and cabbage are the same plant.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover that kale, broccoli, cauliflower, cabbage, and Brussels sprouts are all one species, bred for different parts. Learn how selective breeding turned wild mustard leaves into heads, florets, and stems — a living lesson in plant breeding.

name: Carrots: The Orange Root
teaser: A root bred from a bitter white ancestor.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the carrot, first grown for its aromatic leaves and seeds, later bred into the orange root we know. Learn how Dutch growers may have popularized orange, and how carrots store vitamin A as beta-carotene, the pigment that colors them.

name: Spinach: The Iron Myth
teaser: A leafy green with a famous decimal error.

exploreAction.instruction: Uncover the spinach iron myth: a misplaced decimal point made it seem ten times richer in iron than it is, inspiring Popeye. Learn how spinach really earns its keep with vitamins, and how its taste changes with the seasons.

name: Lettuce: The Salad Leaf
teaser: A leaf crop bred from a wild bitter weed.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet lettuce, grown by Egyptians and Greeks, and bred from a bitter wild weed into today's crisp heads and leaves. Learn why it bolts and turns bitter in heat, how iceberg got its name, and how the plant was once eaten for its seeds and oil.

name: Prayer Plant: The Folder
teaser: A houseplant that folds its leaves at night.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the prayer plant
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the prayer plant, whose oval leaves fold upward at night as if praying, then spread flat by day. Learn why this daily movement happens, how its patterned leaves brighten shelves, and how it thrives in warm humid rooms.

name: Alocasia: Elephant Ears
teaser: Dramatic arrow-shaped leaves on jungle plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover alocasia, tropical plants with huge arrow-shaped leaves that earned the name elephant ears. Learn how their stems rise from underground corms, why they love humidity, and how some species grow leaves over a meter long.

name: Calathea: The Striped Beauty
teaser: Houseplants with painted-looking leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet calathea, tropical houseplants whose leaves look hand-painted with stripes and spots. Learn why they fold at night like the prayer plant, why they demand humidity, and why their vivid patterns evolved to cope with forest-floor shade.

name: Philodendron: The Heart Leaf
teaser: A trailing vine with glossy heart-shaped leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover philodendrons, one of the most popular houseplant groups, named 'tree lover' for climbing trees in the wild. Learn why heart-leaf philodendron tolerates low light, how to propagate it from cuttings, and how its aerial roots grip bark.

name: Indoor Cacti: Desert on the Shelf
teaser: Why desert cacti thrive on windowsills.

exploreAction.targetName: how to care for indoor cacti
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow cacti indoors: bright sun, fast-draining soil, and rare watering. Understand how their winter rest, shallow pots, and 'soak and dry' cycles mimic the desert, and why most indoor cacti die from kindness rather than neglect.

name: Air Plants: No Soil Needed
teaser: Plants that live on air alone.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet air plants, tillandsias that grow without soil, absorbing water through fuzzy leaf scales. Learn how they cling to branches and rocks in the wild, how to water them with a soak or mist, and why they flower once before making pups.

name: String of Pearls: The Beaded Vine
teaser: A hanging plant that looks like a necklace.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of string of pearls
exploreAction.instruction: Discover string of pearls, a hanging succulent whose stems are strung with bead-like leaves. Learn how the round leaves store water and why they are fragile, how the plant was named, and how to grow it in bright indirect light.

name: Jade Plant: The Money Plant
teaser: A glossy succulent that is said to bring good luck.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the jade plant
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the jade plant, a succulent with glossy oval leaves that is considered lucky in many cultures. Learn how its tree-like trunk and plump leaves store water, how it lives for decades, and why its leaves root wherever they fall.

name: Easy Garden Herbs
teaser: The herbs anyone can grow on a windowsill.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the easiest herbs to grow at home: basil, mint, chives, parsley, and rosemary. Understand which want sun and which tolerate shade, how to pinch and harvest without killing the plant, and why fresh herbs beat dried ones.

name: Growing Tomatoes
teaser: The garden favorite and its simple secrets.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow great tomatoes: full sun, rich soil, and steady watering. Understand why pruning suckers helps some varieties, how staking keeps fruit off the ground, and why homegrown tomatoes taste different from store ones.

name: Hand Pollination
teaser: When gardeners play bee.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn when gardeners must hand-pollinate: no wind indoors, few bees in greenhouses, or stubborn squash flowers. Discover how to transfer pollen with a brush or finger, and how to tell male from female flowers on squash and melons.

name: Raised Beds: The Gardener's Table
teaser: Growing vegetables above the ground.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why gardeners build raised beds: better soil control, warmer spring soil, fewer weeds, and easier weeding. Learn how to fill and maintain them, and why they let gardeners grow more food in less space.

name: Container Gardening: Pots and Patios
teaser: Growing a full garden in pots.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow vegetables and herbs in containers on balconies and patios. Understand why pot size, drainage, and watering matter most, how self-watering pots work, and which crops — like tomatoes and peppers — thrive in pots.

name: Companion Planting: Garden Allies
teaser: Why some plants grow better side by side.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore companion planting, the idea that some plants help neighbors — marigolds deter pests, basil pairs with tomatoes, and beans feed corn. Learn which pairings have real science behind them and which are garden folklore.

name: Garden Birds: The Pest Squad
teaser: How feathered visitors protect your vegetables.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why birds are gardeners' allies: they eat caterpillars, aphids, and slugs by the thousands. Discover how feeders, water, and nesting spots attract them, and how to protect berries while still welcoming insect-eaters.

name: Willows: The Riverside Trees
teaser: Trees that love water and heal with bark.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the willow, a fast-growing tree of riverbanks whose bark gave us aspirin's ancestor. Learn how willow twigs root wherever they touch damp ground, how their flexible wood became cricket bats and baskets, and why they love water.

name: Poplar: The Fast Grower
teaser: Quick timber that reshapes the landscape.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover poplars, among the fastest-growing trees, often planted for quick timber and windbreaks. Learn how their quaking leaves shimmer in the breeze, how cottonwood seeds drift on fluff, and how they are farmed for paper and plywood.

name: The American Chestnut: A Lost Forest
teaser: How a fungus erased a billion trees.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the chestnut blight
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the American chestnut, once a quarter of eastern US forests, wiped out by an imported fungus within decades. Learn how chestnut blight spread, why the trees sprout and die back, and how scientists are breeding blight-resistant hybrids.

name: The Elm: The Lining Tree
teaser: Graceful trees that once shaded the streets.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the elm, the graceful tree that lined boulevards until Dutch elm disease arrived. Learn how the beetle-spread fungus killed millions, how surviving elms are rare, and how cities are replanting disease-resistant hybrids.

name: The Maple: The Gold Tree
teaser: Trees that blaze with autumn color.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover maples, trees famous for their brilliant autumn color and for maple syrup. Learn how their wing-shaped seeds spin like helicopters, why their wood makes guitars and bowling pins, and how Japan's maples became garden icons.

name: Birch Bark: The Canoe Tree
teaser: How bark sheets built watercraft.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Indigenous peoples of North America built canoes from birch bark — sheets peeled from the tree, sewn, and sealed with pitch. Discover why birch bark is waterproof, rot-resistant, and peels in paper-thin sheets.

name: Oak Acorns: The Forest Feast
teaser: The nuts that feed entire forests.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore the acorn, the oak's seed, a food source for squirrels, jays, deer, and people. Learn why acorn harvests vary from year to year in 'mast years', how jays bury and forget thousands, planting forests by accident.

name: Sequoia vs Redwood
teaser: Two giants, two records.

exploreAction.instruction: Sort out the two giant conifers: coast redwoods are the tallest, while giant sequoias are the most massive. Learn where each grows, how their bark resists fire, and how both survive for thousands of years.

name: Cedars: The Aromatic Trees
teaser: Scented evergreens of mountains and legends.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet cedars, aromatic evergreens whose wood smells of pencil shavings and built temples and ships. Learn the difference between true cedars and the many 'cedars' that are junipers or cypresses, and why the wood repels moths.

name: Bald Cypress: The Swamp Tree
teaser: Trees that breathe through woody knees.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the bald cypress
exploreAction.instruction: Discover the bald cypress, a swamp tree whose roots send up woody 'knees' above the water. Learn why the knees may help the roots breathe, how the tree drops its needles in fall, and how its rot-resistant wood built docks.

name: Eucalyptus and Fire
teaser: Trees that both fight and feed flames.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the complicated relationship between eucalyptus and fire: oily leaves burn fiercely, yet the tree survives and regrows, and some species need fire to release seeds. Understand how this shapes Australian landscapes and fire seasons.

name: Palm Trees: The Diverse Family
teaser: Trees, shrubs, and climbers that are actually related.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the palm family, thousands of species from towering coconuts to climbing rattans and dwarf palms. Learn what makes a palm a palm — a single growing tip and fan or feather leaves — and why they define tropical shores.

name: Bristlecone Pines: The Ancients
teaser: The oldest single trees on Earth.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet bristlecone pines, whose gnarled, half-dead forms hide the oldest single trees alive, nearing 5,000 years. Learn how slow growth on dry mountain slopes, dense resinous wood, and harsh weather let them endure millennia.

name: Yucca: The Desert Candle
teaser: Spiky plants with towers of white flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet yucca, a desert plant with dagger leaves and tall stalks of white bell flowers. Learn how each yucca depends on a single moth species that pollinates it while laying eggs, and how the plant's fibers were woven into rope and sandals.

name: Mesquite: The Desert Tree
teaser: A thorny tree that sweetens and shades the desert.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover mesquite, a thorny tree of the American Southwest that shades the desert and produces sweet pods. Learn how its pods were ground into flour, how its deep roots find water, and how it fixed nitrogen in poor soil.

name: The Green Revolution
teaser: How new seeds and chemistry changed world farming.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Green Revolution
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the Green Revolution of the mid-1900s doubled grain harvests with short, high-yield wheat and rice plus fertilizers. Understand the trade-offs: more food for millions, but heavy water and chemical use, and how its legacy shapes farming today.

name: GMO Crops: The Debate
teaser: What genetic modification really means.

exploreAction.instruction: Understand what genetically modified crops are — genes added or changed in a lab — and why they spark debate. Learn how Bt corn and herbicide-tolerant soy are used, what the science shows about safety, and how labeling rules vary worldwide.

name: Organic Farming: The System
teaser: Growing food without synthetic chemicals.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how organic farming grows food without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers, using compost, rotation, and natural predators instead. Learn what the label actually requires, its benefits and challenges, and how it compares on yields.

name: Cover Crops: Green Manure
teaser: Plants grown to feed the soil itself.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about cover crops — plants like clover, rye, and vetch grown between harvests to protect and feed the soil. Understand how they hold topsoil, add nitrogen, and smother weeds, and why farmers call them green manure.

name: Irrigation: Farming With Water
teaser: How humans have moved water to crops for millennia.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow irrigation from ancient canals and shadufs to modern drip lines and center pivots. Learn how moving water to dry fields multiplied harvests, how salting ruined old soils, and how efficient irrigation is reshaping water use today.

name: Monoculture: The Single Crop
teaser: Why planting one crop is efficient and risky.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore monoculture, planting one crop over vast fields for efficiency. Learn why this invites pests and diseases — the Irish potato famine and banana Panama disease both followed monoculture — and how diversity acts as insurance.

name: Seed Banks: The Backup Copies
teaser: Vaults that preserve the world's seeds.

exploreAction.instruction: Visit the world's seed banks, from the Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Arctic ice to national collections. Learn how seeds are dried, frozen, and stored, why saving crop diversity matters, and how vaults have already restored lost varieties.

name: Plant Breeding: The Long Craft
teaser: How humans have redesigned crops for millennia.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace plant breeding from early farmers saving the best seeds to modern genetics. Learn how selection changed wild grasses into wheat and corn, how cross-breeding created new varieties, and how breeders today use DNA to speed the process.

name: Breeding the Perfect Tomato
teaser: Why tomatoes come in so many shapes and colors.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how breeders shaped the tomato from small yellow fruits into today's range of colors, sizes, and flavors. Learn why heirlooms taste different from hybrids, how breeding for shipping changed texture, and what breeders chase now.

name: Rising Yields: Feeding More
teaser: How farms produce more food on the same land.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how wheat, rice, and corn yields have tripled and quadrupled through breeding, fertilizers, and better farming. Understand what pushed the gains, where growth has slowed, and how the world will feed more people with less land.

name: Native Plants: The Home Team
teaser: Why local plants suit local gardens best.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why gardeners are planting natives — local species adapted to local soil, rain, and wildlife. Learn how native gardens use less water, feed native insects and birds, and support pollinators better than exotic lawns.

name: Lawns and Their Alternatives
teaser: Rethinking the water-hungry grass lawn.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore why lawns soak up water, fertilizer, and mowing time — and what replaces them: clover, native meadow, ground covers, and gardens. Learn how cities are encouraging 'lawn-free' yards that feed bees and save water.

name: Xeriscaping: The Dry Garden
teaser: Landscaping designed to survive drought.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the principles of xeriscaping: choosing drought-tolerant plants, improving soil, mulching, and watering wisely. Understand how this water-wise approach turns dry yards into gardens that thrive with a fraction of the water.

name: Rooftop Gardens: The Sky Gardens
teaser: Green roofs that cool cities and grow food.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover rooftop gardens, from herb patches on apartment buildings to green roofs that insulate and cool. Learn how they absorb rain, reduce heat, and provide fresh food, and how cities from New York to Singapore are embracing them.

name: Victory Gardens: Wartime Harvests
teaser: When whole nations grew food in every spare patch.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the victory gardens of the world wars, when families grew vegetables in yards and parks to free food for soldiers. Learn how governments encouraged them, how much they produced, and how they inspired today's home food movement.

name: Forests and the Climate
teaser: How trees store carbon and shape weather.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of forests and climate
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how forests absorb carbon dioxide, store it in wood and soil, and release water that makes rain. Understand why deforestation accelerates climate change, why old-growth forests matter, and how reforestation is a natural climate tool.

name: The Amazon: River of Trees
teaser: The great rainforest that makes its own weather.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Amazon rainforest
exploreAction.instruction: Enter the Amazon, the largest rainforest on Earth, home to one in ten known species. Learn how the forest recycles its own rainfall, why its trees release water vapor that seeds clouds, and why its loss threatens the planet's climate.

name: The Boreal Forest: The Green Ring
teaser: The vast northern forest circling the globe.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the boreal forest
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the boreal forest, the vast belt of spruce, pine, and birch circling the far north. Learn how it stores enormous carbon in soil and peat, how it has been shaped by fire and caribou, and why it is crucial to the climate.

name: Deforestation: The Vanishing Forest
teaser: Why the world keeps losing trees.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore why forests are cleared — for cattle, soy, palm oil, and timber — and what is lost with them. Learn how much forest has vanished, how deforestation threatens species and climate, and what policies and choices can slow it.

name: Reforestation: Bringing Trees Back
teaser: How forests can regrow after clear-cutting.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how forests regrow after logging — through natural regeneration, replanting, or a mix. Understand why planting the right mix of native trees beats monoculture plantations, and how regrown forests recover wildlife and carbon.

name: Agroforestry: Trees on Farms
teaser: Growing crops and trees together on purpose.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover agroforestry, growing trees alongside crops and livestock. Learn how trees shade coffee, shelter cattle, fix nitrogen, and diversify income, and why this old practice is being rediscovered for climate-friendly farming.

name: Wildfire and Forests
teaser: Why fire is both destroyer and renewer.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how wildfires shape forests: some trees need heat to release seeds, and fire clears undergrowth. Understand why decades of fire suppression built up dangerous fuel, and how managed burns are making forests healthier.

name: Urban Trees: Cooling the City
teaser: Why street trees make cities cooler and calmer.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how street trees cool cities by shading pavement and releasing water vapor, cutting heat and energy bills. Discover how they absorb storm water, filter air, and even lift moods, and why cities are planting more of them.

name: Old-Growth Forests: The Ancient Stands
teaser: Why untouched forests are irreplaceable.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet old-growth forests, never logged, with trees centuries old and complex webs of life. Learn why their deep soils, rotting logs, and canopy habitats can't be recreated by planting, and why protecting them matters so much.

name: Palm Oil: The Controversial Crop
teaser: The most used oil, grown at a cost.
