exploreAction.instruction: Learn why palm oil is in half of packaged foods: the oil palm is astonishingly productive. Understand the cost — rainforests cleared for plantations in Southeast Asia — and how certification and better practices are trying to change that.

name: The Canopy: The Sky Forest
teaser: The sunlit world at the top of the trees.

exploreAction.instruction: Climb into the forest canopy, the sunlit upper layer where most forest life gathers. Learn how researchers study it with ropes and towers, how epiphytes and animals live there, and why it is sometimes called the last frontier.

name: Root Networks: The Forest Web
teaser: How trees may share news underground.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore the underground networks of roots and fungi that link forest trees. Learn what experiments show about trees sharing water, nutrients, and warnings, and how scientists debate how much of the 'wood wide web' is real.

name: Trees Under Drought
teaser: How water shortage stresses and kills trees.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of drought and trees
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how drought kills trees: when soil dries, air bubbles form in water-carrying tubes, blocking flow like a stroke. Understand why hot dry years trigger die-offs, and how forests are responding to a warming world.

name: Shifting Seasons for Plants
teaser: How warming changes when plants bloom.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how warming springs are moving bloom times earlier across the world. Learn why earlier flowers can mismatch with the insects that pollinate them, and how scientists track these shifts with records and satellites.

name: Hardiness Zones: The Plant Map
teaser: The map that tells gardeners what survives winter.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about hardiness zones, the map dividing regions by average winter cold so gardeners know what survives. Understand how zones are shifting as winters warm, and how gardeners are planting new species once thought impossible.

name: The Spice Trade: A World History
teaser: How flavor drove global exploration.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the spice trade
exploreAction.instruction: Follow the spice trade from ancient caravans to the age of sail, when pepper, cinnamon, and cloves were worth fortunes. Learn how the search for spices launched voyages, built empires, and connected continents centuries before globalization.

name: Vanilla: A Global Obsession
teaser: From Aztec courts to every ice cream shop.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace vanilla from Aztec chocolate drinks to the islands where Edmond Albius found the hand-pollination trick. Learn how French colonists carried vines worldwide, and how one boy's discovery made vanilla affordable for everyone.

name: The Potato: Feeding the World
teaser: How one Andean tuber reshaped global diets.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the potato's spread
exploreAction.instruction: Follow the potato from the Andes to Ireland, Russia, and beyond, where it fueled population booms. Learn how it survived poor soils, fed armies and laborers, and how its dependence on a single variety brought the Great Famine.

name: The Tomato: From Fear to Fame
teaser: How a New World fruit conquered world cuisine.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the tomato's rise
exploreAction.instruction: Trace the tomato's rocky rise: feared in Europe, adored in Italy, and now eaten on every continent. Learn how it traveled from Mexico to Spain, how it became central to Italian cooking, and how it conquered the world in three centuries.

name: Chocolate: From Bean to Bar
teaser: How a bitter drink became a global sweet.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow chocolate from cacao beans used as currency in Mesoamerica to the sweet bars of today. Learn how Europeans added sugar, how the Industrial Revolution made it affordable, and how modern chocolate is made from bean to bar.

name: Coffee: The History of a Brew
teaser: How a drink from Ethiopia conquered the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace coffee from Sufi monasteries in Yemen to the coffeehouses of Europe and the plantations of the tropics. Learn how coffee fueled revolutions, built empires, and created a global economy worth billions.

name: Tea: The Global Leaf
teaser: From Chinese emperors to British tea time.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow tea from ancient China through Japan, India, and the British Empire. Learn how tea taxes sparked a revolution in America, how clipper ships raced the harvest, and how one leaf became the world's second-favorite drink.

name: Sugar: The Sweet History
teaser: How a luxury spice became a daily staple.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace sugar from a rare luxury to the world's most common sweetener. Learn how the sugar trade drove slavery and colonies, how sugar shaped diets and industry, and how cheap sweetness transformed the way the world eats.

name: The Banana: History of a Clone
teaser: How one fruit went global and nearly vanished.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the banana from Southeast Asia across oceans to every supermarket. Learn how the Gros Michel variety built a global trade and how disease destroyed it, forcing the switch to today's Cavendish — a switch now happening again.

name: The Apple: A Long History
teaser: From wild forests to the world's orchards.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace the apple from wild forests of Central Asia along trade routes, where it became a thousand varieties. Learn how grafting kept favorites alive, how settlers carried apples across oceans, and how the apple became a global fruit.

name: Citrus: The Sour Origins
teaser: How bitter fruits became sweet and global.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow citrus from sour wild ancestors in Southeast Asia to the oranges, lemons, and limes of today. Learn how trade routes spread them, how sailors' scurvy made citrus famous, and how most varieties are ancient hybrids.

name: Corn: The American Journey
teaser: How a grass became the world's most grown grain.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace corn from its teosinte ancestor, bred by Indigenous Americans, to fields on every continent. Learn how corn fed civilizations, traveled the world after 1492, and now appears in food, fuel, and countless products.

name: Rice: The Ancient Staple
teaser: How one grass fed the great civilizations of Asia.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow rice from ancient paddies in Asia to the staple of half the world. Learn how wet-rice farming shaped landscapes and societies, how it spread to every continent, and why it remains the most important food grain.

name: Wheat: The History of the Staff
teaser: How a wild grass built the modern world.

exploreAction.instruction: Trace wheat from wild grasses in the Fertile Crescent to the vast fields of today. Learn how farming wheat changed human society, how it spread across the world, and how modern breeding doubled its yields.

name: The Herb Garden: An Ancient Plot
teaser: Why every culture grew a plot of herbs.

exploreAction.instruction: Visit the herb garden, grown by Egyptians, Romans, monks, and homemakers for medicine, flavor, and scent. Learn how monastery gardens preserved herb knowledge, how herbs were used for everything from headaches to embalming, and how they shape gardens today.

name: Blue Roses: The Impossible Flower
teaser: Why true blue roses do not exist.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why true blue roses don't exist — roses lack the pigment to make blue. Discover how scientists engineered 'blue' roses by adding a pansy gene, and why the blue rose remains a symbol of the impossible in folklore.

name: The Black Tulip: The Myth
teaser: A flower made famous by a novel.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the black tulip
exploreAction.instruction: Uncover the truth behind the black tulip, made famous by Alexandre Dumas's novel. Learn why a truly black tulip cannot exist, how very dark purple varieties mimic it, and how the myth inspired real breeding quests.

name: Edelweiss: The Alpine Star
teaser: A woolly flower of high mountain crags.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet edelweiss, the woolly white flower that grows high in the Alps, treasured as a badge of courage. Learn how its fuzzy hairs protect it from cold and sun, why climbers risked their lives to pick it, and how it became a national symbol.

name: Orchid Keikis: The Baby Plants
teaser: How some orchids grow their own plantlets.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about keikis, baby orchids that sprout along flower stems of some species. Understand how to recognize and root them, why some orchids produce them naturally, and how growers use them to multiply prized plants.

name: The Language of Flowers
teaser: How Victorians spoke in bouquets.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore floriography, the Victorian code where flowers sent messages — roses for love, yellow roses for jealousy, ivy for fidelity. Learn how bouquets were arranged to spell feelings, and how the language was compiled into dictionaries.

name: Flower Colors Beyond Sight
teaser: How bees see flowers we can't.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover that flowers show colors we cannot see — ultraviolet patterns invisible to humans but vivid to bees. Learn how these 'nectar guides' point pollinators to the reward, and how scientists photograph flowers in UV.

name: Flower Fragrance: The Chemistry
teaser: Why flowers smell the way they do.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how flowers produce scent: volatile oils released to attract pollinators or warn of pests. Discover why some flowers smell sweet, some foul, and why fragrance changes with day and night — and how chemists capture it in perfume.

name: Pollination Syndromes
teaser: How flower shapes match their pollinators.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how flower shapes, colors, and scents match specific pollinators — tube flowers for hummingbirds, dull smelly blooms for flies, white night flowers for moths. Understand how these matched pairs evolved together.

name: Hummingbird Flowers
teaser: Why some flowers are built for hovering birds.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet flowers adapted for hummingbirds: red or orange, tubular, with nectar deep inside. Learn why red appeals to birds but not bees, how the flower's shape matches the bird's bill, and how both evolved together.

name: Moth Flowers: Night Bloomers
teaser: Flowers that open for the night shift.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover flowers that bloom white and fragrant at dusk to attract night-flying moths. Learn how their long tubes match moth tongues, how they open as the sun sets, and how gardeners plant them for evening scent.

name: Bee Flowers: The Bee's Garden
teaser: What bees see and love in flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what makes a flower bee-friendly: blue and purple colors, UV nectar guides, and landing platforms. Understand how bee vision differs from ours, and why planting bee flowers supports the insects that pollinate our food.

name: Beetle Flowers: The Ancient Pollinators
teaser: The first insects to visit flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet beetle-pollinated flowers like magnolias, which evolved before bees. Learn how large sturdy flowers with strong scents cater to clumsy beetles, and how this ancient partnership predates most other pollination.

name: Wind-Pollinated Plants
teaser: How grasses and trees mate without insects.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how grasses, pines, and oaks pollinate by wind, releasing clouds of pollen. Learn why their flowers are small and plain, why their pollen triggers allergies, and how they became the dominant plants of open landscapes.

name: Self-Pollination: The Shortcut
teaser: Why some plants pollinate themselves.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why some plants pollinate themselves — a reliable shortcut when pollinators are scarce. Discover how peas and tomatoes self-pollinate, why this reduces genetic variety, and how plants balance selfing with cross-pollination.

name: Hybrid Flowers: The Breeders' Art
teaser: How new flower colors and shapes are created.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how breeders create hybrid flowers by crossing varieties — new colors, double petals, and bigger blooms. Understand how crossing works, how hybrid vigor helps, and how famous flowers like modern roses came from centuries of crosses.

name: Fertilizer: Plant Food
teaser: The three numbers on every bag explained.

exploreAction.instruction: Decode fertilizer labels: the N-P-K numbers for nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Learn what each nutrient does — leafy growth, roots and blooms, and overall health — and how over-fertilizing can burn plants.

name: Nitrogen: The Growth Engine
teaser: Why plants need more nitrogen than anything.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why nitrogen is the nutrient plants need most — it builds the proteins and DNA of every cell. Discover how plants get it from soil, how legumes fix it from air, and why nitrogen limits growth everywhere.

name: Phosphorus: Roots and Blooms
teaser: The nutrient behind energy, roots, and flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet phosphorus, the nutrient that powers plant energy, root growth, and flowering. Learn why blooms and fruits demand it, how plants move it slowly, and why deficiency shows as purple leaves and weak roots.

name: Potassium: The Health Mineral
teaser: The nutrient that toughens plants against stress.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how potassium keeps plants healthy: it regulates water, builds strong stems, and helps plants resist drought and disease. Discover why potassium-starved plants yellow at the edges and wilt easily.

name: Micronutrients: The Tiny Essentials
teaser: The trace minerals plants cannot live without.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the micronutrients — iron, zinc, manganese, and others — needed in tiny amounts but vital to plant health. Learn how deficiency shows in yellowing leaves and poor growth, and why soil chemistry controls their availability.

name: Soil pH: The Acidity Scale
teaser: Why soil acidity controls what plants can eat.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how soil pH — acidity or alkalinity — controls whether plants can absorb nutrients. Discover why blueberries need acid soil, why lime sweetens fields, and how pH determines what grows where.

name: Watering Plants: The Right Way
teaser: Why most houseplants die of kindness.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to water plants properly: check soil before pouring, water deeply and less often, and match schedule to season. Understand why overwatering drowns roots, and why droopy leaves can mean too much or too little.

name: Repotting: The Plant Upgrade
teaser: When and how to move a plant to a bigger pot.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn when to repot: roots circling the bottom, slow growth, or soil exhausted. Understand how to choose a slightly larger pot, loosen the root ball, and water in — and why skipping repotting eventually starves the plant.

name: Light for Houseplants
teaser: Reading the sun for indoor plants.

exploreAction.targetName: how to match plants to light
exploreAction.instruction: Learn to read light in a home: bright, indirect, low, and the difference between a sunny south window and a dim corner. Understand why light is the number one limit on indoor plants, and how to match plants to their spot.

name: Humidity for Houseplants
teaser: Why tropical plants crave moist air.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why tropical houseplants like ferns and calatheas suffer in dry indoor air. Discover how to raise humidity with trays, grouping, or misting — and why brown leaf tips are often a humidity problem.

name: Propagation: Growing From Cuttings
teaser: How a snipped stem becomes a new plant.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow new plants from cuttings: snip a stem, remove lower leaves, and root it in water or soil. Understand why some plants root easily and others struggle, and how hormones help stubborn cuttings.

name: Leaf Cuttings: Plants From a Leaf
teaser: How a single leaf can become a whole plant.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow from leaf cuttings
exploreAction.instruction: Discover how plants like African violets, begonias, and jade grow from a single leaf. Learn where to cut, how to keep the leaf humid, and how plantlets form along the edge — nature's most efficient cloning.

name: Dividing Plants: More From One
teaser: Splitting clumps to multiply perennials.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to divide clumping perennials — dig, split, and replant — to get more plants for free. Understand when to divide, how to keep roots moist, and why division also revives tired plants.

name: Bulbs, Corms, and Tubers
teaser: Underground storage that becomes flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the difference between bulbs, corms, and tubers — underground storage organs that hold next season's growth. Discover how tulips, gladioli, and potatoes each store energy differently, and how gardeners plant and lift them.

name: Perennials vs Annuals
teaser: Plants that return vs plants that finish.

exploreAction.instruction: Understand the two great plant life strategies: annuals complete their lives in one season, perennials return year after year. Learn how gardens mix them for color, and why the same species can act differently in different climates.

name: Blueberries: The Acid Bush
teaser: Berries that demand sour soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the blueberry, a bush that grows only in acidic soil and pays back with antioxidant-packed berries. Learn how wild blueberries differ from cultivated ones, how bees pollinate the bell flowers, and why the berries are blue only on the outside.

name: Raspberries: The Bramble Fruit
teaser: Delicate berries on thorny canes.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover raspberries, the delicate fruits of thorny bramble canes, each made of dozens of tiny drupelets. Learn how canes fruit in their second year, how the plant spreads by roots, and why ripe raspberries slip off their core.

name: Blackberries: The Wild Bramble
teaser: Sweet berries from a plant people love and curse.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the blackberry, a vigorous bramble that fills hedgerows with sweet berries — and thorns. Learn how it spreads ruthlessly, how its berries differ from raspberries, and why foragers watch for the dark, plump ones.

name: Strawberry Runners: The Cloning Vines
teaser: How strawberries send out baby plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how strawberry plants reproduce by runners — long stems that root at the tip to form new plants. Understand how farmers use runners to fill fields, and how this cloning keeps every plant identical.

name: Cherries: Sweet and Sour
teaser: Two kinds of cherry for two kinds of cooking.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the two cherries: sweet cherries for eating fresh, sour cherries for pies and preserves. Learn how both grow on trees that need cold winters, how the stones protect the seed, and why cherry trees blossom in a spring show.

name: Plums: The Stone Fruit
teaser: Sweet fruit around a hard pit.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover plums, the round stone fruits that ripen in summer, from small wild sloes to big sweet varieties. Learn how plums are dried into prunes, how they hybridize with cherries, and why they fruit so heavily some years.

name: Apricots: The Soft Stone
teaser: Delicate orange fruit from Central Asia.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the apricot, a delicate orange stone fruit first grown in Central Asia thousands of years ago. Learn why it dries so well into sweet dried fruit, how the kernel tastes like almond, and why it ripens quickly on the tree.

name: Peaches: The Fuzzy Fruit
teaser: A stone fruit wrapped in fuzz.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the peach, a stone fruit whose fuzz evolved to deter insects. Learn how nectarines are smooth-skinned peaches, how peach trees spread from China along trade routes, and why the fruit is best picked tree-ripe.

name: Pears: The Gritty Fruit
teaser: Why pears feel sandy in the mouth.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the pear, a fruit whose flesh has gritty cells — stone cells that give it texture. Learn why pears are picked hard and ripen off the tree, how they were bred into the melting 'butter' pears, and why they pair with cheese.

name: Watermelon: The Giant Berry
teaser: A fruit that is technically a huge berry.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn that the watermelon is botanically a berry — a giant one with a hard rind. Discover how its sweetness was bred from bitter wild ancestors in Africa, how seedless ones are made, and why it is mostly water.

name: Melons: The Sweet Cucurbits
teaser: Cantaloupes, honeydews, and their wild cousins.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet melons — cantaloupe, honeydew, and muskmelon — sweet members of the squash family. Learn how they came from Africa and Asia, how the netted rind of cantaloupe forms, and how to tell when a melon is ripe.

name: Cucumber: The Cool Fruit
teaser: A fruit eaten as a vegetable.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why the cucumber, botanically a fruit, is eaten as a vegetable. Discover how its cool watery flesh keeps it crisp, how bitter wild relatives were tamed, and how pickling transforms it into gherkins.

name: Pumpkins: The Legendary Squash
teaser: The giant orange squash of autumn.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the pumpkin, a New World squash grown for food, pie, and jack-o'-lanterns. Learn how giant pumpkins are bred to weigh over a ton, how the flowers become fruit, and why pumpkins store so well through winter.

name: Zucchini: The Fast Squash
teaser: A squash that fruits at astonishing speed.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover zucchini, a summer squash famous for appearing overnight. Learn how the plant fruits continuously, why it grows so fast, and how its flowers are eaten stuffed or fried in many cuisines.

name: Eggplant: The Purple Fruit
teaser: A glossy fruit with a vegetable reputation.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the eggplant, a glossy purple fruit eaten as a vegetable, from Asia originally. Learn why it was once called mad apple, how its spongy flesh soaks up flavor, and how white varieties gave it its name.

name: The Fastest Growing Plants
teaser: Which plants win the growth race.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the fastest growers on Earth: bamboo can rise nearly a meter a day, kelp grows half a meter daily, and duckweed doubles overnight. Learn how they pour energy into growth and what limits even the fastest.

name: The Slowest Growing Plants
teaser: Plants that take centuries to change.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover plants that grow at a snail's pace: saguaro cacti add centimeters a year, and some lichens grow a millimeter a century. Learn why harsh conditions force slowness, and how slow growth can mean great age.

name: The World's Largest Flowers
teaser: Blooms the size of tires.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the giants: rafflesia's meter-wide bloom and the titan arum's towering spike. Learn how these record flowers grow from parasites or huge underground tubers, and why they bloom so rarely and briefly.

name: The World's Smallest Flowers
teaser: Tiny blooms measured in millimeters.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the world's tiniest flowers: duckweed's pinhead blooms and Wolffia's barely visible ones. Learn why they are so small, how they reproduce so fast, and why size is a strategy, not a limitation.

name: Tallest Flower Spike
teaser: A bloom spike taller than a house.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the titan arum and giant echium, whose flower spikes tower meters high. Learn why plants invest so much energy in one massive bloom, and how these spikes attract pollinators from far away.

name: The Strangler Fig: The Killer Tree
teaser: A tree that starts on another tree and smothers it.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the strangler fig, which sprouts high in another tree's crown, sends roots down its host, and eventually surrounds and strangles it. Learn how this slow takeover works, why the fig survives the fall, and how it becomes a hollow giant.

name: Parasitic Plants: The Borrowers
teaser: Plants that steal from their neighbors.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet parasitic plants like dodder, broomrape, and mistletoe, which steal water and nutrients from other plants. Learn how some lost their leaves and chlorophyll entirely, and how mistletoe became a holiday tradition.

name: Mistletoe: The Hanging Parasite
teaser: The kissing plant that lives on tree branches.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover mistletoe, a plant that grows on tree branches, sinking roots into the host for water. Learn how birds spread its sticky seeds, why it stays green in winter, and how it became the kiss-under-the-doorway tradition.

name: Dodder: The Vampire Vine
teaser: A yellow vine with no leaves that steals from hosts.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet dodder, a yellow thread-like vine that has no leaves or chlorophyll. Learn how its seedling finds a host, taps in, and drains it, and how scientists study dodder's chemical sensing to find its victims.

name: Hydnora: The Underground Flower
teaser: A parasitic flower that blooms from desert soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet hydnora, a parasitic plant that lives underground on acacia roots and bursts through desert soil only to bloom — smelling of dung to attract beetles. Learn how it survives years without light, and how local people eat its fruit.

name: Night-Blooming Cereus
teaser: A cactus flower that opens once, at night.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the night-blooming cereus
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the night-blooming cereus, whose huge white flower opens after dark and closes by morning, blooming only once a year. Learn why night blooming suits its moth pollinators, and why owners camp out to watch it open.

name: Saguaro Blooms: Night Flowers
teaser: A giant cactus with crown of white flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the saguaro cactus flowers each spring, its white blooms opening at night for bats and closing by afternoon. Discover how a saguaro may hold hundreds of flowers, and how each bloom lasts less than a day.

name: Ice Plants: The Sparkling Succulents
teaser: Succulents that look frosted with crystals.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet ice plants, low succulents whose leaves glisten with bladder cells that look like frost. Learn how they cover dry slopes with bright flowers, how they store water, and why some have become invasive on coasts.

name: Living Stones: The Pebble Plants
teaser: Succulents that disguise themselves as rocks.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet living stones, desert succulents that mimic the pebbles around them to avoid being eaten. Learn how two fleshy leaves hold their water, how the plant splits to reveal a flower, and how collectors treasure their patterns.

name: Cochineal: The Cactus Bug
teaser: The insect that made a famous red dye on cactus.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cochineal insects that feed on prickly pear cacti were crushed to make carmine, a brilliant red dye prized for centuries. Discover how the Aztecs and Spanish used it, and how it is still used in food and cosmetics today.

name: Foraging: Wild Food
teaser: Eating the weeds and berries around us.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the basics of foraging: identifying wild edibles like dandelion, chickweed, and blackberries. Understand why positive identification is essential, how to harvest sustainably, and how foragers are reviving an ancient skill.

name: Mushrooms: Not Plants
teaser: The forest's hidden fungal network.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why mushrooms are fungi, not plants — they don't photosynthesize and are more related to animals. Discover how the mushroom is just the fruit of a vast underground web, and how fungi feed the forest.

name: Truffles: Underground Treasure
teaser: Fungi that grow below ground and cost a fortune.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet truffles, fungi that grow underground near tree roots and are hunted with pigs or dogs. Learn why their scent is so prized, how the fungus partners with trees, and why a good truffle can sell for thousands.

name: Harvesting Saffron
teaser: The dawn ritual behind the world's priciest spice.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow a saffron harvest: workers pick purple crocus flowers at dawn before they wilt, then pluck the three red stigmas by hand. Learn why the process takes 40 hours of labor per kilogram and why machines can't replace it.

name: Capers: The Pickled Buds
teaser: A condiment that is simply unopened flower buds.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover capers, the unopened flower buds of a Mediterranean shrub, pickled in brine or salt. Learn why they must be picked by hand before blooming, how they add salty tang to sauces, and how the bush thrives in rocky soil.

name: Mustard: From Seed to Squeeze
teaser: How a tiny seed becomes a fiery condiment.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how mustard seeds become the condiment: grinding them releases enzymes that create the sharp heat. Discover how the seed's chemistry works, how different seeds make yellow, brown, and Dijon mustards, and how the plant grows like a weed.

name: Horseradish: The Sharp Root
teaser: A root whose heat disappears when cooked.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet horseradish, a root whose sharp heat is released only when grated fresh — cooking destroys it. Learn how the same chemistry as mustard works, why it clears sinuses, and how the plant spreads aggressively.

name: Wasabi: The Impostor
teaser: Why most 'wasabi' is actually horseradish.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why most wasabi served with sushi is dyed horseradish: real wasabi comes from a slow-growing Japanese root that is expensive and fades quickly. Discover how real wasabi is grated fresh and why it is so prized.

name: Seaweed: The Ocean Vegetable
teaser: Algae eaten across the world's coasts.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet edible seaweeds — nori, kombu, and wakame — algae farmed and eaten across Asia for centuries. Learn how they absorb minerals from seawater, how nori wraps sushi, and why seaweed farming needs no fresh water or fertilizer.

name: Nori: The Sushi Sheets
teaser: How red algae becomes the paper of sushi.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover nori, the dried seaweed sheets that wrap sushi. Learn how red algae are harvested, washed, and pressed into thin sheets, and how modern farming in the sea made nori plentiful and affordable.

name: Agar: The Seaweed Gel
teaser: A jelly made from algae that sets without chilling.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet agar, a gel made from red seaweed that sets at room temperature and melts only when heated. Learn how it is used in food, petri dishes, and desserts, and how it was discovered by accident in a Japanese kitchen.

name: Mint Tea: The Calming Cup
teaser: Why mint tea settles the stomach.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why mint tea has been drunk after meals for centuries: the menthol in mint relaxes the digestive tract. Discover how to brew fresh or dried mint, and how mint spread from the Mediterranean to every garden.

name: Ginger for Nausea
teaser: The root that calms queasy stomachs.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how ginger, a tropical rhizome, has been used for thousands of years to ease nausea. Discover what studies say about its effect on motion sickness and morning sickness, and how its pungent compounds work.

name: Echinacea: The Cold Remedy
teaser: The coneflower that filled the cold aisle.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore echinacea's journey from Native American remedy to the best-selling cold supplement. Learn what the studies actually show, how the root and flower differ, and why its reputation persists despite mixed evidence.

name: Elderberry: The Dark Berry
teaser: A berry long used to ward off winter illness.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet elderberry, the dark berry of the elder tree, used in syrups and remedies for centuries. Learn why the raw berries and bark are toxic and must be cooked, and how elderberry syrup became a home remedy staple.

name: Chilies Around the World
teaser: How one fruit became the world's favorite heat.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the chili around the planet: from the Americas to Asia, Africa, and Europe, where it became essential to Thai curries, Indian pickles, Korean gochujang, and Hungarian paprika. Learn why it spread so fast after 1492.

name: Paprika: The Hungarian Spice
teaser: How a sweet pepper became a nation's emblem.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover paprika, the ground spice from dried sweet peppers that became Hungary's national treasure. Learn how the pepper arrived from the Americas, how Hungarians bred sweeter varieties, and how paprika colors and flavors goulash.

name: Five-Spice: The Chinese Blend
teaser: The classic mix behind Chinese cooking.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet five-spice, the Chinese blend of star anise, cloves, cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, and fennel. Learn how each spice contributes sweet, warm, numbing, and aromatic notes, and how the blend defines a cuisine.

name: Curry Leaves: The Fragrant Leaf
teaser: The leaf that perfumes South Indian cooking.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the curry leaf tree, whose fragrant leaves are fried in oil to perfume South Indian cooking. Learn why the leaves are used fresh, not dried, how the tree grows easily in warm gardens, and why they are not 'curry powder'.

name: Lemongrass: The Citrus Herb
teaser: A grass that tastes of lemon.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover lemongrass, a tropical grass whose stalks carry a fresh lemon scent. Learn how it flavors soups and teas across Southeast Asia, how its oils repel insects, and how it grows in clumps from the tropics to warm windowsills.

name: Galangal: The Ginger Cousin
teaser: A pungent rhizome behind Thai cooking.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet galangal, a rhizome closely related to ginger that is essential to Thai curries and soups. Learn how its sharp, piney flavor differs from ginger, how it grows, and why it is used fresh in Southeast Asian kitchens.

name: Kaffir Lime Leaves
teaser: The double-lobed leaves that perfume Thai food.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of kaffir lime leaves
exploreAction.instruction: Meet kaffir lime leaves, the glossy double-lobed leaves used fresh in Thai cooking for their intense citrus aroma. Learn why they are torn, not chopped, how the tree's bumpy fruit is used for zest, and why the leaves don't dry well.

name: Coriander: Seed and Leaf
teaser: One plant, two very different flavors.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover coriander, the plant that gives us cilantro leaves and coriander seeds — two completely different flavors. Learn why people either love or hate the leaf, how the seed is used in spice blends, and how both traveled the world.

name: Cardamom: The Green Pods
teaser: A spice of tiny pods with a huge price.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet cardamom, the green pods of a ginger-family plant, among the world's most expensive spices. Learn why it is hand-harvested in the monsoon hills of India and Guatemala, and how it perfumes chai, rice, and pastries.

name: Cloves: The Dried Buds
teaser: A spice that is simply dried flower buds.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover cloves, the dried flower buds of an Indonesian tree, shaped like little nails — 'clavus' means nail. Learn how the buds are picked before they open, why the Spice Islands guarded them, and how clove oil numbs toothaches.

name: Star Anise: The Eight-Point Spice
teaser: A fruit shaped like a star with a licorice flavor.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet star anise, a spice shaped like an eight-pointed star, harvested from a small evergreen tree. Learn how its licorice flavor comes from the same compound as anise seed, and how it became essential to Chinese cooking and cough medicines.

name: Fennel: Seed and Bulb
teaser: A plant with a licorice flavor in every part.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet fennel, whose bulb, stalks, and seeds all carry a mild licorice flavor. Learn how the seeds aid digestion after meals, how the bulb is eaten raw in salads, and how wild fennel grows along Mediterranean roads.

name: Dill: The Pickle Herb
teaser: The feathery herb that guards pickle jars.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover dill, the feathery herb whose seeds and leaves season pickles, salmon, and soups. Learn why its name comes from an old Norse word for lull — it was used to soothe babies — and how it self-seeds in gardens.

name: Cilantro: Love It or Hate It
teaser: The genetic twist behind a polarizing herb.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why cilantro tastes like soap to some people: a genetic variant makes them sensitive to its aldehydes. Discover how the same compounds give the leaf its fresh aroma to others, and why the debate is in our genes.

name: Basil Around the World
teaser: From sweet Genovese to Thai holy basil.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour basil's many faces: sweet basil for pesto, Thai basil with anise notes, holy basil for teas, and lemon basil. Learn how each variety was bred in different regions and how they differ in flavor, leaf shape, and use.

name: Cacao Fermentation
teaser: The step that turns bitter beans into chocolate.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why cacao beans are fermented for days before drying: fermentation develops the chocolate flavor and kills the bitter raw bean. Discover how the beans are piled, turned, and how microbes transform them.

name: Coffee Roasting: The Transformation
teaser: How green beans become brown and fragrant.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow coffee from green beans to roast: heat drives off water, triggers browning reactions, and creates hundreds of aroma compounds. Learn why light roasts keep more acidity and dark roasts taste richer, and how roasters control it all.

name: Tea Oxidation: Green to Black
teaser: The processing step that changes tea's color.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the same tea leaf becomes green, black, or oolong depending on oxidation — the time leaves are bruised and exposed to air. Discover how enzymes darken the leaf and deepen flavor, and how each tradition stops the process at a different point.

name: Wine: The Grape's Ferment
teaser: How yeast turns grape sugar into wine.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how wine is made: grapes are crushed, yeast ferments their sugar into alcohol, and the wine ages. Discover why grape variety, soil, and climate — terroir — matter, and how one fruit became thousands of wines.

name: Beer: The Grain Brew
teaser: How barley becomes the world's oldest drink.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow beer from barley: the grain is malted, mashed, boiled with hops, and fermented by yeast. Learn how each step builds flavor and alcohol, how hops preserve and bitter, and why beer is among humanity's oldest crafts.

name: Sake: The Rice Brew
teaser: A Japanese drink made by fermenting rice.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover sake, the Japanese brew made from fermented rice. Learn how a mold called koji breaks down rice starch into sugar for yeast, how water quality shapes the flavor, and why sake is served warm or chilled.

name: Kombucha: The Fermented Tea
teaser: A fizzy tea brewed by a living scoby.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet kombucha, tea fermented by a scoby — a colony of yeast and bacteria — into a tangy fizzy drink. Learn how the scoby grows, what the fermentation does, and why the ancient drink became a modern favorite.

name: Olive Oil: The First Press
teaser: How olives become liquid gold.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how olive oil is made: olives are crushed and pressed, and the oil is separated from the water and pulp. Discover why 'extra virgin' means first cold press with no chemicals, and how the oil's quality is judged.

name: Maple Sugar: Beyond Syrup
teaser: How maple sap becomes sugar and candy.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how maple sap is boiled far past syrup to make maple sugar and candy. Discover how Native peoples first made maple sugar, how much sap a single batch needs, and why the season is a short window each spring.

name: Honey: The Flower's Gift
teaser: How bees turn flower nectar into honey.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how honey begins as flower nectar, gathered by bees and concentrated into honey by evaporation. Discover how different flowers make different honey, why honey never spoils, and how bees store it to feed the colony.

name: Cooking With Flowers
teaser: Edible blooms from salads to syrups.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the flowers we eat: nasturtiums and pansies in salads, elderflowers in fizz, rose petals in jam, and squash blossoms fried. Learn which blooms are safe, how to use them, and how flowers have flavored food for centuries.

name: Lavender in Food
teaser: A floral herb from shortbread to ice cream.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how lavender's floral flavor is used in shortbread, honey, and ice cream. Learn why culinary lavender must be the right variety, why a little goes a long way, and how the Provence region made it famous.

name: Rose Water: The Fragrant Essence
teaser: A distilled perfume used in food.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet rose water, made by distilling rose petals, used to perfume sweets from the Middle East to India. Learn how it is made, why it flavors baklava and lassi, and how it was once used to wash hands at feasts.

name: Orange Blossom Water
teaser: The citrus flower essence of Mediterranean baking.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of orange blossom water
exploreAction.instruction: Discover orange blossom water, distilled from bitter-orange flowers, a signature of North African and Middle Eastern baking. Learn how it perfumes pastries and sweets, how the flowers are harvested, and why it is used in celebrations.

name: Vanilla Extract: The Baker's Bottle
teaser: How vanilla pods become the brown bottle.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how vanilla extract is made: vanilla pods are chopped and steeped in alcohol to draw out the flavor. Discover why real extract differs from imitation, how the pods are graded, and why the vanilla orchid is so labor-intensive.

name: Keukenhof: The Tulip Garden
teaser: The world's most famous flower garden.

exploreAction.instruction: Visit Keukenhof in the Netherlands, the world's most famous spring garden, planted with millions of tulips. Learn how Dutch flower growers created it, how the gardens are replanted each year, and how the tulip became a national icon.

name: The Amsterdam Flower Market
teaser: A floating market of flowers and bulbs.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the Amsterdam flower market, built on houseboats along a canal, selling bulbs and blooms for centuries. Learn how Dutch flower auctions work, how cut flowers are flown worldwide, and why the market endures.

name: Flower Carpets: The Bloom Tapestry
teaser: Huge patterns built from begonias.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cities like Brussels build giant carpets from millions of begonia flowers. Discover how the patterns are designed, how quickly volunteers lay them, and why begonias are chosen for their color and durability.

name: Hanami: Viewing the Cherry
teaser: Japan's spring tradition of sitting under blossoms.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about hanami, Japan's tradition of gathering under cherry blossoms to picnic and watch the short-lived bloom. Discover how the custom began with plum viewing among poets, and how the forecast of bloom dates is a national event.

name: Ikebana: The Art of Arrangement
teaser: The Japanese discipline of flower arranging.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet ikebana, the Japanese art of flower arrangement that treats stems, space, and asymmetry as carefully as the blooms. Learn how it began in temples, how each school teaches its style, and why emptiness is part of the design.

name: Garlands and Leis: The Flower Necklaces
teaser: Why flowers are strung into welcome and honor.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore how flowers are strung into garlands across cultures — Hawaiian leis, Indian marigold strings, and European laurel wreaths. Learn how each tradition uses local blooms and why giving flowers is a universal gesture.

name: Arranging Cut Flowers
teaser: How to make bouquets last.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the basics of arranging cut flowers: cut stems at an angle, strip lower leaves, and change water daily. Discover why flower food works, how to revive drooping stems, and how to design a pleasing bouquet.

name: Dried Flowers: The Long Bloom
teaser: Keeping flowers past their season.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to dry flowers by hanging, pressing, or using silica gel. Discover why some flowers hold color and shape better than others, and how dried blooms are used in wreaths, frames, and arrangements.

name: Pressed Flowers: Flat Art
teaser: The art of flattening blooms into keepsakes.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover flower pressing, the craft of flattening flowers between pages until they dry. Learn which flowers press best, how pressing preserves color, and how Victorians used pressed flowers in albums and love letters.

name: Planting Bulbs for Spring
teaser: The autumn job that rewards in spring.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why spring bulbs are planted in autumn: they need cold to root and bloom. Discover how deep to plant, how to arrange bulbs for natural drifts, and how to plant in layers for a long season of blooms.

name: Moss Lawns: The Soft Alternative
teaser: A green carpet that needs no mowing.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the moss lawn, a soft green carpet that needs no mowing, watering, or fertilizer. Learn where moss thrives — shade and acid soil — and how gardeners establish and care for it.

name: Garden Design Basics
teaser: Arranging plants with purpose and beauty.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the basics of garden design: consider light, soil, and views; plan layers of height and season; and repeat shapes and colors for harmony. Understand how paths, borders, and focal points structure a garden.

name: Cottage Gardens: The Overflow
teaser: The relaxed, packed garden style.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the cottage garden, a romantic style of dense, relaxed planting with flowers, herbs, and vegetables tumbling together. Learn how it began with working homes, and how to mix color, height, and self-seeders for the look.

name: Japanese Gardens: Plants and Calm
teaser: Gardens designed as quiet landscapes.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore Japanese gardens, where maples, pines, moss, and stones are arranged with care. Learn how borrowed scenery, pruning clouds, and the sound of water create calm, and how plants are shaped over decades.

name: Zen Gardens: Raked Stone
teaser: Gardens of gravel meant for meditation.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the zen garden, a dry landscape of raked gravel and placed stones meant for meditation. Learn how the raked lines imitate water, how the stones are arranged in balance, and how these gardens began in Japanese temples.

name: Mahogany: The Furniture Wood
teaser: A rich red wood that built fine furniture.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet mahogany, a tropical hardwood prized for its rich red color, straight grain, and stability. Learn how it built fine furniture and ships, how overharvesting emptied forests, and how sustainable plantations now supply it.

name: Oak Barrels: The Aging Wood
teaser: How oak wood flavors wine and whiskey.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how oak barrels age and flavor wine, whiskey, and beer: the wood adds vanilla, spice, and color as the liquid breathes. Discover how toasting the barrel deepens flavor, and why new oak is prized by distillers.

name: Balsa: The Lightest Wood
teaser: A wood so light it floats like cork.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet balsa, among the lightest woods on Earth, yet surprisingly strong for its weight. Learn how it is grown fast in Ecuador, how it built model planes and rafts, and how it is used in wind turbine blades.

name: Ebony: The Black Wood
teaser: A dense black wood carved into treasures.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover ebony, a dense, heavy tropical wood so dark it is nearly black. Learn why it is used for piano keys, chess pieces, and carvings, how slow it grows, and why overharvesting has made it rare and protected.

name: Rosewood: The Aromatic Tonewood
teaser: A fragrant wood behind fine guitars.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet rosewood, a tropical hardwood with a sweet scent used for guitar bodies and fretboards. Learn how its density shapes tone, why Brazilian rosewood became endangered, and how luthiers seek sustainable alternatives.

name: Maple: The Tonewood
teaser: A bright wood behind violins and drum shells.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of maple in music
exploreAction.instruction: Learn why maple is prized in music: its dense, bright tone backs violins and builds drum shells and guitar necks. Discover how the figured flame maple grain is revealed in finishing, and why Stradivarius used it.

name: Spruce: The Soundboard Wood
teaser: The wood that gives instruments their voice.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why spruce, with its even grain and high strength-to-weight ratio, tops violins and pianos. Learn how slow-grown Alpine spruce is favored, how the wood is quarter-sawn, and how it carries sound across a concert hall.

name: Tree Sap: The Sticky Lifeblood
teaser: What sap is and what we make from it.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the difference between sap, which feeds the tree, and resin, which defends it. Discover what we make from each — maple syrup from sap, turpentine and rubber from resin, and how tapping works without killing the tree.

name: Tapping Rubber: The Morning Cut
teaser: How latex is collected from rubber trees.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow a rubber tapper's morning: a thin diagonal cut, a cup to catch dripping latex, and months before the tree is tapped again. Learn how the cuts heal, how latex is coagulated into sheets, and how tappers read the tree's yield.

name: Resin and Turpentine
teaser: How pine resin becomes paint thinners and perfumes.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet resin, the sticky substance pines produce to seal wounds and repel insects. Learn how it is collected, distilled into turpentine and rosin, and used in varnish, perfumes, and the bows of string instruments.

name: Tanbark: The Leather Bark
teaser: How tree bark turned hides into leather.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how oak and chestnut bark, rich in tannins, were used to tan leather for centuries. Discover how bark was stripped and ground, how tanning pits worked, and how synthetic tanning replaced the old tanneries.

name: Tannins: The Bitter Protectors
teaser: The plant chemicals behind tea, wine, and leather.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet tannins, plant compounds that taste bitter and astringent, protecting plants from being eaten. Learn why they give tea and red wine their bite, how they tan leather, and how food processing tames them.

name: Gum Arabic: The Acacia Gum
teaser: A tree gum used in food, ink, and art.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover gum arabic, the dried sap of acacia trees, used for millennia as glue, ink binder, and food thickener. Learn how it stabilizes soft drinks and candy, why it is harvested in Sudan and the Sahel, and how it still shapes global trade.

name: Harvesting Cork
teaser: The nine-year rhythm of stripping cork oak.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow a cork harvest: workers carefully peel the outer bark of cork oaks, which regrows over about nine years. Learn why the trees live for centuries, how the bark is boiled and punched into corks, and why the forest must rest.

name: Hazel: The Coppice Wood
teaser: A woodland that regrows from its own stumps.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet hazel, a tree that regrows many shoots from a cut stump — a practice called coppicing. Learn how coppiced hazel supplied rods for hurdles, baskets, and walking sticks for millennia, and how it keeps woodlands alive.

name: Linnaeus: Naming Nature
teaser: The scientist who organized the plant world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet Carl Linnaeus, who gave every species a two-part Latin name and organized plants into families. Learn how his system tamed the chaos of naming, why his Latin names still rule science, and how he inspired a generation of plant hunters.

name: Plant Hunters: The Explorers
teaser: The adventurers who scoured the world for plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the plant hunters of the 1700s and 1800s, who braved jungles and disease to find new plants. Learn how they smuggled seeds and cuttings — tea from China, rubber from Brazil — and how their finds reshaped gardens and empires.

name: Darwin and the Plants
teaser: How the great naturalist studied plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover that Darwin devoted years to plants — studying climbing vines, orchids, and insect-eating species. Learn how plant studies supported his ideas on adaptation, and how his book on orchid pollination startled Victorian readers.

name: Mendel's Peas: The Hidden Laws
teaser: The monk whose pea garden founded genetics.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet Gregor Mendel, whose careful crosses of pea plants revealed the hidden laws of heredity. Learn how he counted wrinkled and smooth seeds, why his work was ignored for decades, and how it became the foundation of modern genetics.

name: Burbank: The Plant Wizard
teaser: The breeder who gave us the russet potato.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet Luther Burbank, the self-taught American breeder who created hundreds of new varieties, from the Burbank russet potato to the Shasta daisy. Learn how his fast, massive breeding programs inspired and puzzled scientists.

name: George Washington Carver's Plants
teaser: The botanist who transformed Southern farming.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of George Washington Carver
exploreAction.instruction: Meet George Washington Carver, who championed peanuts, sweet potatoes, and soil restoration for Southern farmers. Learn how his crop rotations rebuilt worn soils, how he found hundreds of uses for the peanut, and why he is a legend.

name: Early Botanists: The Founders
teaser: The first scientists of the plant world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the founders of botany, from Theophrastus, the 'father of botany' in ancient Greece, to the herbalists who cataloged plants for medicine. Learn how their writings, gardens, and illustrations built the science of plants.

name: Herbals: The Plant Books
teaser: The illustrated books that taught medicine from plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover herbals, the illustrated books that for centuries taught people which plants healed and which harmed. Learn how monks copied and preserved them, how printing spread them, and how they mixed observation with legend.

name: Botanical Illustration: Drawing Science
teaser: The art that documented the plant world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet botanical illustration, the art that documents plants with scientific accuracy. Learn how illustrators traveled with explorers, how the images helped identify species, and how the tradition continues today.

name: Herbaria: The Pressed Libraries
teaser: Museums of pressed plants for science.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about herbaria, collections of pressed, labeled plants stored in museums. Discover how scientists use them to identify species, track climate change, and study history — and how some specimens are centuries old.

name: Why Plants Have Latin Names
teaser: The system behind every plant's two names.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why plants carry Latin names: a genus and species pair that works worldwide, whatever the local language. Discover how names honor people and places, how naming rules work, and why scientists still use the system.

name: Indigenous Plant Knowledge
teaser: The deep knowledge of local plants and uses.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of traditional plant knowledge
exploreAction.instruction: Explore the deep botanical knowledge of Indigenous peoples — which plants heal, feed, and poison, and how to harvest sustainably. Learn how this knowledge is studied, valued, and passed down, and how it is being preserved today.

name: Ethnobotany: Plants and People
teaser: The science of how cultures use plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet ethnobotany, the science of how people use and understand plants. Learn how researchers study traditional medicines, foods, and rituals, and how this knowledge has yielded modern drugs and crops.

name: Plants in Myth and Folklore
teaser: The legends woven around trees and flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Wander through plant folklore: the mistletoe of the druids, the mandrake that shrieked, and the rowan that warded off evil. Learn how people explained plants they couldn't fully understand, and how those tales still color our symbols.

name: Sacred Trees of the World
teaser: Trees honored across cultures and faiths.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet sacred trees: the Bodhi tree of Buddhism, the oak of the druids, the olive of peace, and the ash Yggdrasil of Norse myth. Learn why trees became symbols of life, wisdom, and connection across cultures.

name: Essential Oils: The Plant Perfumes
teaser: How plants make their aromatic oils.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how essential oils are made: plants concentrate aromatic compounds in glands, and distillation or pressing extracts them. Discover how the same oil that attracts pollinators also repels pests, and how these oils are used in scent and medicine.

name: Plant Pigments: Beyond Green
teaser: The colors hidden in every leaf and petal.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the pigments that color plants: green chlorophyll, orange carotenoids, and red-blue anthocyanins. Learn how each absorbs different light and protects the plant, and how they combine to produce autumn's color show.

name: Anthocyanins: The Red and Blue
teaser: The pigments behind autumn reds and berry purples.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover anthocyanins, the pigments that make berries purple and autumn leaves red. Learn why plants make them — to protect leaves and attract seed spreaders — and how acid or alkaline conditions change their color.

name: Carotenoids: The Orange Family
teaser: The pigments behind carrots and marigolds.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet carotenoids, the orange and yellow pigments in carrots, pumpkins, and marigolds. Learn how they protect plants from sun damage, how they become vitamin A in our bodies, and why they appear when chlorophyll fades.

name: Phytochemicals: The Defenders
teaser: The plant chemicals that protect and nourish.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about phytochemicals — the thousands of compounds plants make to defend themselves. Discover how some, like the resveratrol in grapes, are studied for human health, and how plant foods deliver a chemical toolkit.

name: Antioxidants: The Plant Defense
teaser: Why colorful plant foods are praised.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how antioxidants in plants — from the anthocyanins of berries to the vitamin C of citrus — neutralize damaging molecules. Understand what antioxidants do in our bodies and why whole plant foods deliver them best.

name: Alkaloids: The Bitter Drugs
teaser: The nitrogen compounds behind coffee, tobacco, and more.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet alkaloids, bitter nitrogen compounds plants use to deter animals — including caffeine, nicotine, morphine, and quinine. Learn how these molecules work on our nervous systems, and how they gave medicine both cures and addictions.

name: Caffeine: The Plant's Defence
teaser: Why coffee and tea plants make caffeine.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why coffee, tea, and cacao plants make caffeine: it is a natural insecticide that also shapes the plants' biology. Discover how caffeine works on insect and human nerves, and how much of it a plant produces per bean.

name: Nicotine: The Tobacco Defense
teaser: A plant poison with a long human history.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how nicotine, a powerful toxin, protects tobacco plants from insects. Discover how it became one of humanity's most consumed substances, how it acts on the brain, and how its history is a cautionary tale.

name: Latex: The Milky Defense
teaser: Why some plants bleed white.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover latex, the milky sap some plants ooze when damaged, gluing shut the mouths of hungry insects. Learn why dandelions, figs, and rubber trees make it, and how latex became rubber, chicle, and more.

name: Saponins: The Soapy Chemicals
teaser: Plants that lather like soap.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet saponins, plant compounds that foam in water, found in soapwort and quillaja bark. Learn how these natural detergents were used for washing, how they protect plants, and why they are used in vaccines and foam.

name: Plant Waxes: The Raincoats
teaser: The waxy coats that keep plants dry.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about the waxy cuticle that coats leaves, keeping water in and rain out. Discover how waxes shed dirt and pests, how the blue-gray bloom on grapes and plums is wax, and why some plants are waxy to survive dry air.

name: Volatile Oils: The Scent Defense
teaser: The fragrant chemicals that defend and attract.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how volatile oils — the fragrant compounds of mint, pine, and citrus — both repel pests and attract pollinators. Discover how their small, airborne molecules carry scent, and how plants release them when damaged.

name: Tannins in Plants
teaser: The bitter compounds that preserve and protect.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of tannins in plants
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how tannins, bitter compounds in oak bark, tea leaves, and unripe fruit, protect plants from grazing. Discover how they bind proteins — which is how they tan leather — and why they make some foods puckery.

name: Sugar From Plants
teaser: Where the world's sugar really comes from.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn that commercial sugar comes from two plants: sugarcane, grown in the tropics, and sugar beet, grown in cooler climates. Discover how both are processed into identical white crystals, and how each fills a different part of the market.

name: Orchid Trickery: Fooling Bees
teaser: Orchids that mimic female bees.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how some orchids trick bees: their flowers mimic female bees so perfectly that males try to mate with them, carrying pollen in the process. Discover how this deception evolved and how scientists study its precision.

name: Carnivorous Plants of the Rainforest
teaser: Meat-eating plants in the wettest forests.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the carnivorous plants of tropical rainforests: giant pitcher plants, sundews, and bladderworts. Learn how the downpours and poor soil drive them to hunt, and how they catch prey in the steaming jungle.

name: Tropical Fruit Gardens
teaser: The backyard orchards of the tropics.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of tropical fruit gardens
exploreAction.instruction: Visit a tropical home garden, where mango, papaya, banana, and citrus fruit nearly year-round. Learn how the warm climate supports layered planting, and how these gardens feed families without supermarkets.

name: Australian Flora: The Unique South
teaser: Plants that grow nowhere else.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet Australia's distinctive flora: eucalyptus, wattles, banksias, and grass trees. Learn how long isolation and poor soil shaped plants that survive fire and drought, and how many are found nowhere else on Earth.

name: Madagascar's Plants: The Isolated Island
teaser: An island flora that evolved alone.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore Madagascar's plant life, isolated for millions of years: its own baobabs, palms, and orchids found nowhere else. Learn how the island's unique history created one of the world's most unusual floras — and one of the most threatened.

name: The Fynbos: Cape Flowers
teaser: A tiny region with astonishing plant diversity.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the fynbos, a small region of South Africa that holds one of the world's richest plant communities — proteas, ericas, and restios. Learn why this Mediterranean-climate heathland is called a kingdom of flowers.

name: Alpine Plants: The High Garden
teaser: Plants that bloom at the roof of the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet alpine plants, the tough blooms of high mountains: cushion plants, saxifrages, and gentians. Learn how they hug the ground, grow slowly, and use fuzzy coats to survive wind, cold, and fierce sun at altitude.

name: Mediterranean Flora: The Dry Summer
teaser: Plants built for hot dry summers.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore Mediterranean flora — olives, vines, cypress, and aromatic herbs — adapted to mild wet winters and hot dry summers. Learn how leathery leaves, deep roots, and scented oils help these plants survive the drought season.

name: Desert Blooms: The Rain Awakening
teaser: How deserts explode into flower after rain.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how deserts burst into flower after rain: seeds that waited for years sprout together, carpeting sand in color. Learn how these ephemeral plants race through their life cycle, and how desert wildflower seasons draw visitors.

name: Prairie Flowers: The Grassland Blooms
teaser: The wildflowers of the great grasslands.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet prairie flowers — coneflowers, blazing stars, and goldenrods — that color the great grasslands. Learn how their deep roots survive drought and fire, and how they feed the pollinators of the plains.

name: Wetland Plants: The Water's Edge
teaser: Plants that live with their feet in water.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet wetland plants — cattails, reeds, and water lilies — that thrive with roots underwater. Learn how they filter water, shelter wildlife, and build peat, and why marshes are among the most productive habitats.

name: Bog Plants: The Acid Specialists
teaser: Plants that survive waterlogged acid soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover bog plants — sphagnum moss, sundews, and cranberries — that live in waterlogged, acid, low-oxygen soil. Learn how carnivory supplies the nitrogen the bog lacks, and how bogs preserve what falls into them.

name: Coastal Plants: The Salt Tolerators
teaser: Plants that thrive where waves and salt rule.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet coastal plants that survive salt spray and sandy soil: sea thrift, beach grass, and salt-tolerant shrubs. Learn how they hold sand dunes together, filter salt, and anchor the shifting shore.

name: Mountain Meadows: The Summer Blooms
teaser: Wildflowers that race through a short season.

exploreAction.instruction: Visit mountain meadows, where wildflowers bloom in a burst during the short summer between snows. Learn how these plants store energy underground, flower quickly, and feed bees at high altitude.

name: Island Plants: The Endemics
teaser: Why islands grow plants found nowhere else.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore why islands have unique plants: species that arrived by wind, wave, or bird evolved in isolation into new forms. Learn about island giants, lost flightless birds' food plants, and why island floras are fragile.

name: Wheat Varieties and Flour
teaser: Why different wheats make different bread.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how wheat varieties differ: hard wheats with more protein make chewy bread flour, soft wheats make tender cake flour, and durum makes pasta. Discover how gluten builds structure, and how breeders match wheat to its use.

name: Gluten: The Bread Builder
teaser: The protein network that gives bread its chew.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet gluten, the protein network that forms when wheat flour meets water and kneading. Learn how it traps gas and makes dough rise, why it gives bread its chew, and what it means for people who avoid it.

name: Sourdough: The Wild Yeast
teaser: Bread leavened by wild microbes.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how sourdough rises with wild yeast and bacteria instead of packaged yeast. Discover how the starter is fed and kept alive, why the slow fermentation adds tang and keeps bread longer, and how bakers keep cultures for decades.

name: Rice Varieties: The Many Grains
teaser: From jasmine to arborio.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour the rice family: long-grain basmati and jasmine, sticky short-grain sushi rice, and starchy arborio for risotto. Learn how each variety's starch and aroma suit different dishes, and how breeding created them.

name: Corn Varieties: The Many Colors
teaser: Sweet, flint, dent, and popcorn.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the corn varieties: sweet corn eaten fresh, flint corn in many colors, dent corn for feed, and popcorn that explodes. Learn how each kernel type behaves differently when heated or milled.

name: Popcorn: Why It Pops
teaser: The science of an exploding kernel.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why popcorn pops: each kernel's hard shell traps steam until pressure explodes the starch into foam. Discover why only certain corn pops, how the moisture content matters, and why popcorn is a whole grain.

name: Sorghum: Many Uses
teaser: The grain that feeds, brews, and brooms.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover sorghum's many uses: grain for food, sweet syrup, livestock feed, and brooms from its stiff stalks. Learn how one plant serves everything from porridge to molasses, and why it thrives in dry heat.

name: Teff: The Tiny Ethiopian Grain
teaser: A grain so small it sows like dust.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet teff, one of the world's smallest grains, the foundation of Ethiopian injera bread. Learn how the tiny seeds are harvested and ground, why teff tolerates harsh conditions, and how it is being grown beyond Ethiopia.

name: Amaranth: The Aztec Grain
teaser: A tiny seed that fed an empire.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover amaranth, a tiny grain that fed the Aztecs and was nearly lost when Spanish rulers banned it. Learn how its seeds cook like a grain, how the plant's leaves are eaten as greens, and how it is making a comeback.

name: Buckwheat: Not a Wheat
teaser: A fruit seed that cooks like a grain.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why buckwheat is not a wheat — it is a fruit seed from a plant related to rhubarb. Discover how its nutty groats become soba noodles, pancakes, and kasha, and why it flowers so beautifully for bees.

name: Spelt: The Ancient Wheat
teaser: An old wheat cousin making a comeback.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet spelt, an ancient relative of wheat grown for millennia before being replaced by higher-yield modern wheats. Learn how its nutty flavor and tough husk make it distinctive, and why bakers are reviving it.

name: Kamut: The Legendary Grain
teaser: A wheat variety wrapped in legend.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover kamut, a large ancient wheat variety marketed with a legend linking it to Egyptian tombs. Learn how it actually traces to the Middle East, why its buttery flavor is prized, and how it is grown organically.

name: Sugarcane vs Sugar Beet
teaser: The two plants behind the world's sugar.

exploreAction.instruction: Compare sugarcane, a tropical giant grass, with sugar beet, a temperate root crop. Learn how each stores sugar differently, how processing differs, and how climate decides which one supplies a region.

name: Flax: Seed and Fiber
teaser: A plant that gives both linen and linseed oil.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how flax gives two harvests: its stem fibers make linen, and its seeds make linseed oil and omega-rich food. Discover how farmers grew flax for both cloth and paint for centuries, and how it is grown today.

name: Sesame: The Ancient Seeds
teaser: Tiny seeds with oil and crunch.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet sesame, among the oldest oilseed crops, grown for four thousand years. Learn how its pods burst open at harvest, how its oil and paste — tahini — flavor world cuisines, and why the seeds are so prized.

name: The Coconut Palm: Tree of Life
teaser: Why islanders call the coconut the tree of life.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the coconut palm
exploreAction.instruction: Learn why the coconut palm is called the tree of life: it supplies food, drink, oil, fiber, thatch, and timber. Discover how every part of the palm is used, how coconuts float to colonize islands, and how the palm feeds coastal people.

name: The Oil Palm: The Productive Giant
teaser: The most efficient oil crop in the world.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the oil palm
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the oil palm, which produces more oil per hectare than any rival, used in food, soap, and fuel. Learn how its fruit clusters are harvested and pressed, and the environmental cost when rainforests become plantations.

name: Date Palms of the Desert
teaser: The palm that made oases possible.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how date palms transform deserts into oases by shading cooler ground where other crops grow. Discover how palms are pollinated and pruned, how dates are harvested by climbers, and why the palm is sacred in desert cultures.

name: Rattan: The Climbing Palm
teaser: A palm that climbs and bends into furniture.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet rattan, a climbing palm whose long flexible stems become cane furniture and baskets. Learn how it grows up trees using hooks, how harvesters pull it down, and why it is one of the most valuable forest products.

name: Sago: The Starch Palm
teaser: A palm trunk full of edible starch.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover sago, starch harvested from the trunks of certain palms, a staple in New Guinea and Southeast Asia. Learn how the trunk is felled and the starch washed out, and how sago fed people before rice and wheat arrived.

name: The Banana Pseudostem
teaser: Why the banana trunk is not a trunk.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of the banana stem
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the banana's 'trunk' is a pseudostem — stacked leaf sheaths, not wood. Discover how the flower pushes up through the center, how each stem fruits once then dies, and how new shoots rise from the underground corm.

name: Taro and Poi
teaser: The Hawaiian staple from a starchy corm.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow taro to Hawaii, where the cooked corm is pounded with water into poi, a fermented staple. Learn how taro fields — lo'i — were engineered with irrigation, and how poi remains central to Hawaiian identity.

name: Breadfruit: The Starchy Fruit
teaser: A fruit that bakes like bread.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet breadfruit, a starchy tropical fruit that cooks like bread or potato. Learn how Captain Bligh's voyage carried it to the Caribbean, how one tree feeds a family, and how it is being revived as a climate-resilient crop.

name: Guava: Fruit and Leaves
teaser: A fruit eaten whole and a tree of many uses.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover guava's many uses: the fruit eaten fresh or juiced, the leaves brewed as tea, and the wood used for tools. Learn how guava trees fruit young and heavily, and why they have spread across the tropics.

name: Papaya: The Fast Fruit
teaser: A tree that fruits within a year.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how papaya trees grow and fruit astonishingly fast — often within a year of planting. Discover how the soft-trunked tree matures quickly, how its fruit ripens after picking, and why farmers love the quick turnaround.

name: Tropical Climbers: The Vines
teaser: Vines that climb to the sun.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet tropical climbing plants — lianas, rattans, and vines that climb trees to reach light. Learn how they use hooks, tendrils, and twining stems, how they connect the canopy, and why they are called jungle ladders.

name: Epiphyte Gardens: Branches Alive
teaser: The mini-gardens growing on tree branches.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how tree branches host miniature gardens of orchids, ferns, and bromeliads. Learn how these epiphytes catch falling leaves and rain, how bromeliads hold water in cups, and how animals drink from these treetop pools.

name: Bromeliads: The Water Cups
teaser: Tropical plants that hold rain in their leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet bromeliads, tropical plants whose overlapping leaves form cups that hold rainwater. Learn how tree frogs and insects live in these treetop pools, how some bromeliads trap insects for nutrients, and how they anchor to bark.

name: Mangosteen: The Queen
teaser: Why a purple fruit earned a royal title.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why mangosteen is called the queen of fruits: its sweet-tart segments were once reserved for royalty in Southeast Asia. Discover how the thick rind protects the flesh, how the fruit was long forbidden to export, and how it travels now.

name: Durian: The Smell Science
teaser: The chemistry behind the king of fruits' aroma.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what makes durian smell so powerful: a cocktail of sulfur compounds detectable across a room. Discover why the same compounds can smell savory and sweet to some, and how the fruit's smell is studied by chemists.

name: National Flowers: The Emblems
teaser: The blooms that symbolize nations.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour the world's national flowers: the rose of England and America, the chrysanthemum of Japan, the lotus of India, and the tulip of the Netherlands. Learn why each nation chose its bloom and what it symbolizes.

name: State Flowers: The American Garden
teaser: How every US state chose a flower.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how each US state adopted an official flower, from Alabama's camellia to Wyoming's Indian paintbrush. Learn why schoolchildren championed some choices, and how the flowers reflect each state's landscape.

name: The Rose: A Breeding History
teaser: How five thousand years of breeding shaped the rose.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the rose through five millennia of breeding, from simple five-petaled wildflowers to layered hybrids. Learn how China's repeat-blooming roses transformed European gardens, and how breeders create new varieties.

name: Tulip Mania: The Bubble
teaser: The flower frenzy that became a legend.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore tulip mania, the 1630s Dutch craze when single bulbs sold for fortunes before prices collapsed. Learn what really happened, how the streaked 'broken' tulips were caused by a virus, and how the legend grew in the telling.

name: Orchid Mania: The Victorian Fever
teaser: The flower craze that sent collectors around the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet orchid mania, the Victorian obsession that sent collectors to jungles for rare orchids. Learn how fortunes were spent, how some collectors died in the field, and how the craze left millions of plants in European greenhouses.

name: Flower Shows: The Competitions
teaser: Where growers compete with perfect blooms.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover flower shows, from local halls to the Chelsea Flower Show, where growers compete for prize blooms. Learn how judges score size, color, and condition, and how chrysanthemum and dahlia growers push their plants to extremes.

name: The Tradition of Giving Flowers
teaser: Why we give flowers on every occasion.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore why flowers are the universal gift — for love, sympathy, celebration, and apology. Learn how the tradition spans cultures and centuries, and how the meaning of flowers has been codified and reimagined.

name: Flower Festivals of the World
