teaser: Carnivals and parades built on blooms.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour the world's flower festivals: the Rose Parade in Pasadena, the Chelsea Flower Show, the flower battles of the Riviera, and India's flower festivals. Learn how communities turn blooms into parades and spectacles.

name: Daffodils: The Spring Signals
teaser: The golden blooms that announce spring.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the daffodil, one of the first flowers of spring, whose trumpet blooms push through cold soil. Learn how its bulbs multiply, why it is the symbol of cancer charities, and how it naturalizes into golden drifts.

name: Iris: Named for the Rainbow
teaser: A flower of a hundred colors.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the iris, named for the Greek goddess of the rainbow because of its color range. Learn how the bearded iris's falls and standards are arranged, how it became the fleur-de-lis, and how it grows from rhizomes.

name: The Poppy: For Remembrance
teaser: A flower that grew on battlefields.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the remembrance poppy
exploreAction.instruction: Learn why the red poppy became the symbol of remembrance: it bloomed on the ravaged battlefields of the First World War. Discover how the poppy's seeds wait in soil and flower after disturbance, and how it honors the fallen.

name: Lilies: The Many Meanings
teaser: From Easter lilies to tiger lilies.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the lily family: Easter lilies, fragrant white madonna lilies, and spotted tiger lilies. Learn how lilies grow from bulbs, why some are toxic to cats, and how they appear in art and religion across cultures.

name: Chrysanthemums: The Autumn Blooms
teaser: The flower that ends the growing season.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the chrysanthemum, the flower of autumn, treasured in Japan where it graces the imperial crest. Learn how it blooms as days shorten, how it is bred into endless forms, and why it is the flower of longevity in East Asia.

name: Geraniums: The Window Box Classic
teaser: The bright bloom of balconies worldwide.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the geranium, the bright bloom of window boxes from Switzerland to Morocco. Learn why true geraniums and 'geraniums' called pelargoniums differ, and how these sun-loving plants flower all summer with little care.

name: Petunias: The Summer Color
teaser: Trailing and upright blooms for every pot.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover petunias, among the most planted summer flowers, from trailing wave petunias to upright doubles. Learn how they come from South America, how they are bred for heat and rain, and why they flower nonstop.

name: Plant Life Cycles: The Circle
teaser: From seed to seed, the plant's journey.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of plant life cycles
exploreAction.instruction: Follow a plant's full life cycle: seed, germination, growth, flowering, fruiting, and death. Learn how annuals, biennials, and perennials divide the journey differently, and how each stage is tuned to the seasons.

name: Annuals, Biennials, Perennials
teaser: Three life strategies, three timelines.

exploreAction.instruction: Sort out the three plant life strategies: annuals complete their life in one year, biennials take two, and perennials return for many. Learn how each strategy suits different climates, and how gardeners use all three.

name: Dormancy: The Plant's Rest
teaser: How plants pause through winter.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants enter dormancy, a state of slowed life that survives winter, drought, or heat. Discover how buds and seeds wait for the right signal, and how chilling requirements keep plants from blooming too early.

name: Buds: The Plant's Future
teaser: Where next season's growth hides.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet buds, the packed packages of future stems, leaves, and flowers that wait on branches. Learn how terminal and lateral buds direct growth, how buds break in spring, and how pruning can wake sleeping buds.

name: Leaf Shapes and Jobs
teaser: Why leaves come in so many forms.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how leaf shape reflects function: broad leaves catch sun in shade, needle leaves save water, and divided leaves shed heat. Discover how size, thickness, and surface all adapt to light and climate.

name: Leaf Fall: Letting Go
teaser: How trees drop their leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how trees shed leaves: a layer of cells seals each leaf stem before it falls. Discover why deciduous trees drop leaves to save water in winter, how the tree recycles nutrients first, and why evergreens keep theirs.

name: Evergreens: Keeping Their Leaves
teaser: Why some trees stay green all year.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how evergreen trees keep leaves through winter with waxy coats and antifreeze chemistry. Discover why keeping leaves pays off in mild climates and poor soil, and how evergreens still shed leaves gradually.

name: Deciduous Trees: The Shedders
teaser: Why some trees lose everything each year.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why deciduous trees drop all their leaves each autumn: leaves are costly to keep through freezing winter. Learn how shedding saves water, and how the annual cycle of growth and drop shapes temperate forests.

name: Tree Bark: The Living Armor
teaser: What bark is and what it does.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what bark really is: outer dead cork and inner living phloem that carries food. Discover why bark protects against fire, insects, and weather, how it heals wounds, and why some barks peel in striking patterns.

name: Heartwood and Sapwood
teaser: The two woods inside a trunk.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how a trunk has two kinds of wood: sapwood, which carries water, and heartwood, the darker dead core that gives strength. Discover how heartwood forms and why it is often the wood we use.

name: Annual Rings: The Growth Record
teaser: How a tree grows wider each year.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how trees grow wider by adding a ring of new wood each year — wide and light in spring, narrow and dark in summer. Discover how to count a tree's age and read its history from the rings.

name: Bark and Insects
teaser: The battle between bark and borers.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how insects attack tree bark — borers tunneling beneath it — and how trees fight back with resin and callus. Discover how bark beetles spread disease and why stressed trees are most vulnerable.

name: Phloem: The Food Tubes
teaser: How sugars travel down the tree.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet phloem, the tubes that carry sugars from leaves to roots, fruits, and growing tips. Learn how pressure drives the flow, how phloem sits just inside bark, and why girdling a trunk — cutting phloem — kills a tree.

name: The Cambium: The Growth Layer
teaser: The living sleeve that makes new wood.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the cambium, a thin layer of dividing cells between bark and wood that adds new rings each year. Learn how it makes phloem outward and xylem inward, and why a single ring of cells grows the whole trunk.

name: Girdling: The Tree Killer
teaser: Why removing a ring of bark kills a tree.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why girdling — cutting a ring through the bark and phloem — kills a tree: food stops reaching the roots. Discover how this old technique clears land without felling, and how it is used in forestry and archaeology.

name: Greenhouse Crops: The Indoor Farm
teaser: What grows best under glass.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn which crops thrive in greenhouses — tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, and herbs — where heat and light are controlled. Discover how growers manage temperature, humidity, and pollination under glass for year-round harvests.

name: Polytunnels: The Budget Greenhouse
teaser: A hoop of plastic that extends the season.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the polytunnel, a hoop of plastic sheeting that warms soil and shelters crops without a glass house. Learn how it extends growing seasons and protects plants, and how gardeners use it on a budget.

name: Cold Frames: The Simple Greenhouse
teaser: A glass box that hardens off seedlings.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the cold frame, a low glass box that traps heat to protect plants and start seeds early. Learn how it works like a tiny greenhouse, how it hardens off seedlings, and why gardeners build one against a sunny wall.

name: Cloches: The Plant Covers
teaser: Bell jars that protect single plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the cloche, a glass bell or plastic cover placed over individual plants to trap warmth and shelter them. Learn how Victorian gardeners used glass cloches, and how modern ones protect early crops from cold.

name: Shade Houses: The Filtered Light
teaser: Structures that soften harsh sun.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how shade houses filter intense sun with netting, protecting shade-loving plants and reducing heat. Discover why nurseries in hot climates use them, and how gardeners build simple shade frames.

name: Seed Trays: The Nursery
teaser: How trays of tiny seeds become gardens.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how seed trays work: small cells of compost, one seed each, kept moist and warm until germination. Discover why drainage and light matter, how to prick out seedlings, and how trays standardize the start of the season.

name: Potting Mix: The Recipe
teaser: What goes into the bag of soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Decode potting mix: peat or coir for moisture, perlite for drainage, and compost for food. Learn why 'soilless' mixes beat garden soil in pots, and how the blend changes for seeds, succulents, and orchids.

name: Perlite and Vermiculite
teaser: The two volcanic minerals in your pots.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of perlite and vermiculite
exploreAction.instruction: Meet perlite, the white volcanic glass that aerates soil, and vermiculite, the golden mineral that holds water. Learn how each is made by heating rock, and when gardeners choose one over the other.

name: Garden Watering Systems
teaser: From cans to drip lines.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore garden watering systems: watering cans, soaker hoses, sprinklers, and drip lines. Learn how drip irrigation delivers water to roots with little waste, and how timers and sensors make watering automatic.

name: Rain Barrels: Catching the Sky
teaser: Storing rain for the garden.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how rain barrels capture roof runoff for the garden, saving water and reducing storm runoff. Discover how to set one up, why covered barrels keep mosquitoes out, and how the stored water suits plants better than tap.

name: Greywater: The Recycled Water
teaser: Reusing household water in the garden.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about greywater — gently used water from sinks and showers — reused to irrigate gardens. Discover what to avoid, how to divert it safely, and why it matters in dry regions.

name: Soil Testing: Know Your Dirt
teaser: The simple tests that reveal soil health.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to test garden soil — pH strips, nutrient tests, and the feel and smell of good earth. Discover why testing guides lime and fertilizer choices, and how home tests compare to lab analysis.

name: Mulch Types Compared
teaser: Wood chips, straw, and leaves at work.

exploreAction.instruction: Compare mulches: wood chips last and slowly feed, straw is light and weed-free, leaves are free and quick, and gravel suits succulents. Learn which mulch to use where, and how each changes the soil beneath.

name: Filling Raised Beds
teaser: The layered recipe for a new bed.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to fill a raised bed: drainage at the base, bulky organic matter, and rich compost at the top. Discover the lasagna method of layering, why beds settle, and how to keep the soil fertile over years.

name: Trellises: Training the Vines
teaser: Teaching climbing plants to grow up.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how trellises, stakes, and cages support climbing plants — beans up poles, tomatoes in cages, vines on wires. Discover why growing up improves airflow and harvests, and how to train tendrils and ties.

name: Top Pollinator Plants
teaser: The flowers that feed bees and butterflies best.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn which plants attract pollinators best: lavender, coneflower, salvia, and native wildflowers. Discover why flower shape, color, and bloom timing matter, and how a pollinator patch supports the insects that feed us.

name: Butterfly Gardens: The Flutter Patch
teaser: Planting for caterpillars and butterflies.

exploreAction.targetName: how to build a butterfly garden
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to build a butterfly garden: nectar flowers for adults and host plants like milkweed for caterpillars. Discover why a garden needs both, how to avoid pesticides, and how butterflies find your patch.

name: Milkweed: The Monarch's Home
teaser: The only plant monarch caterpillars eat.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet milkweed, the only food of monarch caterpillars and the plant monarchs need to survive. Learn how its milky sap protects the caterpillars, how planting milkweed helps the migration, and why it is disappearing.

name: Gardens for Bees
teaser: Planting for the world's best pollinators.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to plant for bees: nectar-rich flowers, bloom from spring to fall, and no pesticides. Discover why bumblebees need early flowers, how different bees favor different blooms, and how your garden becomes a bee stop.

name: Hummingbird Gardens
teaser: Planting the red tubes hummingbirds love.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to create a hummingbird garden with tubular red and orange flowers like trumpet vine and salvia. Discover why feeders are only part of the story, and how native flowers support these tiny birds.

name: Night Gardens: The Moth Shift
teaser: Planting pale fragrant blooms for the night.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the night garden, planted with white and pale flowers that glow at dusk and release fragrance to attract moths. Learn which flowers bloom at night, and how a moon garden invites nocturnal pollinators.

name: Gardens That Feed Birds
teaser: Berry bushes and seed heads for winter birds.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to plant a bird-friendly garden: berry bushes, seed heads, and evergreen shelter. Discover which plants feed birds through winter, and why leaving the garden 'messy' can be best for wildlife.

name: Hedgerows: The Wildlife Corridors
teaser: Living fences packed with life.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the hedgerow, a living fence of shrubs and trees that shelters birds, insects, and mammals. Learn how hedges serve as wildlife corridors, how they are laid and managed, and why they are vital to farmland.

name: Planting Wildflower Meadows
teaser: Turning a lawn into a sea of blooms.

exploreAction.targetName: how to plant a wildflower meadow
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to plant a wildflower meadow: prepare poor soil, scatter native seeds, and resist mowing. Discover why meadows take years to establish, how to manage them, and the rewards for bees and butterflies.

name: Lawns That Feed Bees
teaser: Turning grass into pollinator pasture.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how a 'bee lawn' mixes grass with low flowers like clover and self-heal to feed pollinators while staying walkable. Discover how reducing mowing height and frequency turns a plain lawn into habitat.

name: Nectar-Rich Flowers
teaser: The flowers that produce the most nectar.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn which flowers produce the most nectar and why — from borage and phacelia to linden trees. Discover how nectar content varies with weather and variety, and how to choose flowers that feed bees longest.

name: Host Plants: The Caterpillar Menu
teaser: Why butterflies need specific plants to lay eggs.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about host plants — the specific plants each butterfly species needs for its caterpillars. Discover why monarchs need milkweed and swallowtails need fennel, and how planting hosts supports butterflies.

name: Seeding Annuals and Perennials
teaser: The different sowing strategies.

exploreAction.targetName: how to sow annuals and perennials
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how sowing differs: annuals bloom the first year from seed, perennials take their time building roots before flowering. Discover when to sow each, and how gardeners mix both for a lasting garden.

name: Winter Gardens: The Rest Season
teaser: What gardens do when the world sleeps.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the winter garden, where bare branches, berries, and evergreens carry the scene. Learn how gardeners plan for winter interest, protect tender plants, and let the soil rest before spring.

name: Planning a Garden Year
teaser: Mapping planting, harvest, and rest.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to plan a garden year: what to sow in each season, when to harvest, and when to let beds rest. Discover how crop calendars, successions, and hardy plants keep a garden productive across the months.

name: Broccoli: The Bred Flower
teaser: How a wild cabbage became a vegetable.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how broccoli was bred from wild cabbage, selected for its unopened flower heads. Discover how the plant stores energy in the head, why it is harvested before flowers open, and how Roman growers refined it.

name: Cauliflower: The White Head
teaser: How gardeners keep a flower head white.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how cauliflower's white head is kept pale by blanching — folding leaves over the developing curd. Learn how this cousin of broccoli is bred and grown, and why the curd is actually immature flowers.

name: Kale: The Hardy Greens
teaser: A cold-loving cabbage cousin.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet kale, a cabbage cousin that sweetens after frost and thrives in cool seasons. Learn how its curly leaves stand up to winter, why it is packed with vitamins, and how it became a modern superfood.

name: Brussels Sprouts: The Tiny Heads
teaser: Little cabbage heads along a tall stem.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Brussels sprouts grow as tiny cabbage heads along a tall stem, each a bud in a leaf axil. Discover why they need cool weather, how the stem is stripped upward as they ripen, and how breeding made them sweeter.

name: Cabbage: The Fermenter
teaser: How cabbage becomes sauerkraut and kimchi.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cabbage is fermented into sauerkraut and kimchi: salt draws out water, and lactic acid bacteria preserve and sour the leaves. Discover how this ancient technique stored cabbage through winter, and why the results are probiotic.

name: Cucumbers and Pickles
teaser: How cucumbers become pickles.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cucumbers become pickles: soaked in brine or vinegar with dill and spices, then fermented or canned. Discover what makes a good pickling cucumber, and how different brines create dill, sweet, or sour pickles.

name: Bell Peppers: The Sweet Capsicums
teaser: A pepper bred for no heat.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the bell pepper, a capsicum bred to carry no capsaicin heat. Learn how its blocky shape and crisp flesh were selected, how green peppers are just unripe ones, and how breeding added yellow, orange, and purple.

name: Summer Squash: The Quick Harvest
teaser: Squash picked young and tender.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover summer squash — zucchini, yellow crookneck, and pattypan — picked young while the skin is tender. Learn how they differ from winter squash, how fast they fruit, and why one missed zucchini becomes a giant.

name: Winter Squash: The Storer
teaser: Squash that cure and keep for months.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet winter squash — butternut, acorn, and pumpkin — whose hard skins let them store for months. Learn how curing hardens the skin, how the dense flesh sweetens in storage, and how they differ from summer squash.

name: Peas: The Cool Crop
teaser: A legume that loves early spring.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet peas, a cool-season legume sown early and harvested in spring. Learn how the pods develop from flowers, how the vines climb with tendrils, and how peas fix nitrogen for the garden soil.

name: Green Beans: Pole and Bush
teaser: Two growth habits, one delicious pod.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the two ways green beans grow: pole beans climb high and yield long, bush beans stay low and ripen together. Discover how both are picked young, and how the plants fix nitrogen as they grow.

name: Radishes: The Fast Crop
teaser: A root ready in under a month.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the radish, one of the fastest crops, ready to pull in under a month. Learn how its peppery bite comes from mustard oils, how it was bred from a wild Asian root, and why it is perfect for impatient gardeners.

name: Beets: The Sweet Roots
teaser: A root that hides surprising sweetness.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover beets, whose deep red roots are surprisingly sweet, and whose leaves are eaten as greens. Learn how the color comes from betalain pigments, how beets were bred from sea beet, and how sugar beets came from them.

name: Turnips: The Simple Roots
teaser: The humble root that fed Europe.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the turnip, a humble root that fed Europe for centuries, eaten by people and livestock alike. Learn how it grows fast in cool weather, how its greens are also edible, and how it was once a staple before potatoes arrived.

name: Leeks: The Mild Onions
teaser: A sweet onion cousin that never bulbs.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover leeks, an onion cousin grown for its thick white stalk rather than a bulb. Learn how hilling soil keeps the stem pale and tender, how leeks survive frost, and why they are the emblem of Wales.

name: Planting Fruit Trees
teaser: The first steps to a lifelong harvest.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to plant a fruit tree: choose a sunny spot, dig wide not deep, and stake young trees. Discover why the graft union must stay above soil, how to water young trees in, and how the first years shape the tree's future.

name: Orchard Design: The Fruit Garden
teaser: Planning rows of fruit for years ahead.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to design a home orchard: choose varieties for your climate, space trees for sun, and plan for pollinators. Discover how dwarf trees fit small gardens, and how mixed orchards spread harvests across the season.

name: Dwarf Fruit Trees
teaser: How tiny trees grow full-size fruit.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how dwarf fruit trees grow full-size fruit on small trees by grafting onto rootstocks that limit growth. Discover why they suit small gardens, how they fruit sooner, and what care they need.

name: Pruning Apple Trees
teaser: The yearly cuts that shape and fruit.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why apple trees are pruned each winter: to shape the tree, let in light, and spur new fruiting wood. Discover the open-center style, how to remove crossing branches, and why good cuts mean better apples.

name: Thinning Fruit: Fewer, Better
teaser: Why gardeners remove baby fruit.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why gardeners thin fruit — removing some young fruit so the rest grow bigger and the tree isn't overloaded. Discover how to thin apples and peaches, and why a biennial cycle of heavy and light crops is avoided.

name: Grafting Fruit Trees
teaser: Joining a favorite variety to a strong root.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how fruit trees are grafted: a bud or shoot of a chosen variety is joined to a rootstock. Discover why grafting keeps varieties true, how whip and cleft grafts work, and why orchards rely on the technique.

name: Espalier: Training Against Walls
teaser: Shaping fruit trees flat and beautiful.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the espalier, a fruit tree trained flat against a wall or wires, its branches shaped in tiers. Learn how the technique suits warm walls and small spaces, and how pruning directs the tree's growth.

name: Fan Training: The Flat Fan
teaser: Spreading fruit branches like a hand.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to train a fruit tree as a fan, its branches spread like an open hand against a wall. Discover why plums, peaches, and figs suit this style, and how careful summer pruning shapes it.

name: Fruit Pollination Partners
teaser: Why some trees need a partner.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why many fruit trees need another variety nearby to cross-pollinate — apples, pears, and cherries. Discover how bees carry pollen between trees, what a pollinator partner is, and how some trees are self-fertile.

name: Growing Stone Fruits
teaser: Peaches, plums, and cherries in the garden.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow stone fruits — peaches, plums, cherries, and apricots — which ripen in summer. Discover why they need cold winters, well-drained soil, and careful thinning, and how they differ from pome fruits.

name: The Berry Patch
teaser: Growing strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow a berry patch: strawberries on raised beds, raspberries on canes, and blueberries in acid soil. Discover how each berries differently, and how to manage runners, canes, and pruning for years of fruit.

name: Training Grape Vines
teaser: Teaching vines to grow on wires.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how grape vines are trained onto wires in the classic forms — cordons and guyots. Discover why pruning back hard each winter forces fruiting wood, and how the vine's growth is directed along the trellis.

name: Growing Kiwi Vines
teaser: The vigorous vine that fruits in cool gardens.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how kiwi vines grow: vigorous climbers needing a strong support and both sexes or a self-fertile variety. Discover how the fuzzy fruit develops, how pruning tames the rampant vine, and how hardy kiwis suit cold gardens.

name: Growing Fig Trees
teaser: A warm-wall fruit that ripens twice.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how fig trees grow best against a warm wall, producing an early and a main crop. Discover how the roots are often restricted to encourage fruit, and how winter protection helps them in cool climates.

name: Growing Citrus in Pots
teaser: Oranges and lemons away from the tropics.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow citrus in pots
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow citrus in pots, moving them indoors for winter in cool climates. Discover why drainage and feeding matter, how to manage scale insects, and how a sunny conservatory keeps lemons happy.

name: Yellow Leaves: The Diagnosis
teaser: Why plant leaves turn yellow.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why leaves yellow: too much or too little water, missing nitrogen, poor drainage, or root damage. Discover how to read the pattern — whole leaf, between veins, or lower leaves — to find the real cause.

name: Wilting: Too Much or Too Little
teaser: The confusing plant distress signal.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why plants wilt from both drought and drowning — each starves the roots of what they need. Discover how to tell which it is by checking soil and roots, and how to rescue a plant from either extreme.

name: Root Rot: The Silent Killer
teaser: Why overwatering kills plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how root rot happens: waterlogged soil starves roots of oxygen, letting fungi rot them. Discover why the topsoil can look dry while roots drown, and how repotting in fresh soil rescues a plant.

name: Houseplant Pests: The Invaders
teaser: The bugs that move in with your plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet common houseplant pests — spider mites, mealybugs, aphids, and scale — which multiply fast indoors. Learn how to spot their signs, how to wash and treat plants, and how quarantine stops the spread.

name: Aphids: The Sap Suckers
teaser: Tiny insects that drain plant sap.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how aphids feed by sucking sap, stunting growth and spreading viruses. Discover why ants farm them for honeydew, and how ladybugs, water sprays, and soap control them naturally.

name: Slugs and Snails: The Night Feeders
teaser: The garden's most patient pests.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of slugs and snails
exploreAction.instruction: Meet slugs and snails, which graze plants at night and hide by day. Learn why they love damp mulch, how beer traps and barriers work, and how encouraging birds and ground beetles helps control them.

name: Powdery Mildew: The White Coating
teaser: A fungus that dusts leaves white.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how powdery mildew coats leaves in white fungal spores, weakening plants. Discover why it strikes in warm dry days and cool nights, and how spacing, airflow, and resistant varieties prevent it.

name: Tomato Blight: The Collapse
teaser: The fast disease that ruins tomato crops.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet blight, a fast fungal disease that browns and kills tomato and potato plants within days. Learn how wet weather spreads the spores, and how resistant varieties and airflow reduce the risk.

name: Beneficial Insects: The Garden Helpers
teaser: Bugs that protect your plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the insects that protect gardens — ladybugs that eat aphids, lacewings that hunt mites, and parasitic wasps. Learn how to attract them with flowers and avoid killing them with broad pesticides.

name: Integrated Pest Management
teaser: The smart way to handle garden pests.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about integrated pest management, a strategy that starts with prevention and only escalates as needed: tolerate some pests, encourage predators, and use chemicals last. Discover how it balances gardens naturally.

name: Nematodes: The Invisible Pests
teaser: Microscopic worms that attack roots.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet nematodes, microscopic worms in soil that can damage roots, and the beneficial ones used to control pests. Learn how to recognize root damage, and how certain nematodes are sold as natural pest control.

name: Preventing Plant Disease
teaser: The habits that keep plants healthy.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the habits that prevent plant disease: choose resistant varieties, space plants for airflow, water at the base, and clean tools. Discover why most disease is environmental, and how healthy soil grows healthy plants.

name: Frost Damage: The Cold Bite
teaser: How cold snaps injure plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how frost damages plants: ice crystals form inside cells and burst them. Discover why some plants survive light frost, how fleece and watering protect tender crops, and how to rescue frost-damaged plants.

name: Heat Stress: The Hot Bite
teaser: How heat waves hurt plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how heat stresses plants: they lose water faster than roots can replace it, scorching leaves and dropping fruit. Discover how mulch, shade cloth, and morning watering help gardens survive heat waves.

name: Transplant Shock: The Move
teaser: Why plants sulk after being moved.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why plants wilt after transplanting — roots are damaged and can't keep up with water loss. Discover how to dig with a big root ball, water well, and shade new plants to ease the move.

name: Growing Hydrangeas
teaser: The mopheads and their needs.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow hydrangeas: they want morning sun, rich soil, and steady moisture. Discover how to prune old-wood and new-wood types differently, and how to shift bloom color with soil pH.

name: Rose Care Basics
teaser: The simple habits for healthy roses.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the basics of rose care: full sun, deep watering, feeding in spring, and regular deadheading. Discover why air circulation prevents disease, and how winter protection varies by climate.

name: Growing Peonies
teaser: The long-lived bloom that hates to be moved.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow peonies: plant them shallow in full sun and leave them alone — they resent disturbance. Discover why ants visit the buds, how to support heavy blooms, and why peonies live for decades.

name: Growing Dahlias
teaser: The tuberous showstoppers of late summer.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet dahlias, tuberous flowers that bloom from midsummer to frost. Learn how to plant the tubers, stake the tall stems, and lift the tubers each autumn in cold climates to store for spring.

name: Tulips: Plant and Care
teaser: Getting the spring classic right.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow tulips: plant bulbs deep in autumn in well-drained soil and full sun. Discover why some gardeners treat them as annuals, how to deadhead, and why the foliage must die back naturally.

name: Daffodils: The Naturalizers
teaser: Bulbs that spread into golden drifts.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how daffodils naturalize, multiplying into drifts that return for decades. Discover why they thrive in grass, how long to leave foliage, and how to plant them in informal swathes.

name: Growing Lavender
teaser: The sun-loving Mediterranean shrub.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow lavender: full sun, poor sandy soil, and no summer water. Discover why it hates wet feet, how to prune woody plants, and how to harvest the fragrant spikes.

name: Clematis: The Climbing Blooms
teaser: Vines that flower across the seasons.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet clematis, climbing vines with spectacular flowers that climb by twining leaf stems. Learn how to plant them deep with shaded roots and sunny heads, and how pruning differs between the groups.

name: Wisteria: The Gorgeous Vine
teaser: A climber of cascading purple blooms.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet wisteria, a vigorous climber whose cascades of purple flowers announce spring. Learn why it must be pruned hard twice a year, how it twines around supports, and why it can take years to first bloom.

name: Fuchsias: The Delicate Dancers
teaser: Hanging flowers that thrive in shade.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet fuchsias, whose hanging two-tone flowers thrive in shade and coolness. Learn how they are grown in baskets and borders, how to keep them blooming by deadheading, and how tender ones overwinter indoors.

name: Begonias: The Versatile Blooms
teaser: Flowers for sun, shade, pots, and beds.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover begonias, a huge group with flowers and foliage for sun or shade. Learn how fibrous begonias fill beds, tuberous begonias shine in baskets, and how their tubers are stored in winter.

name: Pelargoniums: The Balcony Classic
teaser: The 'geraniums' that love sun and dryness.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow pelargoniums — the plants commonly called geraniums — which love sun, heat, and dry soil. Discover how they root from cuttings, how to overwinter them, and why they flower best when slightly pot-bound.

name: Impatiens: The Shade Color
teaser: Busy Lizzies for the dark corners.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet impatiens, the busy lizzies that carpet shady beds with color. Learn how they self-seed freely, why a mildew disease hit some types, and how new resistant varieties restored the classic.

name: Marigolds: The Bright Annuals
teaser: Golden blooms that guard the garden.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover marigolds, easy annuals in gold and orange that bloom all season. Learn why gardeners plant them among vegetables — their scent may deter pests — and how they self-seed and keep flowering when deadheaded.

name: Snapdragons: The Dragon Blooms
teaser: Spikes of flowers that snap open.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet snapdragons, whose spikes of 'dragon mouth' flowers snap open when pinched. Learn how they bloom in cool weather, how pinching makes them bushy, and how they are used as cut flowers.

name: Cannas: The Tropical Leaves
teaser: Big leaves and hot blooms.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet cannas, tropical plants with huge paddle leaves and bold flowers grown for a lush look. Learn how their rhizomes are planted in spring, how tall they grow, and how to lift and store the rhizomes in winter.

name: Ornamental Bananas
teaser: Growing banana 'trees' for their giant leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow banana plants for their enormous leaves, even in cool climates. Discover how the pseudostems die back each year, how new shoots regrow, and how wrapping the stems helps them overwinter.

name: Bird of Paradise: The Crane Flower
teaser: A flower shaped like a bird in flight.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of bird of paradise
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the bird of paradise, whose orange and blue flowers look like a bird's head. Learn how the plant grows from rhizomes in warm gardens, how long it takes to bloom, and why its flowers are built for sunbirds.

name: Bougainvillea: The Paper Flowers
teaser: Brilliant 'flowers' that are really leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn that bougainvillea's brilliant color comes from papery bracts, not its tiny white flowers. Discover how the thorny vine thrives in heat and dryness, how it cascades over walls, and how it resents wet roots.

name: Hibiscus: The Many Species
teaser: From tropical showstoppers to hardy shrubs.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the hibiscus family, from the huge tropical flowers of Hawaii to the hardy shrubs of cooler gardens. Learn how each type grows, why the flowers last a single day, and how tea is made from the blooms.

name: Plumeria: The Lei Flower
teaser: Fragrant blooms of the islands.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover plumeria, the fragrant flower of island leis, which grows from cuttings and blooms in the heat. Learn why the tree drops leaves in winter, how its waxy flowers avoid fading, and how it is rooted easily.

name: Growing Frangipani From Cuttings
teaser: A tree that roots from a snapped branch.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how frangipani grows from cuttings: a snapped branch can be dried and rooted in sandy soil. Discover why the milky sap must dry first, how long rooting takes, and why this makes the tree easy to share.

name: Caring for Monstera
teaser: The Swiss cheese plant at home.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to care for monstera: bright indirect light, a moss pole to climb, and watering when the topsoil dries. Discover why the leaves split, how to propagate stem cuttings, and why it forgives mistakes.

name: Peace Lily Care
teaser: The forgiving bloom for low light.

exploreAction.targetName: how to care for peace lilies
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to care for peace lilies: they thrive in low light and droop dramatically when thirsty, then recover. Discover why brown tips mean too much water or chlorine, and how to divide crowded clumps.

name: Caladiums: The Painted Leaves
teaser: Arrow leaves in pink, white, and red.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet caladiums, tropical plants grown for their painted arrow-shaped leaves. Learn how their tubers are planted in warmth, how they love shade and humidity, and how to store the tubers for next year.

name: Coleus: The Colorful Foliage
teaser: Plants grown for a rainbow of leaves.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover coleus, tropical plants grown for leaves in every combination of green, pink, red, and purple. Learn how pinching keeps them bushy, how they root easily from cuttings, and how they fill shade with color.

name: Ginger Lilies: The Fragrant Blooms
teaser: Tropical gingers with perfumed flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet ginger lilies, tropical gingers with fragrant showy blooms above leafy canes. Learn how their rhizomes grow into clumps, how the flowers attract hummingbirds, and how they bring a tropical scent to warm gardens.

name: Habanero: The Fiery Pepper
teaser: A small pepper with enormous heat.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the habanero, a small lantern-shaped pepper with intense heat and fruity flavor. Learn how its capsaicin content is measured, how it grows in warm climates, and how it ranks among the world's hottest peppers.

name: The Ghost Pepper: A Million Scovilles
teaser: The pepper that crossed the million mark.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the ghost pepper, one of the first peppers to exceed a million Scoville heat units. Learn where it comes from in India, how its heat builds slowly, and why handling it requires gloves.

name: The Scoville Scale: Measuring Heat
teaser: How pepper heat is measured.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of the Scoville scale
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the Scoville scale measures pepper heat by diluting extracts until heat is no longer felt. Discover how capsaicin concentration is now measured directly, and where common peppers fall on the scale.

name: The Largest Leaves
teaser: Leaves the size of umbrellas.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the record leaves: the giant Amazon water lily's meter-wide pads and the enormous leaves of some palms. Learn how these leaves are supported, why they grew so large, and how they survive storms.

name: The Smallest Seeds
teaser: Seeds as fine as dust.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the world's tiniest seeds — orchid seeds as fine as dust, with no food stored. Learn how they depend on fungi to germinate, and how their lightness lets them drift across oceans.

name: The Largest Seeds
teaser: A seed the size of a beach ball.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the coco de mer
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the coco de mer palm, whose seed is the largest in the world, weighing tens of kilograms. Learn how it grows in the Seychelles, why its double-lobed shape is famous, and how the palm's slow growth makes it rare.

name: The Oldest Seed to Sprout
teaser: A seed that waited 2,000 years.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the ancient seed
exploreAction.instruction: Learn about the oldest seed ever germinated: a 2,000-year-old date palm seed found at Masada, which sprouted into a living tree. Discover how its location and dry storage preserved it, and how it was grown.

name: The Deepest Roots
teaser: Roots that reach astonishing depths.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how far roots can reach: fig trees can root tens of meters down, and some desert plants plunge far beyond their height. Learn how deep roots find water and why shallow roots are more common.

name: The Widest Plants
teaser: Plants that spread across entire landscapes.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet plants that spread furthest: banyan trees with root systems over a hectare, and clonal grasses covering kilometers. Learn how vegetative spreading lets one genetic individual claim vast territory.

name: The Heaviest Fruits
teaser: Fruits that weigh more than a person.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the heaviest fruits: pumpkins bred past a ton, jackfruit at 30 kilograms, and giant squash. Learn how growers feed and guard record pumpkins, and how giant fruit is judged at competitions.

name: The Most Toxic Plants
teaser: Plants with deadly chemistry.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the world's most toxic plants: the castor bean's ricin, the rosary pea's abrin, and hemlock's poisons. Learn how their compounds work, how they were used in history, and why most are harmless unless eaten.

name: Castor Bean: Ricin
teaser: A garden plant that hides a deadly toxin.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the castor bean plant, grown for castor oil, also contains ricin — one of the most toxic natural substances. Discover how ricin works, why the oil is safe, and why the beans are dangerous if chewed.

name: Hemlock: The Poison of Athens
teaser: The plant that killed Socrates.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet hemlock, the plant whose poison reportedly killed Socrates in ancient Athens. Learn how its alkaloids paralyze, how to identify its feathery leaves, and how it is distinct from harmless lookalikes.

name: Oleander: The Toxic Beauty
teaser: A beautiful shrub that is deadly to eat.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet oleander, a flowering shrub so toxic that even its smoke can be harmful. Learn why it thrives in dry warm climates, how its cardiac glycosides work, and why it is planted anyway for its beauty.

name: The Manchineel: The Poison Tree
teaser: A tree whose sap burns on contact.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the manchineel, sometimes called the most dangerous tree: its sap blisters skin, its fruit is toxic, and even rain dripping off its leaves can burn. Learn where it grows and how it got its fearsome reputation.

name: The Stinging Tree
teaser: An Australian tree with a vicious sting.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the stinging tree
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the stinging tree of Australia, whose leaf hairs inject a painful neurotoxin that can hurt for months. Learn why it is feared in the rainforest, how it is related to the nettle, and how even dead leaves sting.

name: Touch-Me-Not: The Exploding Seed
teaser: A plant that flings its seeds.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet touch-me-not, also called jewelweed, whose ripe seed pods explode at the lightest touch, flinging seeds meters away. Learn how this dispersal strategy works and why the plant is named for its reaction.

name: Seed Dispersal: The Many Rides
teaser: The tricks seeds use to travel.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour the ways seeds travel: wind wings, sticky hooks, edible fruits, explosion, and water rides. Learn how each strategy places seeds where they can grow, and how plants bet on different travelers.

name: The Columbian Exchange: Plants on the Move
teaser: How 1492 swapped the world's crops.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Columbian exchange
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Columbus's voyages began the greatest plant swap in history: corn, potatoes, and tomatoes went east; wheat, rice, and coffee went west. Discover how this exchange reshaped diets, populations, and landscapes on every continent.

name: New World Crops: The American Gift
teaser: The foods the Americas gave the world.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of New World crops
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the crops born in the Americas: corn, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, peppers, squash, and chocolate. Learn how these foods traveled the globe after 1492 and became staples from Italy to China.

name: Old World Crops: The Other Half
teaser: The foods that crossed to the Americas.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of Old World crops
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the crops that sailed west with Europeans: wheat, rice, sugar, coffee, bananas, and citrus. Learn how these Old World staples found new homes in the Americas and transformed its farms and tables.

name: Indigenous Agriculture: The First Farmers
teaser: The farming systems that predated Europe.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about the sophisticated farming of Indigenous peoples: the three sisters garden of corn, beans, and squash, terraced Andean fields, and Amazonian dark earth soils. Discover how these systems fed millions sustainably.

name: The Three Sisters: The Perfect Trio
teaser: Corn, beans, and squash growing as one.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the three sisters
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the three sisters garden: corn for the beans to climb, beans to fix nitrogen, and squash to shade the soil. Learn how Indigenous farmers combined them, and how the partnership fed generations.

name: Potato Diversity: The Andean Bank
teaser: Thousands of varieties in one mountain range.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how the Andes grew thousands of potato varieties in every color and shape. Learn how Indigenous farmers matched varieties to altitudes, and how this diversity is preserved as insurance for the world's food.

name: Rice Terraces: The Staircase Fields
teaser: Mountain steps that feed valleys.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the rice terraces of Asia, where mountainsides were carved into flooded steps. Learn how the terraces capture rain and silt, how the water flows from top to bottom, and how they have fed families for centuries.

name: Chinampas: The Floating Fields
teaser: The Aztec gardens built on water.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover chinampas, the Aztec 'floating gardens' built from mud and reeds on lake shallows. Learn how they fed Tenochtitlan, how the canals irrigated and fertilized them, and how some still grow food in Mexico City.

name: Terrace Farming: The World's Steps
teaser: Fields cut into hillsides everywhere.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour terrace farming worldwide, from the rice terraces of Asia to the stone terraces of Peru and the vineyards of Europe. Learn how terracing controls erosion, holds water, and turns steep land into farmland.

name: Heirloom Tomato Flavors
teaser: Why old varieties taste so different.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why heirloom tomatoes taste different from grocery varieties: their genes, thin skins, and vine-ripening create complex flavor. Discover how breeders traded flavor for shipping toughness, and how heirlooms made a comeback.

name: Eating With the Seasons
teaser: Why food tastes best in its own season.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore why seasonal food tastes better: crops harvested at their peak, ripened on the plant, and eaten fresh. Learn how seasonality shapes cuisines, and how storage and transport changed what we eat and when.

name: The Slow Food Movement
teaser: A global stand for local, traditional food.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the slow food movement
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the slow food movement, founded in Italy as a stand against fast food. Learn how it champions local, traditional, and good food, and how its seed banks and fairs protect regional crops and recipes.

name: Farm to Table: The Short Journey
teaser: Eating food grown nearby.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of farm to table
exploreAction.instruction: Learn about farm-to-table eating, where food travels from nearby farms to your plate in days or hours. Discover why freshness, flavor, and local farms benefit, and how farmers markets make it possible.

name: The Victory Garden Revival
teaser: Growing food at home in modern times.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the modern victory garden
exploreAction.instruction: Discover how the wartime victory garden idea returned: people growing vegetables at home for health, cost, and climate. Learn how balcony herbs, backyard beds, and community plots revived the tradition.

name: Kitchen Gardens Around the World
teaser: The small plots behind every home.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour kitchen gardens worldwide, from French potagers to Middle Eastern herb plots and tropical home gardens. Learn how each culture grows a small plot of essentials, and why the kitchen garden is a universal idea.

name: Best Houseplants for Beginners
teaser: The forgiving plants to start with.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the best houseplants for beginners: snake plant, pothos, spider plant, and ZZ plant, which forgive missed waterings and dim corners. Learn why these tough plants build confidence before harder ones.

name: Low-Light Houseplants
teaser: Plants that survive dark corners.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn which houseplants tolerate low light: snake plant, ZZ plant, pothos, and peace lily. Discover how they adapt to dim rooms, why they grow slowly there, and how to tell when even they need more light.

name: High-Light Houseplants
teaser: Plants that crave bright sun.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet houseplants that need bright light: jade, succulents, fiddle-leaf fig, and citrus. Learn why a sunny window matters, how to avoid leaf scorch, and how these plants reward a bright spot.

name: Hanging Houseplants: The Trailers
teaser: Plants that spill from shelves and baskets.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the best trailing houseplants — pothos, string of pearls, trailing philodendron, and inch plant — that spill from baskets. Learn how to keep their vines full and how to propagate them from cuttings.

name: Flowering Houseplants
teaser: Blooms for the windowsill.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet houseplants that flower indoors: African violets, orchids, peace lilies, and jasmine. Learn what each needs to bloom — light, rest, or humidity — and why flowering indoors takes a little patience.

name: Fragrant Houseplants
teaser: Scents for the windowsill.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover houseplants that fill a room with scent: jasmine, gardenia, lavender, and citrus blossoms. Learn what each needs to flower and release fragrance, and how to keep the perfume coming.

name: Air-Purifying Plants
teaser: What the research says about clean-air plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what the famous NASA clean-air study found and its limits: houseplants remove some indoor pollutants but slowly. Discover which plants score best, and why ventilation matters more than plants.

name: Pet-Safe Houseplants
teaser: Green friends that won't hurt cats and dogs.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn which houseplants are safe around pets: spider plant, calathea, and peperomia, versus toxic ones like lilies and philodendron. Discover how to check toxicity and how to keep curious pets away from plants.

name: Terrariums: Gardens in Glass
teaser: Tiny sealed worlds in jars.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to build a terrarium: layers of drainage, charcoal, and soil in a glass jar, planted with moisture-loving plants. Discover how the sealed world recycles its own water, and which plants suit the life inside.

name: Kokedama: The Moss Balls
teaser: Plants wrapped in moss instead of pots.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet kokedama, the Japanese art of wrapping plant roots in a ball of moss instead of a pot. Learn how the moss ball is made, how it is watered by soaking, and how these hanging green spheres became a trend.

name: Styling With Houseplants
teaser: Arranging plants like a designer.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to style rooms with plants: group varied heights, use stands and shelves, and mix textures and leaf shapes. Discover how plants soften spaces, and how to build a layered green corner.

name: Measuring Light for Plants
teaser: Finding out if your corner is bright enough.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to measure light for plants with apps, meters, or simple shadow tests. Discover what bright indirect light really means, how seasons change it, and how to place plants by their light needs.

name: Watering Indoor Plants
teaser: The method behind watering houseplants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn a reliable method for watering houseplants: check the soil, water thoroughly until it drains, and let the top dry between. Discover why most houseplants die from overwatering, and how pots and seasons change the schedule.

name: Feeding Houseplants
teaser: When and how to fertilize indoor plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to feed houseplants: a balanced liquid fertilizer during the growing season, at half strength. Discover why overfeeding burns roots, why resting plants need none, and how to read the plant's needs.

name: Cleaning Plant Leaves
teaser: Why dusting leaves matters.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why cleaning plant leaves helps: dust blocks the light plants need and invites pests. Discover how to wipe large leaves, rinse small ones, and use neem for shine without harming the plant.

name: Plant Experiments You Can Try
teaser: Easy experiments that reveal plant science.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn simple plant experiments: bean seeds in jars to watch germination, celery in dye to see xylem, and cress toward a window to see phototropism. Discover how home science reveals the hidden lives of plants.

name: Celery in Dye: Seeing Xylem
teaser: How food coloring travels up stems.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the classic celery experiment: stand celery in colored water and watch the dye climb the xylem tubes. Discover what the colored pattern shows about how water moves, and how to repeat it with white flowers.

name: Bean in a Jar: Watching Germination
teaser: How a seed wakes up in a glass jar.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to sprout a bean in a jar with wet paper towels, watching root, shoot, and leaves appear. Discover what each stage needs and how the seed's stored food powers the first growth.

name: Cress and Light: The Bend Test
teaser: Growing seedlings toward a window.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to test phototropism with cress or bean seedlings: grow them beside a window and watch them bend toward the light. Discover what the bend reveals about auxin and growth.

name: Plant Pigment Art
teaser: Making natural paints and inks.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to make pigments from plants: boil berries for red, turmeric for yellow, and spinach for green. Discover how to extract color, how to fix it with a mordant, and how to paint with nature's palette.

name: Sprouting Seeds to Eat
teaser: Growing crunchy sprouts in a jar.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to sprout seeds for eating: rinse beans, lentils, or broccoli seeds in a jar, drain, and watch them grow in days. Discover why sprouts are nutritious, how to avoid spoilage, and which seeds sprout best.

name: Regrowing Kitchen Scraps
teaser: Growing new plants from food waste.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to regrow plants from kitchen scraps: green onions in water, lettuce stems, and avocado pits. Discover which scraps root easily, how long they take, and how this turns waste into windowsill gardens.

name: Growing an Avocado From a Pit
teaser: The toothpick-and-jar classic.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow an avocado pit
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow an avocado plant from a pit: suspend it over water with toothpicks, wait for roots, then pot it. Discover how long it takes, why a fruiting tree needs grafting, and how to keep the plant happy.

name: Sweet Potato Vines in Water
teaser: Turning a potato into a trailing vine.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow sweet potato vines
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow a sweet potato vine in water: prop the tuber in a jar and watch stems sprout with heart-shaped leaves. Discover why it makes a fast houseplant and how to pot the rooted slips.

name: Plant Tissue Culture: The Lab Garden
teaser: Growing whole plants from tiny pieces.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how tissue culture grows entire plants from tiny pieces in sterile jars, cloning thousands of identical plants. Discover how it saves rare orchids and bananas, and why labs use it for disease-free stock.

name: Cloning Plants: The Natural Copies
teaser: Why every plant can be a clone.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why plants clone so easily: many grow new roots from cuttings, runners, or bulbs, making genetic copies. Discover how farmers exploit this for consistent crops, and how it differs from seed reproduction.

name: Micropropagation: The Many Copies
teaser: Multiplying rare plants in labs.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet micropropagation, growing thousands of plants from one piece in the lab. Learn how it saves endangered species and supplies orchids, and how tiny cuttings become entire nurseries.

name: Cross-Pollination and Hybrids
teaser: How pollen from one plant changes another.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cross-pollination works: pollen from one variety fertilizes another, mixing traits in the seeds. Discover how breeders use it to create hybrids, and how gardeners can do simple crosses with a brush.

name: Collecting Seeds From the Garden
teaser: Saving next year's garden for free.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to collect and save seeds from your garden: let pods dry, clean and label them, and store them cool and dry. Discover which plants breed true from seed and which surprise you.

name: Testing Seed Viability
teaser: Finding out if old seeds will still grow.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to test whether old seeds will still sprout: count a sample onto wet paper and watch for germination. Discover why some seeds last years and others weeks, and how storage affects viability.

name: Rainforest Medicines
teaser: The healing plants of the jungle.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how rainforest plants supplied medicines — from quinine and curare to cancer-fighting compounds. Discover how researchers search the canopy for healing chemicals, and why forest loss may be losing cures.

name: Rubber Plantations: The Amazon Escape
teaser: How rubber left Brazil for Asia.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how Henry Wickham smuggled rubber seeds from Brazil to Kew Gardens, and how seedlings reached Southeast Asia. Discover how plantations replaced jungle tapping, and how this changed the rubber trade forever.

name: Kew Gardens: The Plant Empire
teaser: The garden that moved plants around the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet Kew Gardens, the London botanic garden that became a global hub for plant science and collection. Learn how its scientists moved rubber, tea, and cinchona across empires, and how it still leads plant conservation.

name: Great Glasshouses: The Plant Palaces
teaser: The grand greenhouses of history.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour the great glasshouses of the world — from Kew's Palm House to modern rainforest biomes. Learn how engineers built vast glass palaces for tropical plants, and how they still shelter living collections.

name: The Great Plant Voyages
teaser: The ships that carried living plants around the world.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the ships that carried plants across oceans: Wardian cases of tea, breadfruit on the Bounty, and orchids by the crate. Learn how living plants traveled safely and how voyages changed gardens everywhere.

name: The Wardian Case: The Travel Box
teaser: The glass box that let plants cross oceans.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Wardian case
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the Wardian case, a sealed glass box invented by Nathaniel Ward that let live plants survive sea voyages. Learn how this simple invention moved rubber, tea, and orchids around the globe.

name: Plant Hunting Fever
teaser: The era when new plants were a national obsession.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about the Victorian plant-hunting fever, when new species made headlines and fortunes. Discover how collectors raced to find rhododendrons and orchids, and how the craze stocked the gardens of Europe.

name: Rhododendron Hunters
teaser: The mountain flowers that obsessed collectors.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the rhododendron, whose giant blooms in the Himalayas drew daring plant hunters. Learn how collectors braved mountain passes for new species, and how these finds transformed cold-climate gardens.

name: The Camellia's Journey
teaser: How a Chinese flower reached European gardens.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the camellia from East Asian gardens to Europe, where its glossy leaves and winter blooms charmed gardeners. Learn how camellias traveled with tea traders and became a European obsession.

name: Wisteria in the West
teaser: How an Asian vine conquered western gardens.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how wisteria, native to China, Japan, and America, became a western garden icon. Discover how its cascading blooms were introduced to Europe and why its vigorous growth demanded careful pruning.

name: The History of Gardens
teaser: From hanging gardens to modern backyards.

exploreAction.instruction: Walk through garden history: the Hanging Gardens of Babylon, Roman villas, monastery gardens, Mughal paradise gardens, and English landscape parks. Learn how gardens have always mirrored their cultures.

name: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon
teaser: The legendary garden that may or may not have existed.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the hanging gardens
exploreAction.instruction: Explore the mystery of the Hanging Gardens of Babylon, one of the ancient wonders whose ruins have never been found. Learn how ancient writers described terraced greenery, and how scholars debate where it stood.

name: Monastery Gardens: The Herb Plots
teaser: How monks kept plants and knowledge alive.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the monastery garden, where monks grew herbs for medicine, food, and worship. Learn how these plots preserved classical plant knowledge through the Middle Ages, and how their layout shaped later gardens.

name: Persian Gardens: Paradise on Earth
teaser: The ancient gardens that gave us the word paradise.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore Persian gardens, walled green sanctuaries with water channels that gave the world the word paradise. Learn how their four-part design, shade, and flowing water inspired gardens from Spain to India.

name: The English Landscape Garden
teaser: How Britain invented the 'natural' look.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the English landscape garden of the 1700s replaced formal parterres with rolling lawns, lakes, and 'natural' planting. Discover how Capability Brown reshaped estates and how the style spread worldwide.

name: Vitamin C: The Citrus Gift
teaser: How plants make the vitamin that saved sailors.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how citrus plants make vitamin C to protect themselves from sun damage, and how this compound saved sailors from scurvy. Discover why humans can't make it and must eat plants that do.

name: Beta-Carotene: The Vitamin A Source
teaser: How orange plants give us vitamin A.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how carrots and other orange plants make beta-carotene, which our bodies turn into vitamin A. Discover why vitamin A matters for vision, and how golden rice was engineered to bring it to rice-eating regions.

name: Fiber: The Plant Advantage
teaser: Why plants are our best source of fiber.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about fiber, the plant compounds we can't digest but need: cellulose and pectin keep digestion moving and feed gut bacteria. Discover why whole plant foods are the best source of fiber.

name: Plant Proteins: The Complete Picture
teaser: How plants provide protein.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants make protein and which ones offer complete amino acid profiles — soy, quinoa, and beans with rice. Discover how combining plants covers all the amino acids our bodies need.

name: Omega-3 From Plants
teaser: Plant oils that provide essential fats.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how flax, chia, and walnut provide ALA, a plant omega-3 fat our bodies need. Discover how it compares to fish oils, and how the plants make these oils in their seeds.

name: Antioxidant-Rich Foods
teaser: Which plants pack the most protective compounds.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn which plant foods are richest in antioxidants — berries, dark greens, and colorful spices. Discover how the pigments that protect plants also protect us, and why a colorful plate is a healthy one.

name: Fermented Plant Foods
teaser: How microbes transform plant foods.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore fermented plant foods: kimchi, sauerkraut, miso, and tempeh, transformed by microbes. Learn how fermentation preserves, adds flavor, and creates probiotics, and how it began as food storage.

name: Plant Milks: The Alternatives
teaser: How oats, almonds, and soy become milk.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plant milks are made: grains, nuts, or beans are soaked, blended, and strained into milky drinks. Discover how oat, almond, soy, and rice milks differ in flavor and nutrition, and how they are fortified.

name: Nut Butters: The Creamy Spreads
teaser: How nuts become butter.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how nut butters are made by grinding roasted nuts until their oils release into a creamy paste. Discover why peanut, almond, and cashew butters differ, and how oils separate when no stabilizers are added.

name: Olive Oil Varieties
teaser: How olive type and pressing change the oil.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of olive oil varieties
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how olive variety, ripeness, and pressing affect olive oil's flavor, from peppery to buttery. Discover how early-pressed oils are grassier and how 'extra virgin' standards are judged.

name: Coffee Varieties: Arabica vs Robusta
teaser: The two species behind your cup.

exploreAction.instruction: Compare arabica and robusta coffee: arabica grows at altitude with complex flavor, robusta grows low with more caffeine and bitterness. Learn how each is grown and blended, and how climate threatens arabica.

name: Tea Varieties: The Leaf's Range
teaser: How one plant makes many teas.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how one tea species makes green, black, white, oolong, and pu-erh teas through processing. Discover how region, harvest time, and oxidation change the cup, and how each style developed its tradition.

name: Cacao Varieties: The Bean Types
teaser: Criollo, Forastero, and Trinitario.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the three cacao types: rare Criollo with delicate flavor, hardy Forastero with classic chocolate, and Trinitario hybrids. Learn how each shapes the chocolate made from it.

name: Vanilla Species
teaser: The orchid species behind vanilla.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about the vanilla orchid species used for spice — mostly one species from Mexico — and its relatives used regionally. Discover why only this species produces the prized aroma and why pollination is so tricky.

name: Natural Sweeteners From Plants
teaser: How plants sweeten without sugar.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet plant-based sweeteners: stevia from leaves, monk fruit, maple syrup, and agave nectar. Learn how each is extracted, how their sweetness compares to sugar, and how they are used in food.

name: Plant Scientists Today
teaser: The people who study and protect plants.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of modern plant science
exploreAction.instruction: Meet today's plant scientists: geneticists, ecologists, breeders, and conservationists who study everything from roots to rainforests. Learn how their work feeds the world, saves species, and prepares for climate change.

name: Crop Science: Feeding the Future
teaser: How plant research prepares for more people.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how crop scientists are preparing for a hotter, crowded world: drought-tolerant wheat, flood-tolerant rice, and crops that need less fertilizer. Discover the breeding tools — from gene editing to AI — shaping tomorrow's farms.

name: Gene Editing and Crops
teaser: The new tool reshaping plant breeding.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how CRISPR gene editing lets breeders make precise changes to crop DNA quickly. Discover the difference between editing and GMO insertion, how edited mushrooms and tomatoes have reached markets, and the debates around it.

name: Climate-Resilient Crops
teaser: Plants bred for a changing climate.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the crops being bred for climate change: heat-tolerant wheat, salt-tolerant rice, and drought-proof sorghum. Learn how breeders and farmers are adapting, and why diversity is their best tool.

name: Urban Farming: The City Harvest
teaser: Growing food inside cities at scale.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore urban farming at scale: rooftop farms, indoor vertical farms, and converted warehouses growing greens with LEDs. Learn how cities are growing more of their own food, and where the limits are.

name: The Plant-Based Movement
teaser: Why plant foods are on the rise.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about the plant-based movement: more people choosing plants for health, climate, and animals. Discover how plant meats and milks grew into a major industry, and how plant-heavy diets are shaping menus.

name: Plants as Materials
teaser: From bamboo bikes to mushroom packaging.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the new uses for plants: bamboo for buildings, mycelium for packaging, and plant fibers for fabrics. Learn how designers are replacing plastics and concrete with fast-growing plants.

name: Biofuels: Energy From Plants
teaser: Turning crops and waste into fuel.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how biofuels turn plant sugars and oils into ethanol and biodiesel. Discover the trade-offs — fuel from crops vs food — and how next-generation fuels use algae and waste instead of food.

name: Plants and Carbon Capture
teaser: How plants can help pull carbon from the air.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants capture carbon dioxide as they grow, storing it in wood and soil. Discover why protecting forests and restoring wetlands are among the cheapest ways to slow climate change.

name: The Plant Microbiome
teaser: The tiny life that lives on and in plants.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of the plant microbiome
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the microbiome — the bacteria and fungi living on plant roots and leaves. Learn how these microbes help plants absorb nutrients and resist disease, and how farmers are learning to cultivate them.

name: Soil Microbes: The Underground Team
teaser: The life that makes soil fertile.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how soil microbes — bacteria, fungi, and protozoa — break down organic matter and feed plants. Discover how healthy soil is a living web, and how farming practices build or deplete it.

name: The Rhizosphere: The Root Zone
teaser: The busy world around every root.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore the rhizosphere, the zone of soil around roots packed with microbes trading with the plant. Learn how roots release sugars to feed helpers, and how this underground economy feeds the plant.

name: Nutrient Cycles: The Plant Loop
teaser: How nutrients move through soil and plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how nutrients cycle between soil, plants, and air — nitrogen fixed from the sky, carbon exchanged, and minerals released from rock. Discover how plants return nutrients to the soil when they die.

name: The Phosphorus Cycle
teaser: The nutrient that comes from rock.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how phosphorus, essential for plant energy, comes from weathered rock and recycled organic matter. Discover why it is finite, how fertilizers mine it, and why recycling it matters.

name: Plant Discovery Today
teaser: New plant species are still being found.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of modern plant discovery
exploreAction.instruction: Learn that botanists still discover hundreds of new plant species every year, from rainforest trees to tiny herbs. Discover where the finds are happening, why they matter, and how fast some may disappear.

name: Living Walls: The Green Facades
teaser: Growing plants on vertical surfaces.

exploreAction.targetName: how to build a living wall
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the living wall, a vertical surface planted with greenery for cooling and beauty. Learn how modular panels hold soil and plants, how irrigation drips through, and how cities are covering facades with plants.

name: Green Roofs: The Living Roofs
teaser: Roofs planted with living vegetation.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how green roofs are covered with living plants that insulate, absorb rain, and cool cities. Discover the layers beneath the plants, how sedum roofs need little care, and why cities encourage them.

name: Balcony Gardening: The Small Harvest
teaser: Growing food in a few square meters.

exploreAction.targetName: how to garden on a balcony
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow a full garden on a balcony: pots for tomatoes and herbs, vertical planters for beans, and railing baskets for strawberries. Discover how to manage wind, shade, and watering in the sky.

name: Windowsill Gardens: The Tiny Plot
teaser: Growing herbs and greens on a ledge.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow on a windowsill
exploreAction.instruction: Discover what grows on a windowsill: herbs, sprouts, microgreens, and small peppers in pots. Learn how to match plants to the window's light, and how to keep the tiny garden productive year-round.

name: Microgreens: The Tiny Salads
teaser: Baby greens harvested in a week or two.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how microgreens — tiny seedlings harvested young — grow in trays within a couple of weeks. Discover why they are packed with flavor and nutrients, and how to grow them on a countertop.

name: Sprouts vs Microgreens
teaser: Two ways to eat young plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Compare sprouts, seeds germinated and eaten whole including roots, with microgreens, seedlings grown in soil and cut young. Learn how each is grown, used, and which is safer to eat.

name: The Herb Window Box
teaser: A box of flavor by the kitchen.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow herbs in a box
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to plant a herb window box: basil, parsley, and chives in rich soil with good drainage. Discover how to harvest without killing the plants, and how to keep the box productive all season.

name: The Salad Garden: Cut and Come
teaser: Growing greens that regrow after cutting.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the cut-and-come-again method: harvest outer lettuce and salad leaves and let them regrow. Discover which greens suit it, how to sow in succession, and how to keep a salad supply through the season.

name: Strawberry Barrels: The Tower
teaser: Growing berries in a barrel of pockets.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow strawberries in a barrel
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow strawberries in a barrel or tower with planting pockets up the sides. Discover how the vertical planter fits small spaces, how watering reaches every plant, and how to refresh it each year.

name: Growing Potatoes in Bags
teaser: Tubers on a patio in fabric bags.

exploreAction.targetName: how to grow potatoes in bags
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to grow potatoes in grow bags: plant seed potatoes, mound soil as they grow, and tip the bag to harvest. Discover how this suits small spaces and why earthing up makes more potatoes.

name: Tomato Towers and Cages
teaser: Supporting tomato plants the easy way.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the ways to support tomatoes: cages, stakes, and spiral towers that hold heavy plants upright. Discover why support improves air flow and fruit quality, and how to tie and prune for the best crop.

name: Succession Planting: The Constant Harvest
teaser: Sowing in waves for a steady supply.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn succession planting: sow small batches every few weeks so harvests don't arrive all at once. Discover which crops suit it, how to plan the waves, and how it keeps gardens productive all season.

name: Interplanting: Mixing Crops
teaser: Growing different crops in the same space.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn interplanting: grow fast crops like radishes between slow ones like carrots, or tall with low, to use space fully. Discover how mixing crops shades soil, deters pests, and harvests more per bed.

name: Square-Foot Gardening: The Grid
teaser: Growing a lot in small raised beds.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn square-foot gardening, a method of dividing beds into one-foot grids, each planted with a set number of plants. Discover how it packs small spaces, simplifies planning, and suits beginners.

name: No-Dig Gardening
teaser: Growing without digging the soil.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn no-dig gardening: instead of digging, add compost and mulch on top and let soil life do the work. Discover how it builds soil structure, reduces weeds, and is easier on the gardener's back.

name: The Gardens of Versailles
teaser: The palace gardens that defined an era.
