exploreAction.instruction: Tour the gardens of Versailles, the vast formal gardens built for Louis XIV with geometric parterres, fountains, and clipped hedging. Learn how they displayed royal power, and how the style spread across Europe.

name: Kew's Palm House: The Glass Giant
teaser: A Victorian greenhouse built for giants.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Palm House
exploreAction.instruction: Meet Kew's Palm House, a 19th-century glass palace built to house tropical palms. Learn how Victorian engineers curved iron and glass, how plants were moved in, and how it still shelters tropical giants.

name: The Butchart Gardens: The Quarry Bloom
teaser: A worked-out quarry turned into a garden.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the Butchart Gardens in Canada, created when a limestone quarry was filled with soil and planted. Learn how a family turned an industrial scar into one of the world's great gardens.

name: Majorelle Garden: The Blue Oasis
teaser: A Marrakech garden painted in cobalt blue.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Majorelle Garden
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the Majorelle Garden in Marrakech, where cobalt-blue buildings frame cacti and palms. Learn how the painter Jacques Majorelle created it, how Yves Saint Laurent saved it, and why the blue is iconic.

name: Gardens by the Bay: The Futuristic Park
teaser: A futuristic garden of supertrees.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of Gardens by the Bay
exploreAction.instruction: Visit Gardens by the Bay in Singapore, where 'supertrees' of steel and plants tower over futuristic domes. Learn how the structures collect solar power and rainwater, and how the domes recreate climates.

name: Types of Japanese Gardens
teaser: Stroll, tea, and dry gardens explained.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the main Japanese garden styles: the stroll garden with paths and ponds, the tea garden with its stepping stones, and the dry karesansui garden of raked gravel. Discover what each is for.

name: Chinese Gardens: The Painted Landscapes
teaser: Gardens designed like scroll paintings.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore Chinese scholar gardens, designed like landscape paintings with rocks, water, and pavilions. Learn how they blend nature and architecture, and how each element carries symbolic meaning.

name: Moorish Gardens of Spain
teaser: The water-filled courtyards of Al-Andalus.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour the Moorish gardens of Spain, from the Alhambra's courtyards to the Generalife's terraces, where water channels cool the air. Learn how Islamic garden design brought shade, scent, and sound to arid lands.

name: Italian Renaissance Gardens
teaser: Terraces, statues, and clipped greens.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the Italian Renaissance garden, with terraced slopes, fountains, and box parterres around villas. Learn how they revived Roman garden ideas and became the model for formal European gardens.

name: Victorian Gardens: The Bedding Craze
teaser: The carpet beds of the nineteenth century.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about Victorian carpet bedding, where thousands of annuals were planted in geometric patterns like living rugs. Discover how new plants and glasshouses fueled the craze, and how it shaped public parks.

name: Great Botanic Gardens of the World
teaser: Living museums from Kew to Sydney.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of world botanic gardens
exploreAction.instruction: Tour the great botanic gardens — Kew, Singapore, Sydney, New York, and Cape Town — that collect and study plants. Learn how each began and how they now lead conservation of the world's flora.

name: Garden Ornaments: The Decorations
teaser: Statues, urns, and topiary through history.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the garden ornaments of history: classical statues, stone urns, sundials, and topiary animals. Learn how each era decorated its gardens, and how ornaments give gardens personality.

name: Topiary: The Living Sculpture
teaser: Shaping shrubs into animals and shapes.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the art of topiary, clipping shrubs and trees into geometric or animal shapes. Discover which evergreens suit it, how frames guide the growth, and how this ancient craft still delights gardens.

name: Knot Gardens: The Patterned Hedges
teaser: Low hedges woven into patterns.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the knot garden, where low clipped hedges are laid out in intricate patterns like embroidery. Learn how Tudor gardens popularized them, how they are planted and clipped, and how they frame grand houses.

name: The Cottage Garden Heritage
teaser: The humble origins of a beloved style.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how the cottage garden began with working families growing food and herbs, then became a romantic style. Learn how its mix of practical and pretty plants shaped how we garden today.

name: Birth Flowers: The Month Blooms
teaser: The flower assigned to each birth month.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the tradition of birth flowers, assigning a bloom to each month — carnation for January, rose for June, chrysanthemum for November. Learn where the list came from and what each flower symbolizes.

name: Rose Colors and Meanings
teaser: What each rose color says.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the language of rose colors: red for love, white for purity, yellow for friendship, pink for gratitude. Discover how the meanings formed, and how to choose roses that say the right thing.

name: Flower Festivals of Asia
teaser: Blooms celebrated across the continent.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of Asian flower festivals
exploreAction.instruction: Tour Asia's flower festivals: Japan's hanami, India's onam flower carpets, and Korea's cherry blossom festivals. Learn how each culture celebrates the brief season of blooms.

name: Day of the Dead Flowers
teaser: The marigolds of Mexico's celebration.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how marigolds — cempasuchil in Mexico — are used for Day of the Dead altars, their scent said to guide spirits home. Discover why the golden petals carpet altars and paths each November.

name: The Lotus in Culture
teaser: A flower sacred across Asia.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the lotus in culture
exploreAction.instruction: Explore the lotus as a sacred symbol from Egypt to India and China, standing for purity and rebirth. Learn how it appears in temples, art, and meditation, and why it rises clean from muddy water.

name: The Rose in Literature
teaser: A flower that has inspired poets for centuries.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the rose in writing
exploreAction.instruction: Follow the rose through literature, from Persian poetry to Shakespeare's 'a rose by any other name'. Learn why the rose became the universal symbol of love and beauty in writing.

name: Flowers in Art
teaser: How artists have painted blooms through the ages.

exploreAction.instruction: Tour flower painting through history, from Dutch still lifes with tulips to Impressionist gardens. Learn why artists loved flowers, and how painting them documented new species.

name: Victorian Flower Albums
teaser: Pressed blooms in scrapbooks.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the Victorian flower album, where women pressed and arranged blooms in scrapbooks. Learn how the albums preserved gardens and feelings, and how pressing was a fashionable skill.

name: Wedding Flowers Through History
teaser: Why weddings are full of blooms.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why weddings feature flowers: from Roman wreaths and medieval herbs to the modern bouquet. Discover how bouquets began as fragrant bunches to mask smells, and how each bloom carried meaning.

name: Flowers at Funerals
teaser: The blooms of farewell.

exploreAction.instruction: Explore why flowers are given at funerals, from ancient wreaths to modern arrangements. Learn how lilies, roses, and chrysanthemums carry mourning meanings in different cultures.

name: Flower Power: The Symbol
teaser: How flowers became a peace symbol.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how 'flower power' turned flowers into a 1960s symbol of peace and protest. Discover how protesters offered flowers to soldiers and police, and how the image spread around the world.

name: Flower Crowns: The Ancient Circle
teaser: Wreaths worn through the ages.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the flower crown, worn from Greek laurel wreaths and Roman roses to modern festivals. Learn how crowns honored winners and gods, and how the tradition is reborn in today's celebrations.

name: The Flower Child Era
teaser: A cultural moment named for blooms.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the flower child era
exploreAction.instruction: Discover how the 'flower child' of the 1960s became a symbol of peace and free expression. Learn how music, fashion, and the summer of love turned flowers into an emblem of an era.

name: Flowers at Festivals
teaser: How blooms decorate celebrations everywhere.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of flowers at festivals
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how flowers decorate festivals worldwide — from floats and garlands to confetti and altars. Discover why celebrations turn to blooms for color, scent, and meaning.

name: Flower Confetti: The Petal Throw
teaser: Why petals are thrown at celebrations.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why petals and confetti are thrown at weddings and festivals, from Roman customs to modern celebrations. Discover how biodegradable petal confetti is replacing plastic, and which flowers provide it.

name: How Plants Adapt to Climate
teaser: The strategies for every climate.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants adapt to climate: succulents store water, alpine plants hug the ground, and desert ephemerals race the rain. Discover how leaf size, root depth, and growth timing all respond to where a plant lives.

name: Desert Plant Strategies
teaser: The tricks for surviving the dry.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the desert plant toolkit: water-storing stems, tiny leaves, shallow spreading roots, and seeds that wait years for rain. Discover how cacti, mesquite, and desert ephemerals each survive the dry.

name: Tropical Plant Strategies
teaser: Surviving rain, shade, and competition.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how tropical plants cope: drip-tip leaves shed rain, epiphytes escape dark floors, and buttress roots brace shallow soil. Discover how the rainforest shapes every plant that lives in it.

name: Cold Climate Plant Strategies
teaser: How plants survive freezing winters.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cold-climate plants survive winter: dropping leaves, entering dormancy, and concentrating sugars as antifreeze. Discover how evergreens protect their needles and how buds wait for spring.

name: Aquatic Plant Strategies
teaser: How plants live in water.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how aquatic plants adapt: floating leaves with air chambers, underwater stems that bend, and leaves that split into ribbons to move with currents. Discover how plants breathe in water.

name: Fire-Adapted Plants
teaser: Plants that need flames to thrive.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how some plants depend on fire: thick bark protects, cones open only in heat, and seeds sprout best in ash. Discover how fire-adapted plants recover and regrow after flames.

name: Salt-Tolerant Plants
teaser: Plants that survive salty soils.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants survive salty conditions: mangroves filter salt at the roots, saltbushes store it in leaves, and some excrete it through glands. Discover how salt shapes coastal and desert vegetation.

name: Shade-Tolerant Plants
teaser: Plants that grow under the canopy.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how shade-tolerant plants survive with little light: broader leaves to catch what filters down, and slower, careful growth. Discover which forest-floor plants thrive in deep shade.

name: Drought-Tolerant Plants
teaser: Plants built for dry spells.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how drought-tolerant plants survive dry periods: deep roots, small waxy leaves, and the ability to shut down and wait. Discover why native plants are often the best drought survivors.

name: Flood-Tolerant Plants
teaser: Plants that survive being underwater.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how some plants survive flooding: hollow stems carry air to roots, and specialized cells let roots breathe underwater. Discover which trees and crops tolerate seasonal floods.

name: Alpine Plant Adaptations
teaser: Surviving thin air and fierce weather.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how alpine plants survive: cushion shapes trap warmth, dense hairs block sun, and deep taproots anchor against wind. Discover how they squeeze a growing season into a short summer.

name: Wind-Resistant Plants
teaser: Plants built for exposed places.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants resist wind: flexible stems, deep roots, and small tough leaves. Discover how coastal and mountain plants are shaped by constant wind, and how gardeners choose wind-resistant species.

name: Plants of Poor Soil
teaser: How plants survive without rich nutrients.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plants survive poor soil: carnivorous plants trap insects, legumes fix nitrogen, and proteas send out hair-like roots to scavenge. Discover the strategies for the leanest ground.

name: Pioneer Species: The First Plants
teaser: The plants that colonize bare ground.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the pioneer species that first colonize bare rock, lava, and cleared land — lichens, mosses, and tough grasses. Learn how they build the first soil and make way for later plants.

name: Ecological Succession
teaser: How plant communities change over time.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how plant communities change through succession: bare ground grows grasses, then shrubs, then forest. Discover how each stage alters the soil and light for the next, and how disturbance resets the clock.

name: Eggplant Around the World
teaser: A purple fruit in cuisines everywhere.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the eggplant around the world: baba ganoush in the Middle East, ratatouille in France, and baingan bharta in India. Learn how this Asian fruit traveled the spice routes and became a global favorite.

name: Okra and Gumbo
teaser: How a pod thickened a famous stew.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of okra in gumbo
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how okra's natural sliminess thickens gumbo, the Louisiana stew built on African, French, and Native roots. Discover how the pod traveled from Africa with enslaved people, and how it became a Southern staple.

name: Collard Greens: The Southern Green
teaser: A leafy green of the American South.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet collard greens, a cabbage cousin slow-cooked in the American South with smoked meat and broth. Learn how the greens traveled from Africa and Europe, and how they survive frost with sweeter leaves.

name: Plantain Dishes of the World
teaser: A starchy fruit cooked every way.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how plantains are cooked across the tropics: fried as tostones and maduros, boiled, roasted, and pounded. Learn how the firm starch holds up to cooking and why the fruit is a daily staple for millions.

name: Cassava and Garri
teaser: How a root becomes a West African staple.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cassava is processed into garri, a fermented, toasted West African staple. Discover why the processing removes cyanide, how garri is soaked or cooked, and how it feeds millions daily.

name: Fufu: The Pounded Staple
teaser: The starchy ball of West African tables.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet fufu, the pounded starchy ball of West and Central African meals, made from cassava, yam, or plantain. Learn how it is pounded and eaten with soups, and how the process turns starch into a soft dough.

name: Tortillas: The Corn Flatbread
teaser: How nixtamalization made corn edible.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how tortillas are made from corn treated with lime — nixtamalization — which unlocks nutrients. Discover how the process developed in Mesoamerica, how the dough is pressed and cooked, and how tortillas feed millions.

name: Pesto: The Basil Sauce
teaser: How a Genoese sauce became global.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet pesto, the Ligurian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese, and oil. Learn how its name comes from 'pestle', how it is traditionally pounded, and how it spread from Genoa to kitchens worldwide.

name: Kimchi: The Fermented Staple
teaser: The cabbage dish at every Korean meal.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover kimchi, the fermented cabbage and vegetable dish at every Korean table. Learn how salt, chili, and lactic acid bacteria preserve it, how families make it in huge batches, and why it is a cultural icon.

name: Miso: The Fermented Soy
teaser: A paste aged by molds and patience.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how miso is made: soybeans, rice, and salt are fermented by a mold culture for months or years. Discover how aging deepens its flavor, how it builds miso soup, and how it carries umami.

name: Tempeh: The Fermented Bean
teaser: An Indonesian staple made from whole soybeans.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet tempeh, an Indonesian cake of soybeans fermented by a mold that binds them together. Learn how the fermentation improves nutrition and digestibility, and how tempeh is sliced and fried across Indonesia.

name: Soy Sauce: The Brewed Sauce
teaser: The long fermentation behind a brown liquid.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how soy sauce is brewed: soybeans and wheat are fermented by molds and yeasts over months, developing deep umami. Discover how the process resembles brewing, and how short-cut sauces differ.

name: Tofu: The Curdled Soy
teaser: How soy milk becomes bean curd.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how tofu is made: soy milk is curdled with a coagulant, pressed into blocks. Discover how firmness varies with pressing, and how this simple curd became a staple of East Asian cooking.

name: Falafel: The Chickpea Fritter
teaser: A street food made from soaked chickpeas.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet falafel, deep-fried balls of ground chickpeas, a street food of the Middle East. Learn how dried chickpeas are soaked and ground, why the mix is not cooked before frying, and how it is served in pita.

name: Hummus: The Chickpea Dip
teaser: A simple blend with a long history.

exploreAction.instruction: Discover hummus, the blend of chickpeas, tahini, lemon, and garlic eaten across the Middle East. Learn how the ingredients come together, why it is both ancient and beloved, and how it spread worldwide.

name: Plant Organs: The Basics
teaser: The parts that make a plant a plant.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the basic plant organs: roots that anchor and drink, stems that support and carry, and leaves that photosynthesize. Learn how flowers, fruits, and seeds complete the system.

name: Stems: The Support System
teaser: The trunks, canes, and vines that hold plants up.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what stems do: support leaves, carry water and sugar, and store food. Discover the difference between herbaceous and woody stems, and how vines use stems to climb.

name: Tubers: The Storage Stems
teaser: How swollen stems store food.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how tubers like potatoes are swollen underground stems, with buds that become new plants. Discover how they differ from roots, and how their stored starch feeds both plant and people.

name: Rhizomes: The Creeping Stems
teaser: Underground stems that spread plants.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet rhizomes, underground stems that creep sideways and sprout new shoots, from ginger to bamboo to iris. Learn how they spread plants into clumps and how gardeners divide them.

name: Corms: The Swollen Bases
teaser: The underground stores behind gladioli.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how corms, swollen underground stem bases like gladiolus and crocus, store food for next season. Discover how they differ from bulbs and tubers, and how gardeners lift and replant them.

name: Bulbs: The Layered Stores
teaser: The onion-like packages of spring flowers.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet bulbs, layered underground stores with fleshy scales wrapped around a bud, like onions and tulips. Learn how the layers feed the emerging plant, and how bulbs divide and naturalize.

name: Tendrils: The Grabbing Vines
teaser: The coilers that help vines climb.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how tendrils — modified stems or leaves — coil around supports to lift vines, from grape to pea to passionflower. Discover how they sense touch and curl, and how vines use them to reach light.

name: Thorns and Spines: The Armor
teaser: The plant weapons, explained.

exploreAction.targetName: the difference between thorns and spines
exploreAction.instruction: Learn the difference: thorns are modified stems, spines are modified leaves, and prickles grow from the surface. Discover how each evolved to defend plants from grazers.

name: Flower Anatomy: The Parts
teaser: Sepals, petals, stamens, and pistils.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the parts of a flower: sepals protect the bud, petals attract pollinators, stamens make pollen, and the pistil receives it. Discover how these parts fit together to make seeds.

name: Petals: The Advertisement
teaser: Why petals are shaped and colored.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how petals attract pollinators with color, shape, and guides. Discover why petals vary from landing platforms to spurs, and how some flowers are pollinated without any petals at all.

name: Stamens: The Pollen Makers
teaser: The male parts of the flower.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet stamens, the male parts of flowers, each with an anther that releases pollen. Learn how anthers open, how pollen travels, and how stamen number and shape vary across flowers.

name: The Pistil: The Receiver
teaser: The female part that becomes fruit.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how the pistil, the flower's female part, receives pollen on its stigma and guides it down to the ovary. Discover how the ovary becomes fruit and the ovules become seeds.

name: Nectaries: The Sweet Glands
teaser: Where flowers make their nectar.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet nectaries, the glands where flowers produce nectar to pay pollinators. Learn where they sit in different flowers, how much nectar they make, and how bees find and collect the reward.

name: Fruit Ripening: The Signals
teaser: How fruit knows when to turn sweet.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how fruits ripen: starches turn to sugar, acids soften, and colors and scents change. Discover how the gas ethylene drives the process, and how some fruits ripen only after picking.

name: From Flower to Seed
teaser: How pollination becomes seeds.

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the journey from pollen to seed: pollen lands, fertilizes the ovule, and the ovule grows into a seed while the ovary becomes fruit. Learn how each step depends on the last.

name: Cactus Water Storage
teaser: How cactus stems hold a desert of water.

exploreAction.targetName: the science of cactus water storage
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cactus stems store water in spongy tissue that expands like an accordion after rain. Discover how the pleats allow swelling, how the shallow roots drink fast, and how much a large cactus can hold.

name: Succulent Leaves: The Water Bank
teaser: How plump leaves store the desert.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how succulents store water in their leaves, making them plump and firm. Discover how the water bank sustains them through droughts, and why overwatering — not drought — kills them indoors.

name: Desert Annuals: The Rain Race
teaser: Flowers that live fast after storms.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet desert annuals, seeds that wait for rain then sprout, bloom, and seed within weeks. Learn how they race through their life cycle, and how the desert bursts into color after a good storm.

name: Desert Shrubs: The Root Explorers
teaser: Bushes that reach deep for water.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how desert shrubs survive with roots that plunge deep and spread wide to catch every drop. Discover how creosote and sagebrush claim their own water territory, and how they survive years of drought.

name: Cactus Pollination
teaser: How desert cacti get pollinated.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how cacti are pollinated: bees work daytime blooms, while bats visit the night flowers of saguaro and organ pipe. Discover how each cactus times its bloom to its pollinator.

name: Saguaro and Bats
teaser: The night partnership of a giant cactus.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how saguaro flowers open at night to welcome bats, which drink nectar and carry pollen between cacti. Discover how the cactus depends on the bat and the bat on the cactus.

name: Prickly Pear Tuna: The Fruit
teaser: The red fruit of the cactus.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of prickly pear fruit
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the tuna, the sweet red fruit of the prickly pear cactus, eaten across Mexico and the Southwest. Learn how it is peeled, juiced, and made into drinks and jams, and how its tiny seeds are edible.

name: Nopales: The Edible Pads
teaser: How cactus pads become a vegetable.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how nopales, the young pads of the prickly pear, are eaten as a vegetable in Mexico. Discover how they are de-spined, grilled or scrambled, and why their slimy texture is prized.

name: Cactus Fruits to Try
teaser: The sweet fruits of the desert.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the edible cactus fruits: dragonfruit, prickly pear tuna, and the fruits of barrel and hedgehog cacti. Learn how each tastes, how to handle their spines, and how they are eaten fresh or juiced.

name: Saguaro Country: The Sonoran
teaser: The desert that grows giant cacti.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of the Sonoran Desert
exploreAction.instruction: Learn why saguaro cacti grow only in the Sonoran Desert, with its twin rainy seasons. Discover how the desert's summer and winter rains, mild winters, and rocky slopes create the saguaro's home.

name: Designing a Cactus Garden
teaser: A low-water landscape of spines and blooms.

exploreAction.targetName: how to design a cactus garden
exploreAction.instruction: Learn how to design a cactus garden: choose sun, gravel mulch, and a mix of heights and shapes. Discover how to group cacti by water needs, and how to plant them safely.

name: Agave and Tequila
teaser: How a desert plant becomes a famous spirit.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how blue agave becomes tequila: the plant is harvested, its heart roasted and pressed, and the juice fermented and distilled. Discover how long agaves grow before harvest and how the spirit is aged.

name: Agave Beyond Tequila
teaser: The many uses of a spiky plant.

exploreAction.instruction: Meet the many uses of agave: fibers for rope and mats, sap for syrup, and roasted hearts for mezcal. Learn how different agave species serve different purposes across Mexico.

name: Yucca and Its Moth
teaser: The partnership that saved the flower.

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how yucca flowers depend on a single moth species that pollinates them and lays eggs inside. Discover how this ancient partnership works, and what happens when either partner is missing.

name: Joshua Trees and Their Moths
teaser: The desert tree and its tiny partner.

exploreAction.targetName: the story of Joshua tree moths
exploreAction.instruction: Meet the Joshua tree and its specialized moth, which pollinates the flowers and lays eggs in them. Learn how the partnership works, and why each tree depends on its own moth species.
